synopsis: Air carrier ground personnel reported a box collapsed while attempting to remove a part from the bin. The box had leaked an unknown liquid and was improperly labeled.
text: as i was pulling the part from its bin, the box fell apart almost immediately and the item fell on the floor, upon further inspection it looks as though the part had been leaking for some time leading to extensive corrosion on the bottom of the box, apart from this the box used to package the part had zero 'heavy' labels which are required for items weighing more than 50 pounds which also leads me to believe that even without the extensive corrosion the box would not have held up for long, meaning that if it didn't happen to me it would have happened to someone else down the line

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Event / Encounter Vehicle
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the aircraft rolled into the tug after push back following a failure of ground personnel to properly communicate with the flight crew.
text: prior to push we established communication with the ground crew and released the parking break per aom procedures. the ground crew advised that there was another company aircraft pushed off a gate behind us and asked if we had 'a lot of checklists to do' after push. we stated that we didn't but since the other aircraft was ready, they could park us anywhere out of the way so the other aircraft could taxi out. the ground crew stated it was fine and they would put us in front of the other aircraft. we continued pushing off the gate in redacted. all was normal during the initial phase of the push - we were cleared to start engine 1 and did so. shortly after engine start, the aircraft came to a stop. there was no communication from the ground crew at this point in time. i didn't think twice about the aircraft stopping as we were stopped on an angle, not on the taxi line still somewhat close to the gate. i thought the ground crew was going to pull us forward and straighten us out as there was another aircraft directly behind us. the next thing we heard was loud screaming in our headsets and heavy vibrations coming from the front of the aircraft. at this point i applied the breaks and immediately asked what was happening. the ground crew advised that the aircraft rolled forward into the tug. i stated that they never asked me to set the parking breaking nor did i state 'break set clear to disconnect the inter phone'. the ground crew then admitted that he 'screwed up' and didn't ask us to set the break. he also stated 'this is on me'. i immediately called maintenance control and informed them of the situation.cause: this occurred due to a lack of the required communication from the ground crew to the flight crew that the pushback was complete and to set the parking brake. had ground crew communicated with us prior to releasing the tug, this would not have occurred.suggestions: proper procedures from ground personnel should be adhered to.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict Ground Conflict; Less Severe; No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation
synopsis: Fractional flight crew reported the FMS system on aircraft is outdated and cannot keep up with the runway changes; leading to an increased workload on the flight crew.
text: ongoing issue with operating the grossly outdated honeywell fmz in today's airspace system. each time the landing runway is changed, the fmz reloads the star and decides it must be began from the initial fix. so while conducting a descend via arrival air traffic control changes or adds a runway you are to use, add this change to our wonderful ancient flight management system" and the aircraft drops the mandatory descent you are trying to comply with and begins a 180 turn to go back to the first fix on the star.so each time air traffic control changes your landing runway you must mentally commit to continuing the crossing restriction, choose vertical speed and heading, then authorize pilot not flying to change the landing runway and quickly enter a direct to the fix we were previously navigating to. reselect navigation, then rejoin a new vertical path to the crossing restriction. additionally, the limitations of this unit are leading to more and more things being removed from its database. things that should load via menus are now no longer there, or worse, show the option to be chosen but load nothing. example instrument landing system 26l, berbn transition to las. choose all the options for this and the flight management system will show them "active" but only load the faf and runway.suggestions: i walk the ramp while on the road and check out the flight deck of our competitors aircraft and even our old aircraft that they bought. frequently they have invested in garmin upgrades to keep the airframe capable of navigation in 2025 vs. cutting edge last century tech. the workload and risk of utilizing this outmoded equipment. invest in safety. we can't even do lnav-vnav."

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: General aviation instructor pilot reported a loss of terrain awareness while practicing maneuvers on a training flight in visual conditions. The instructor performed a go around and discovered the lower height above ground in that exact position.
text: during a training flight, i initiated a simulated engine failure. during the approach i had gave myself a go around altitude of 1450 feet msl based on the departure altitude. after initiating a go-around i realized the ground elevation in that area was actually above 1, 000 feet msl making the distance to the ground less than 500 feet agl. what i believe caused this accident was an improper preparation of the given scenario. in the future i will be triple checking the field elevation directly beneath my position rather than using previously known altitudes.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: A pilot practicing acrobatic maneuvers reported a NMAC with an aircraft in level flight.
text: we were in the salinas valley doing airwork. we cleared the airspace looking for traffic, once we both concluded the airspace was clear began a four maneuver series at 5, 000' msl. the first maneuver was an immelmann into a split s that led into a loop ending with an aileron roll. immediately after rolling wings level i began clearing all quadrants of the airspace around our aircraft beginning with my left rear, as soon as i got to the right rear window looking at the 45 degree behind i saw a low wing aircraft, it filled up the window, wing tip to window corner. it was at the same altitude turning into us. it was close enough that i could tell the type of landing light and i could see the individual vanes on the air intake. i immediately took evasive maneuvers performing a descending right 360. the other aircraft continued along to the other side of the valley. needless to say we kept a close eye on that aircraft while we proceeded inbound to our home airport. after some time processing the event i went to 'flight radar' and reviewed the playback of the airspace and was able to determine the time of the near miss and the other aircraft was an aircraft y. i believe what could help prevent near misses such as these from occurring would to have a dedicated training area that is clearly defined in the chart supplement, and possibly on foreflight like notams/drotams, and tfr's. maybe aerobatic pilots could reserve blocks of airspace? part of aerobatics is flying in a defined box, so that airspace could be reserved.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: TOL Tower Controller reported the control panel in the Tower has been out of service for months and has led to an unsafe environment where the Controllers are unable to turn the lights up for aircraft.
text: aircraft x about two miles out on instrument landing system z 25 requested lights to be turned up. i was unable to do so due to the control panel in the tower being out of service. it has been this way for over six months. we have aircraft that require lights to be turned up and down and we're unable to do so. this creates an unsafe environment. whenever we need the lights adjusted we have a contact for the port that has to drive to the station to adjust them. this doesn't help in real time. the port is aware and has been aware of this problem for a long time and are doing nothing to fix it.recommendation: unless someone contacts the port authority here and demands that the lighting panel be fixed, they will not fix it. this is customary for broken equipment here that is the port's responsibility.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported a rejected takeoff when they observed an aircraft on short final in the opposite direction.
text: date/flight info:day 0 | flight abcd | redacted to zzznarrative:while operating flight abcd, we taxied to runway xx at redacted after advising intentions on afis frequency redacted.x. a pop-up tower controller advised no reported traffic in the area" prior to taxi.after completing all pre-takeoff flows and checklists, and once lined up on runway xx, the captain/pilot flying (pf) set takeoff thrust. during the takeoff roll (approximately 50 kias), the captain visually identified inbound traffic landing opposite direction on runway xy. i (first officer (first officer)) confirmed the traffic by sight of its landing light, and immediately called for a rejected takeoff. the captain simultaneously initiated a low-speed rto (rejected takeoff), reducing thrust to idle, braking, and deploying max reverse.the aircraft on approach (later identified as aircraft y) was not on frequency and was roughly 200-500' agl when the captain advised them via radio to go-around. still not on frequency, aircraft y then initiated its go-around. we subsequently back taxied and returned to the ramp to contact dispatch and maintenance control, and allowed right main brake temps (amber range) to cool. once cleared by maintenance control and with brakes cooled, we reattempted departure. aircraft y returned, joined the correct frequency (redacted.x), and safely landed runway xx.our departure/flight to redacted proceeded normally and uneventfully thereafter.cause: non-towered airport operations with ad hoc tower services, opposite direction traffic not monitoring/transmitting on published frequency, and lack of situational awareness by inbound traffic.suggestions: standardized pre-departure briefings to include vigilance for potential incoming opposite direction traffic when operating in/out of uncontrolled fields.reinforcement and more explicit coordination with airport authorities and/or local air traffic control to ensure all aircraft are aware of the correct, published frequency required to be monitoring + transmitting on at uncontrolled fields via notams."

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown; No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation
synopsis: Air carrier Flight Crew reported an inadvertent escape slide deployment. Crew suggests improvement to AOM steps and numbering to decrease confusion.
text: this was a reposition flight to redacted from redacted. we had parked at the gate and completed the shutdown checklist. we are at a hard stand with no jet bridge. i mentioned to the captain that i've never disarmed the slides and opened the door. we talk about that and he leaves the flight deck to go to door l1 and i follow. we both have our efbs with us and are looking in the aom to find the procedure. captain finds it and tells me the page and we both are on page xxy out of xxz, cabin door opening from the inside. i was standing right behind the captain in the galley and he was standing at the door. we are looking at the same page. he pulls the handle up and the door opens and the slide deploys. cause. we did not disarm the door before we opened it. suggestions: change the step numbering on page xxy to follow the steps on page redacted [previous page], so 1, 2, and 3 would become 4, 5, and 6 of the same procedure of disarming and opening door from the inside.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Airborne Conflict; Conflict NMAC; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a traffic conflict with another aircraft while on the arrival. The flight crew followed the TCAS commands to descend and avoided the conflict.
text: on bojid4 rnav arrival, at hifal waypoint air traffic control advise us of aircraft y traffic in our vicinity to our 10 o'clock position conducting traffic pattern work at pne. i responded searching for traffic, however said traffic was heard reporting us in sight with air traffic control relaying same information to us. at approximately eyrie waypoint at 6, 000ft we received a traffic advisory alert via tcas. i immediately searched and found the traffic in our direction, increasing in image size, estimated 200-300 ft above us. simultaneously i told the pilot flying (pf) to descend with the resolution advisory instructing us to descent. pf conducted resolution advisory as instructed. the aircraft eventually paralleled (same direction) us to our 8 o'clock position close enough to see some finer details of the aircraft. during the descent i informed air traffic control we were receiving resolution advisory instructions to which they asked us to let them know when we could descend, in which we responded we were descending at that time. air traffic control instructed us to descend to 5, 000ft. clear of conflict" was given before reaching 5, 000ft.cause: traffic's loss of positional awareness as well as lesser than effective airspace traffic mitigation techniques.suggestion: traffic deconfliction measures need to be implemented at pne such as restriction of type of traffic pattern (left/right pattern only) as well as altitude limitations due to arrivals at class b phl."

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: ERJ-170 flight crew reported a near miss with another aircraft taking off on a crossing runway while on approach.
text: we were on a normal instrument landing system approach in vmc conditions for runway xx, and started hand flying at approximately 1000' agl. at 500' agl my copilot called out 500 stable" as normal, immediately after hearing this i heard air traffic control clear another aircraft for takeoff on runway xy. this was very close in to the landing for us to have to deal with a potential crossing traffic for our runway. i immediately looked over to that runways and saw the aircraft was slowly accelerating on their takeoff. when at 300' agl or so, i noticed the taking off traffic was around 1500' down runway xy and slowly accelerating and knew that we would meet at the runway intersection if we continued the approach and landing. i called for and initiated the go around. as we were climbing through 400' air traffic control told us to fly a heading and climb to 2000'. my copilot then proceeded to set the guidance panel for this while i flew the aircraft following air traffic control instructions. at around 500' we got a traffic alert via tcas but no resolution advisory due to the taking off traffic on xy as we passed above them. as we were dealing with this and flying air traffic control asked numerous times for the reason for our go around. we finally had to tell them to just stand by on this request. at 1100-1200' air traffic control gave us another heading and continued climb to 3000', and again asked for our reason for the go around, then switched us to departure control for radar vectors back to redacted. once level at 3000' we asked for delaying vectors while we got through all our checklists. this was accepted by air traffic control and they again asked for the reason for the go around. i then told them it was due to conflicting traffic on takeoff crossing our runway and we didn't feel safe continuing the landing. we then finished all of our checklists and proceeded to do another approach and landing. when switched to tower, we again were asked for our reason for go around. i again told them there was not enough room for the crossing traffic taking off on runway xy. the controller then attempted to argue and stated "oh there was plenty of room". as we passed with 300-500' of the traffic taking off, there is no doubt in me that we would have had either a collision or a wake turbulence issue at the intersection of the runways during out first landing attempt."

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported that after the last flight; a door was left armed and resulted in the escape slide pack falling out of the housing when catering opened the door.
text: during boarding of flight, a supervisor came on board to inform me that the 2l door on my last flight, redacted-redacted, flight abcd, was left armed. the supervisor further explained that when catering opened the 2l door to cater the aft galley the slide pack began to fall out of the slide pack housing. the caterer stopped opening the door and was able to prevent the slide from deploying and then contacted maintenance. this event did not result in an inadvertent slide deployment (isd). on flight abcd, redacted-redacted, i was working the fa a position assigned to arm/disarm door 2r, cross check door 2l, and sit at jumpseat 2r outboard. when we blocked into the gate at redacted, the seatbelt sign was switched off, i unfastened my seatbelt, disarmed the 2r door, and looked at the 2l door and cross checked it. there was a brief delay from the purser to conduct the all-call to which the aft contacted the fwd and then the purser conducted the all-call per sop. no other irregularities occurred at the time, in my experience. it was after the fact that i was made aware that the 2l door was not disarmed and cross checked properly.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC with a helicopter while in the traffic pattern of C17 non-towered airport.
text: aircraft x was conducting a local flight between untowered airports. when approaching the destination, position and intent callouts were made on ctaf/unicom at approximately 7 and 3 miles, those callouts indicated aircraft x was west of the airport and intended to cross at midfield to enter a left base for runway 17. at the time another (uninvolved) aircraft was conducting operations at the destination, landing 17. at approximately 1.5 miles, aircraft x was on a course of approximately 120m at a ground speed of 120kts and a helicopter crossed behind aircraft x within 50 ft vertically and within 100 feet laterally. the helicopter appeared to be on a northeast course (after landing, public ads-b data was viewed and it indicated the helicopter was on approximately a 050m course). the pilot in command (pilot in command) in the left seat of aircraft x did not see the helicopter until after it passed behind. a private pilot rated and flight current passenger in the right front seat of aircraft x observed the helicopter at approximately the 4 to 5 o'clock position immediately before it passed behind aircraft x leaving no time for any evasive maneuvering. as aircraft x entered the left downwind for 17, a bystander on the ground transmitted on ctaf indicating a helicopter was present or maneuvering around the approach end of 17. aircraft x kept the helicopter traffic in sight, which appeared to continue enroute to the northeast, until turning final for 17 and completed the flight without further incident. the helicopter made no transmissions on the destination ctaf/unicom even though it passed within 1.5nm of the field at pattern altitude. aircraft x did have an operational stratux ads-b receiver and ads-b traffic was being observed around the time of the nmac by the right seat occupant on an ipad. the helicopter did not appear on the ads-b traffic layer, while other nearby traffic was populated on the map. aircraft x was squawking visual flight rules with altitude reporting enabled. as aircraft x was only 1.5 miles from the destination, the pilot's focus had shifted towards identifying the position of an aircraft on final, identifying any other traffic in the pattern, and completing pretending checklists. unannounced traffic from the right was unexpected due to the traffic pattern specified for runway 17 at the destination. all lights on the aircraft x were on including nav, strobes, beacon, and left and right wing landing lights. the helicopter was over a populated area with multiple towers and obstacles. neither occupant of aircraft x recalls identifying any anti-collision lighting on the helicopter as it passed, however due to the nature of the incident it may have just been missed. the aircraft x failed to identify the approaching traffic off its right wing.based on the flight path of the helicopter, it appeared that the helicopter failed to identify the approaching traffic which should have been within their forward field of view.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported a runway incursion when the pilot taxied past the assigned taxiway hold point and a landing aircraft was instructed to go around by ATC.
text: runway at sgj is 13/31. traffic was departing from 31 on day 0. received ground instructions to taxi and hold at b6, which is last taxiway prior to 31. received subsequent instructions to hold at runway 31 and switch to tower. notam for airport lists 'runway markings faded'. pilot mistook the instructions to 'hold at 31' and misinterpreted lines between taxiway b6 and runway 31, and proceeded past hold for taxiway b6 (which is also the hold for runway 31) to edge of runway 31. after switching to tower, tower informed pilot that he had proceeded too close to runway without permission and approaching aircraft went around. proximity of aircraft was not within about 500 linear feet, but was technically a runway incursion although aircraft was not on runway 31. the runway markings, instructions, and taxiway positions for entering runway 31 at sgj are confusing without local knowledge and the notam added to the confusion. suggest that sgj ground replace 'hold at runway 31 and switch to tower' to 'hold at b6 and switch to tower' to avoid confusion in the future for runway 31.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: General aviation instructor pilot reported flying below circling minimums in visual conditions on a practice circling approach with a student. The instructor prompted the student to regain altitude during the practice circling approach.
text: i was practicing a circling approach with an instrument student and when circling, we descended a bit low. i advised my student we needed to get above the circling minimums for that approach and upon adding power, the airplane did not climb very fast. my student also ended up taking out flaps which then let us sink low while we were in the left downwind for 35 at tvy. in the downwind, we were in the range of 4700-4800 indicated and could not seem to get our altitude back. we ended up making our base turn and the aircraft continued to sink low in our base turn at which we then added full power to gain some altitude. although we were both paying attention, for practice circling approaches, it is important that we pay attention to our altitude. the minimum altitude on circling approaches is not to be broken and with days that have high density altitude, it is important we take that into consideration. for future circling approaches, i plan to not allow my students to get too close to the minimums for circling approaches so we don't allow ourselves to get too low. a better briefing of how the circling approach should go will also help the end result in the future..

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: ZTL Controller reported a clearance issuance based on the pilot's cancelled clearance which led to a CFTT and an airspace violation.
text: aircraft x called, on the ground at jzp airport, looking to pick up his instrument flight rules clearance. the d-side next to me was in training so i let them pull up the flight plan for me. the flight plan they pulled up for me was jzp...redacted...redacted...redacted... i cleared the aircraft from the jzp airport to the jzp airport as filed and since the first fix on his flight plan had him making a turn out to the nw after departure, he was released.shortly after, aircraft x called up, departing jzp and heading se bound. at the time it was not a factor with anything, he was radar identified and i waited for him to make his turn to the nw. once the aircraft was about halfway between the jzp airport and atlanta approaches airspace, i told the trainee and trainer to 'watch this guy with a80 because he still isn't making his turn.' immediately after this, the trainee got sidetracked with trying to get a point out on a guy climbing off of redacted which did not need our attention at that moment. realizing this, i quickly called the ne side of atlanta approach to start pointing out aircraft x. unfortunately, our mia (minimum instrument flight rules altitude) in that area is 041 and the aircraft was at 038 so there wasn't anything i could do at this point. the ne side approves the point out, the trainee gets on the line with the nw side of atlanta approach to start making the point out. while they are on the line, i ask aircraft x when he is going to make his turn to redacted. the aircraft responded, 'i'm heading to redacted.' as i'm questioning the aircraft, he starts flashing ca (conflict alert) with an aircraft at 050 in a80's airspace. i do the only thing i can do. i stop him at my lowest altitude of 041 and turn him to a nw bound heading immediately upon reaching to keep him away from a80's traffic. according to the d-side, a80 was watching aircraft x and they said they would keep him separated. this took both me and a80 having to issue extreme headings to our aircraft and the situation should have never got to that point.after getting the aircraft safely away from traffic and away from a80's airspace, we figure out that the pilot had originally filed the flight plan i issued him but removed it and filed a different flight plan going to redacted. when the d-side pulled up his information, they had the info on the flight plan that we issued him (going to redacted) but not the info on the new flight plan going to redacted. since we were unaware their were 2 flighplans, i issued him a clearance 'as filed' assuming he would depart jzp to redacted and not redacted. the aircraft assumed his old flight plan was removed and he was given a clearance to depart and go to redacted. this is what led to the aircraft getting to close to a80's airspace and the lack of timely information exchange/point outs led to a80 having to vector out their aircraft for aircraft x.knowing there was 2 flight plans on file would have alleviated this situation

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the ATC clearance and Jeppesen moving map does not provide information on the requirement of contacting Tower for entry into Runway 22L to get into the international ramp at ORD.
text: taxiing to the international terminal via taxiway v, given a v7 entry to the international ramp, the entry requires a clearance onto runway 22l. the jepp fd pro moving map is not representative of this requirement as it shows multiple hold short bars on taxiways that are under construction and closed. you must transition to n via y then left on v7 via runway 22l. ground control instructed us to simply taxi via v, v7 to the ramp, no mention of the need to contact the tower for 22l entry. at night or in poor visibility it would be very, very easy to have a runway incursion.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a near miss on approach to land with another 737 on approach.
text: flight abcd from redacted to redacted proceeded without issue until the final approach phase into redacted airport. upon approach, air traffic control (air traffic control) instructed us to expect a visual approach to runway xxl and advised that we would be paired with traffic for runway xxr.at approximately 4, 000 feet, redacted approach advised us to look for a boeing 737 on the right downwind for runway xxr. we established visual contact with the aircraft and acknowledged instructions to maintain visual separation. per sop, our tcas remained in ta/ra mode.the aircraft y also reported visual contact with our aircraft and confirmed their intent to maintain visual separation. however, during final approach, aircraft y overshot its turn to final and inadvertently aligned with our final approach course to runway xxl. at that point, the aircraft was nearly directly overhead and slightly ahead of us, causing significant concern on our flight deck. adding to the stress was our limited visual contact with aircraft y given their position above us. both the first officer (first officer) and i had to lean forward and twist to look up at their aircraft.playback data indicates that the separation between our aircraft and aircraft y was approximately 500 feet vertically and 400 feet horizontally. the proximity was close enough that i could look directly into the wheel wells of aircraft y above us.following the alignment conflict, we received a tcas resolution advisory (resolution advisory) instructing us to descend, which we executed promptly. concurrently, i initiated a lateral offset to the south to further increase separation. my worry was that aircraft y would descend on top of us since we were in each other's blind spots. however, aircraft y must have received a corresponding tcas 'climb' resolution advisory, as they ceased descending and subsequently executed a missed approach.due to the loss of visual contact with aircraft y (which was now almost directly overhead in a blind spot), a go-around was considered. however, i determined that continuing the approach with an offset was the safer course of action until the position and intentions of aircraft y were confirmed.once it was evident that aircraft y had discontinued their approach, we realigned with the runway and focused fully on our landing. the remainder of the approach and landing proceeded without further incident. after we left the aircraft i completed a verbal debrief with the chief pilot.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A300 flight crew reported they were unable to stop the aircraft while taxiing on the ramp when the yellow hydraulic system failed. Aircraft was brought to a stop with reverse thrust.
text: while taxing on ramp we were parked with the parking brake set while waiting for our parking spot to become available. we received an ecam fault yellow hydraulic system low pressure followed by a complete loss of yellow hydraulics. i noticed the aircraft started to move on its own. in an attempt to stop the moving aircraft i and my first officer (first officer) applied full brake pressure to the toe brakes and selected all brake settings in an attempt to stop the aircraft. the aircraft continued to move. my first officer suggested using thrust reverse. so in the heat of the moment i applied reverse thrust. the aircraft stopped moving. maintenance approached the aircraft to chock the nose gear which allowed us to safely shut down the engines. the aircraft was then towed to parking. we were informed by maintenance that a hydraulic hose had failed over the right main gear brakes.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude
synopsis: Fractional jet Captain reported an NMAC with a glider on descent as well as another aircraft moments later.
text: we were on the jaike 4 arrival to teb on vectors at 4000' and 3 miles nw of sbj. my first officer saw a glider moving right to left at out 1 o'clock position at about 4025'. he said look out and a second later just as i saw it he took controls and pushed forward to descend to 3800'. the glider passed within 100' feet of us and was not on radar with air traffic control or our tcas. we then reported to air traffic control and climbed back to our assigned altitude. not more than 5 minutes later we had another resolution advisory while being vectored at 3000' about 15 miles nw of teb. this time a visual flight rules traffic at 2500' that climbed towards us. air traffic control advised us of the traffic. we saw it then got the resolution advisory disconnected the autopilot and climbed to avoid. again reported event to air traffic control and returned to assigned altitude. suggestions: being vectored at a low altitude around some of the busiest airspace in the world outside of or below the class b airspace is not safe. we should be inside the b airspace as long as possible to help avoid the visual flight rules traffic

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Incursion Runway; Ground Incursion Taxiway
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported confusing ATC instructions; faded taxiway marking; and confusing intersections resulted in taxiway and runway incursions at MYNN.
text: from the ramp, we asked for taxi clearance for takeoff. our instructions, as i recall them, were runway 28, taxi via lima alpha, cross runway 32". we were not issued hold short instructions of any kind. as we crossed the hold short lines from runway 32 into taxiway alpha, i saw the red runway identifier signs for runway 28 ahead and to our left and continued forward on taxiway alpha towards those signs, as we were told to taxi to runway 28. also, as we cleared runway 32 and entered taxiway alpha, i was looking for taxiway markings and signs that marked taxiway hotel. we had briefed the markings on the 10-9 plate on taxiway hotel that showed the runway 28 hold short lines. in the back of my head, i was not understanding how there could not be runway hold short lines on alpha between runway 32 and hotel. the intersection is frankly, very confusing, the demarcation of when you enter runway 28 from a is not clear with actual signs and taxiway/runway markings and the chart is not well-depicted. further the red runway signs facing hotel seem to indicate the runway area is further up and seems to be in contradiction to the chart markings. as we approached hotel, where i thought we were still on alpha, tower told us to hold and told us that we were on hotel and actually on the active runway. seeing the red runway 28 signs in front of us and to our left, this did not make sense to us. the nose of the aircraft came to a stop just over the divergence of the taxi line from alpha onto hotel. in satellite imagery, i can see now the white dashed line that separates alpha from hotel and we were past that line. however, i do not recall being able to see any markings when we taxied over that area today. i believe they are severely faded or even missing at this point. i think there are several items that made up this runway incursion and ways future incidents could be avoided. ground should have told us to hold short of hotel. we would have therefore been looking for a specific place to stop instead of just rolling towards the red runway signs.we did anticipated the taxi route, but i should have paid more attention to the nagging confusion in the back of my head about the plate symbology and asked ground for clarification on where and how to stay off runway 28 once clearing runway 32 on alpha. the surface markings defining the line between alpha and hotel need to be repainted. the 10-9 plate needs a hot spot circle at this intersection with specific notes on where alpha ends and hotel begins and that this line is actually a runway entry line. better would be another symbol on the plate of runway hold short lines on alpha at hotel, not just the ones on hotel (though i suspect there is a technical reason that this isn't actually a runway hold short line, despite it being thus in practice.)the company should issue a bulletin warning pilots about possible confusion at this intersection. if crossing the line between alpha and hotel is actually entering a runway as tower stated, there should be runway signs and hold short lines at that line, not 50 yards ahead and around the corner."

anomaly: Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported receiving a terrain alert on initial approach.
text: going into sdl, got vectored for about a 10 mile right base. the wx was clear and better than 10 miles visibility.. we had all the higher terrain off to the left insight and thought our flight path on the right base looked good. we got cleared for the visual approach to 26r we were at 5000 ft at 170 knots and flaps 2.we started down, put the gear and put flaps full and slowed to 130 knots. i was descending at a pretty good rate1550-2000ft per minute, but maintaining 130 knots. around 3500ft got a caution terrain filled by red terrain warning, i adjusted my rate of decent and the warning extinguished immediately. the red warning maybe lasted a second. at no time were we in danger of hitting any terrain, all the higher terrain was well to our left. there was no terrain in front of us to hit.suggestions: i would suggest the vor a circle to land for rwy 26r, for visual approaches

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a tight vector to final approach which resulted in an unstable approach and a low altitude alert from the Tower. The Captain instructed the First Officer to level off and re-intercept the glideslope to a landing.
text: approach control gave us a vectored base leg that was almost directly to the final approach fix. it left very little room to capture the loc and get configured and slowed and then capture the gs.the first officer (first officer) is fresh new and just consolidating and still learning the airplane in a line flying setting.as we neared the faf i was working the radio, monitoring his flying and giving him suggestions to make a smooth and stable approach given the circumstances.we captured the loc just outside the faf but were too high to capture the gs so i told him to descend to try and get on the gs. we descended too fast and were under the gs as i accepted and read back the landing clearance. tower gave us a low altitude alert and i responded that we were correcting.i told the first officer to level off and we stayed around 900 feet until gs capture and continued the approach to a landing.cause: bad vectorinexperienced focaptain increased workloada few weeks ago at msy to runway 11 i experienced the same bad vector almost directly to the faf.i should have asked for a longer downwind today.

anomaly: Deviation - Speed All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Fuel Issue; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: ERJ 170 flight crew reported an over fueling event which resulted in incorrect takeoff weight and a performance degradation on initial climb causing a GPWS terrain warning. The crew reconfigured the aircraft; resumed the climb; and continued to destination.
text: we had a little over 1 hour sit between flights. after landing me and the captain both setup the aircraft for the next flight which included the route, takeoff performance and everything else based on our current release and current weather. about 30 mins before departure fuel truck arrived and over fueled the aircraft. during over fueling the eicas message fuel imbalance annunciated. we let the fueler know of the situation and called dispatch letting them know we were over fueled by almost 2100 lbs and imbalanced. dispatch told us they would send a new release with the new fuel weight since we had a light passenger load. we then contacted maintenance and ran the fuel imbalance procedure. at that point boarding had started. me and the captain both reviewed the fuel imbalance procedure and then successfully balanced out the fuel tanks which led me being outside of the plane and captain inside the cockpit. once i arrived back into plane boarding had been completed and flight attendant (fa) stated ready to close doors. we then closed the doors and ran through the proper maintenance log entry followed by a call to maintenance of successful fuel imbalance procedure. then we did a complete briefing followed by a threats briefing, originating and receiving checklist, before start to the line, and before start below the line checklist. we pushed back started our engines while the passenger had been boarded and ready for approximately 20 mins now. during pushback air traffic control notified us of delayed departure time going into redacted. we were then instructed to wait in runway xx hold bay. i was pilot monitoring and captain was pilot flying (pf). once given the cleared to takeoff clearance at redacted runway xx, everything went normal until about 400 ft where we received a epgws (enhanced ground proximity warning system) to low terrain". it was there for about 2-3 seconds and only stated once with amber resolution advisory. once we climbed through 10, 000ft we both discussed why that might have announced and both came to the conclusion that we did not reset and update the proper weight on takeoff configuration page based on the new release and new added weight factor due to the over fueling. essentially leading to a lower takeoff power (flex) setting based on the previous lower weight numbers. rest of the flight went according to plan. once on the ground we both reviewed our performance inputs and what steps we could have taken to prevent this. moving forward this could have been prevented if we updated the takeoff performance immediately once new release was received."

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: General aviation instructor reported a near miss with another aircraft while training instrument approaches at a non-towered airport. The instructor terminated the training approach and left the traffic pattern.
text: today around xa:15 i was doing instrument approaches on the giibs side with a student. i set the student pilot (sp) up for the vor a into hfy. we started about 15 miles out from hfy. we heard aircraft y doing traffic patterns so sp chose to make extra calls for spacing and visibility. aircraft y made a full stop taxi back as we were roughly 7 miles out. when we were between 5-3 miles out aircraft y took off stating they were looking for the incoming traffic. i had them insight while the sp continued the approach. roughly 2 miles out sp was getting ready to turn downwind when aircraft y stated they had us in sight and made their crosswind turn. aircraft y came within 200' of us as we were in downwind. we terminated the approach and turned out to the east toward redacted.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: PA28 Flight Instructor reported an engine malfunction during a training flight; resulting in an off airport landing. There were no injuries; or damage after landing.
text: flying lesson for private pilot. we took off from redacted, runway xx at xa:30. prior to takeoff, we conducted an engine runup. all engine instruments were normal. we took off and all take off climb indications were normal. we proceeded west to the local practice area and conducted the following maneuvers: xc procedures, unusual attitudes, and we then entered into redacted airspace so the student had practice getting into and out of a towered airport. the last maneuver was s-turns at 900 feet agl. we then started a climb to 2, 500 feet where we were going to do steep bank turns. all engine indications were normal on climb up to 1100 msl, where we then experienced a loss of throttle response. upon recognizing a the lack of engine response, i leveled off and got to our best glide airspeed l/d (vg), where we looked for an appropriate field in case i was unable to get the engine restarted. we then ran the checklist as a crew, switched code to redacted and tuned into redacted.x and communicated.we then glided into our landing, and stopped the aircraft with no damage to person, property or aircraft. upon landing, i contacted management.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: Fractional Captain reported the nonstandard threshold markings and lack of lights along with the active construction and inoperative PAPI equipment at VNY led to a very low approach.
text: landed on runway 16r vny. notams stated nonstandard markings on 16r. also north 2000 feet closed. the papi was notam'd out as well. there supposedly is a plasi" but that was nonsensical as well and didn't display any useful information. also the instrument landing system is out and only a vor b approach is available which we can only use for reference. in my opinion there is no discernible threshold markings or lights. the markings are so nonstandard that they are dangerous. on final i had to ask my co-pilot where the threshold was. all i could make out were what appeared to be aim point markings. he had been there recently and described to me what to aim for and where to land. all appeared ok when crossing the end of the runway until i saw that there was a raised marked off square that was colored orange with chevrons. also there were workers on either side of this box on the side of the runway. it appeared i was flying low over the box so i disconnected the autothrottles and applied a little extra power to float over it. it felt too low for a go-around at that point and with the situation, it felt safer to just give the power a little juice to get past the raised box.after we taxied in and disembarked the passenger an airport operations vehicle pulled up to the plane and an official requested to speak to us. he said although we landed after the threshold we were very low. i explained everything to him that i just described. he said the faa signed off on everything but to me everything is so nonstandard there right now that it is dangerous. again we could not make out any type of threshold and without a useable papi and only a vor b approach that we can really only use for reference it's just ridiculous to me.suggestions: they need to make the threshold markings and lighting visible. they need a useable papi or vasi. to me the project they are doing on runway 16r at vny has rendered the runway practically unusable."

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: CL-350 flight crew reported a near miss with another aircraft while on approach in airport traffic pattern.
text: left downwind visual runway xx. traffic advisory from the tower: 'traffic 10 o'clock, one mile, 2400 feet.' the first officer was monitoring traffic while i was flying. the first officer advised me to stop the descent and level a few hundred feet above the traffic. tower advised the other traffic of us and he reported us in sight and advised the tower that he was maintaining visual separation. he was told to pass behind us. an resolution advisory sounded with a command to descend. i saw the traffic briefly at 10 o'clock at about the same altitude and i estimate the distance about 2, 000 feet horizontally . when i heard the resolution advisory i was looking at the red and green markings on the pfd (primary flight display) and beginning to respond when i saw that the first officer already had the controls in his hands and was executing a very abrupt and aggressive evasive maneuver descending and turning right. i realized that he was not just responding to the resolution advisory but to what he was seeing through the windshield. i made the decision to allow the first officer to continue flying. the first officer later told me that he saw the traffic at the same altitude at about 200 feet horizontally and closing quickly. about 10 seconds into the abrupt descent, the tcas quickly changed guidance commanding a climb. at this, we both grabbed the yoke at the same time, pitching up abruptly. after we were clear of conflict we asked for the rnav instrument approach. after the flight i explained to the passengers what had happened and we called the tower on the phone and discussed the incident.suggestions: in hindsight, if i could have done anything differently it would have been to stop my descent much earlier on my downwind, knowing that traffic was there. i also could have asked the tower for a vector for traffic. i think going forward i will ask for an instrument approach as often as possible and do a visual approach only when i have to.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported landing gear disagree indication resulted in expeditious handling to a safe landing.
text: after taking off from redacted on xxl we received a 'gear disagree' warning message due to the nose gear not retracting in the full up position. we advised air traffic control and leveled off at 9, 000 feet and 200 knots and air traffic control [requested priority handling] for us. we then ran the qrh and contacted dispatch. we extended the gear and it locked in the down position. the captain talked to dispatch while i flew the aircraft and talked to air traffic control. we discussed continuing to redacted, or diverting to redacted or redacted. after assessing the situation with dispatch we determined that the best course of action was to return to redacted due to our fuel level. we set up for runway xxl and completed all appropriate checklists. we landed normally and upon inspection from maintenance, they were unable to find the cause of the issue.cause: there was a malfunction with the nose gear that did not allow it to fully retract in the up and locked position. the gear pin was not in and maintenance advised us that there seemed to be nothing that was wrong with the gear upon initial inspection.

anomaly: Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence; Inflight Event / Encounter Wake Vortex Encounter; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported the aircraft banked from a wind gust or wake turbulence from a previous aircraft while on short final at MMSL.
text: on approach, crossing the threshold at approximately 50 feet agl. the plane banked from wake turbulence or a gust. we heard the aural 'bank angle.' continued the landing since wings were level as immediate as we heard the aural warning. landed the airplane without incident.cause: wake turbulence from previous aircraft or wind gust. there were no reports of gusts at the field at the time.suggestions: having a straight in approach instead of the angled approach that requires a slight turn just before landing. not sure that this would've been avoidable.

text: upon arrival to pls, air stairs (ramp) was connected and gate agent knocked on the main cabin door (mcd), i gave the thumbs up and was about to crack the door per sop, when gate agent suddenly, dangerously, and very rapidly, flung open the mcd in my face. the right side of my body was right next to the mcd and my right arm around the arming handle. i quickly jumped back away from the door to avoid getting injured but this was so dangerous!!! apparently island countries rush the arrival and the opening of the mcd due to certain time constraints they are given. i don't know what these are but this is so dangerous and brought about the rushing of this csr to get my mcd open while almost breaking my arm in the process. please not only advise pls of this as this main individual is always receiving air carrier flights and i do not want this to happen again to another fa. this is also the same airport where a maintenance worker tried to open the mcd on another flight of mine, almost deploying the emergency slide and ultimately injuring the purser for that flight in the process.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: GA pilot reported taking evasive action to avoid an Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) during cruise flight.
text: i was operating aircraft x at 9, 000 feet msl, approximately 2.2 nm east of the havns intersection near bos, while in and out of a scattered cloud layer. immediately after exiting one of the clouds, i observed an unidentified object directly ahead at close range. i took immediate evasive action to avoid a potential collision.the object was black, stationary or slow-moving, and did not resemble any known aircraft, drone, or weather balloon. it had a shape similar to a desk fan, with a triangular structure or feature on top. there were no visible lights or signs of a propulsion system. the object was not observed on ads-b prior to visual contact.i reported the sighting to air traffic control. they acknowledged the transmission, but no further information was provided. i am submitting this report to document a close encounter with an unidentified and uncooperative object in controlled airspace under instrument meteorological conditions, which posed a potential safety hazard.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported flying in controlled airspace without authorization.
text: i was preparing for a short flight to document a roofing project for a building recently completed. i went through my standard preflight procedure of checking my aloft air control application for airspace information and to request laanc clearance if required, but i misinterpreted the language in the application. the app confirmed that the area was within the uas facility maps and had automatic approval up to 400'. my misinterpretation resulted in me thinking that this was a class g airspace and did not require laanc approval. upon launch i gained ~100 feet of altitude before i noticed a notification alerting me i was in a class d air space. upon viewing that notification i landed the uas and did not resume flight.i believe the primary cause for this event was my misinterpretation of the text within my mobile application and my rushed execution due to time constraints. a minor cause for this event is the text within my drone's app, as i trusted the text that indicated 'takeoff permitted'. i understand that in the future more time should be reserved for ensuring that all laanc approvals are properly received if i am intending to fly within a restricted air space that is part of the uas facility map.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: EUG TRACON Controller reported an aircraft on vectors failed to intercept the the approach course and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Vehicle
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a convoy of semi-trucks crossing a taxiway in front of the aircraft; requiring a stop.
text: cleared to taxi from 1 left turn on to 2 dash line into gate xx. ground gave us taxi in after aircraft y exiting 2. taxi instructions proceed 1 left onto 2 cleared to gate. as we began taxiing on 1 making the left turn onto 2, an airfield vehicle parallel to 1 began to drive across east to west across 2. i slowed the aircraft in the turn to accommodate the vehicle which was dangerous due to the vehicle being stopped before we began the turn. i didn't think the vehicle would try to squeeze in between the aircraft y taxiing out and our aircraft waiting to taxi in. as the vehicle proceeded causing us to slow, i noticed the vehicle was escorting other vehicles. i let the aircraft slow more, to my surprise the escorted vehicles were two semi trucks. the first truck was towing a heavy loaded paver on very long trailer and the second semi was a large dump truck. realizing the trucks would not stop even though they notice our aircraft turning into them, i flashed all of the lights and came to a stop. we notified ground of the incident after allowing the trucks to pass. none of the vehicles were hit. once clear, we continued taxiing to the gate.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Crossing Restriction Not Met; Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported receiving an aircraft generated GPWS while downwind on a visual approach.
text: during a visual approach rwyxx on the downwind the pf opted to maintain 2400 on a heading of 030 which placed the aircraft parallel to the approach path and safely at 5nm to the runway. whilst maintaining level we experienced a gpws 'terrain pull up' we climbed to 3000' and continued a turn onto base for a normal approach and landing without further incident.maintaining 2400' within 5nm of the airport on a heading that would 'eventually' conflict with terrain however given the position we did not expect a gpws and were visual flight rules completely clear of terrain.suggestion: maintaining 3000 on the downwind at 200 kts or less.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC

text: today i was doing instrument approaches on the redacted side with a student. i set the student up for the vor a into redacted. we started about 15 miles out from redacted. we heard aircraft x doing traffic patterns so the student pilot chose to make extra calls for spacing and visibility. aircraft x made a full stop taxi back as we were roughly 7 miles out. when we were between 5-3 miles out aircraft x took off stating they were looking for the incoming traffic. i had them in sight while the student pilot continued the approach. roughly 2 miles out the student pilot was getting ready to turn downwind when aircraft x stated they had us in sight and made their crosswind turn. aircraft x came within 200' of us as we were in downwind. we terminated the approach and turned out to the east toward redacted.
