synopsis: B737 MAX 8 Flight Attendant reported hearing a high-pitched; whistle sound coming from the L1 door during all legs of the route. Flight Attendant reported the sound to the flight crew; who did not notify Maintenance according to procedure.
text: i am writing this report in regard to an incident that occurred on day 0. our assigned routing for the day was redacted-redacted-redacted-redacted-redacted on aircraft x. during the first leg from redacted to redacted, all four flight attendants reported to the captain a high-pitched, dog-whistle-type sound coming from the l1 door. upon landing in redacted, we discussed the issue with the captain and agreed to observe if the sound would go away after opening and closing the door for the next flight.on the return leg from redacted to redacted, the noise persisted and was slightly worse. we again informed the captain, and maintenance met the aircraft. maintenance cleaned and greased the door seals. on the next leg from redacted to redacted, the sound returned, even higher in pitch. the flight attendant crew notified the captain and first officer that the sound had not improved, and we expressed that we were uncomfortable continuing without further evaluation. we informed them that the next appropriate step would likely be a pressurization test to ensure the issue was fully resolved.upon arrival in redacted, we were surprised to learn that the pilots had not called maintenance, had not contacted the company, and had not entered the issue in the aircraft logbook, despite multiple reports from the flight attendants that the problem continued. the same noise persisted on the final redacted-redacted leg at the end of the night.after arrival back in redacted, the captain called me into the flight deck and asked, 'what's this door issue about?' i responded, 'the same issue that we had on legs one, two, and three.' he replied, 'so if it is fixed, why should i write it up?' i said, 'it hasn't been fixed, the issue is still happening.' he then stated, 'but maintenance came and cleaned the seals and said the door was fine.' i replied, 'but the sound is still coming, and so no, it is not fixed.' the captain then pointed out that the first officer was a flight attendant for another airline for nine years and said that he 'thinks the sound is fine.' i explained that i bid specifically to work on the boeing aircraft and that the sound is not normal and is concerning not only to me but to the entire crew.the captain then said, 'ever since i met you, the first thing you said was if anything goes wrong you're going to call fatigue, ' referencing a previous comment that had been made as a lighthearted joke. he continued by saying that i have a terrible attitude and that i need to fix my attitude. during this exchange, the captain appeared visibly angry, his face turned red, and his tone was raised. the interaction was unprofessional and created an uncomfortable work environment.the flight attendant crew experienced significant ear pain and difficulty equalizing pressure throughout all four legs of the day. the continued presence of the high-pitched sound from the l1 door suggests a possible pressurization or seal issue that was not fully corrected. despite our repeated reports and discomfort, the issue was not logged or re-evaluated as required.this situation appears to be a direct violation of 14 cfr §121.703, which requires carriers to report mechanical irregularities, as well as 14 cfr §121.701, which states that before each flight, the pilot in command must ensure that mechanical irregularities disclosed by the flight crew are entered in the aircraft log. faa ac 120-72a and faa order 8900.1 volume 3 also specify that all discrepancies reported by cabin crew must be documented and resolved or properly deferred per the minimum equipment list. the flight attendants complied fully with 14 cfr §121.563 by reporting the issue multiple times to the captain.overall, this incident raises serious concerns about compliance with faa mechanical reporting procedures, proper communication between the flight deck and cabin crew, and professional conduct. the flight attendants did everything required of us under the fars, yet our concerns were not taken seriously, and the aircraft continued to operate with a potential door or pressurization issue. i would like to know that the company will take action regarding this event.

gns430's which just went black. at this point in time when the gns430's failed the system automatically reverted to guard and we lost the ability to adjust the flight plan, approach, and any frequencies. i also took flight controls and had the final say in all flight operations at this point in time. redacted approach was listening on guard as well as we were helped relay information by another nearby aircraft. i told them we had experienced a failure on both of our gps, as well as our flight instruments, and needed to receive clearance for a visual approach to runway xx at redacted. in sight i let them know and they cleared me for the visual approach. almost instantly after receiving clearance for the visual approach for xx both the pfd and mfd went black and we lost all engine indications including fuel quantity and pressure and oil temperature and pressure. at this point in time i requested priority handling and squawked 7600 per the request of approach on guard for lost redacted tower issued us a landing clearance for runway xx #1. i read back the landing clearance and advised them that we would attempt to exit the runway at taxiway 1. we were able to exit on taxiway 1 and within 30 seconds all communication failed in the cockpit and with air traffic control. the transponder also failed with the annunciation 'xfailx' before going dark. i held position once exiting the runway at taxiway 1 and waited for fire brigade and airport operations vehicles to escort. the fire chief came up to the aircraft and asked if we were okay to which i responded yes and then he told me that they would follow us to park at the academy ramp. i taxied and crossed runway xy to the flight school ramp. i shutdown the plane, advised my student not to answer any questions and immediately called school before talking to any airport personnel. person a with flight ops advised me that i should talk to maintenance. at this point in time the airport operations personnel questioned me about the event. shaky at higher power settings and the left mag barely showed an rpm loss and was rough even with carb heat engaged. in any event, we decided to shut down and call maintenance and get further direction. we shut down and while i was calling center to verify we were safe, my student noticed white smoke coming from the engine inlets. landing and taxi was uneventful and we never fully loss engine power, but it was close for a while. i said my prayers to my guardian angels which helped me calm and focus on flying it safely.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported an NMAC with a UAS during descent. The pilot took evasive action to avoid collision.
text: whilst transiting afw airspace to the east of the field, navigating to redacted. i was in a descent from around 2500 to 1600ft for pattern altitude. i glanced down to adjust prop, manifold pressure, and autopilot settings. when i looked up, i passed underneath a drone. i cannot confirm if it was a professional or recreational type. i saw what looked to be a quad-copter configuration. i was around 1900ft to 2000ft. this was roughly 2.5 miles directly east of the field. the drone must have been maybe 100ft above me, probably less as i clearly heard the motors spinning above me. evasive action was taken, however as i was already in a clear descent, it wasn't an exaggerated dive.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported being directed away from terrain by ATC during initial climb while following the departure procedure as cleared.
text: on day 0 at about xa:47 local time, myself pilot in command and sic (second in command) was given a clearance from clearance delivery in redacted. the clearance stated ' cleared to redacted direct to redacted, redacted transition redacted expect fl370 squawkxxxx departure frequency redacted.x. the clearance was read back as is and air traffic control responded with the word 'correct'. we took off on runway xx and made a right turn climbing through 5400 msl towards the redacted vor to track the 035 radial to redacted. while in the turn we went over to the departure frequency, air traffic control told us we need to turn south immediately due to terrain, while in the turn to a south heading she told us we need to maintain the 360 heading and climb immediately. we had a visual of the terrain and no warnings were issued. the air traffic control lady asked us what clearance were we given and who gave it to us. i told her what we got and she came back and said we were given the redacted departure. i told her that was not mentioned in the clearance and what we read back to clearance on the ground was confirmed by the clearance controller. the airplane was maneuvered safely and the flight continued with no problems.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: DA40 Flight Instructor with student reported engine roughness and low fuel indications during cruise. Flight crew landed safely.
text: this was a training mission. my student and i noticed a little bit of roughness when we started the aircraft originally. we thought it was most likely fouled spark plugs and we called our on call assistant flight training manager. we ran some tests and after a few minutes the roughness did not occur. run up was normal and we decided to continue our mission (instrument flight rules flight in visual flight rules conditions from redacted-redacted-redacted). during the enroute phase of flight we noticed that a slight reduction to our mixture setting caused engine roughness sooner than usual, at this point we were closer to redacted so we decided to continue towards that airport and continued to monitor the situation. we were currently headed towards the iaf for the rnav xx approach about 5 miles to go until we arrived at the fix when we got an indication for low fuel pressure. in addition to the low fuel pressure we then received a low fuel flow indication and then our egts rapidly dropped what looked like around 200-300 degrees. to me having multiple signs of fuel/engine problems indicated to me that we might have a possible full or partial engine failure. we were on an instrument flight plan however the conditions were vfr. because of the warnings and the environmental allowance we decided the safest course of action would be to head directly towards the airport rather than continue flying outbound towards the fix. we let redacted center know we were potentially having engine problems and that we needed to turn directly towards the airport and land immediately. they cleared us for the visual approach and we continued inbound. redacted center asked if we wanted to request priority handling and initially we declined, however, we changed our minds and did just to be on the safe side. we were able to land safely at redacted and contacted center on the ground to let them know we were alright and clear of the runway parked at the fbo.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Flight Instructor with a student reported a NMAC in the traffic pattern during take-off with an aircraft landing opposition direction runway.
text: we were on a regular training flight, the runway in use was 27. after about 4 landings, we noticed the wind was favorable for runway 9. we asked on downwind 'looks like the winds are favoring 9, should we switch?'no response we were on base and heard 'yeah let's change to 9.'on final we said 'okay we are on final for 9, we will make one last landing and head back towards redacted'on takeoff after this landing we had a near mid air collision with an aircraft on final for 27. we did not hear them say they were on final for 27.we took prompt evasive action and did not get in a collision, and proceeded back towards redacted immediately. i believe we should have just done a full stop landing on 9 and taxied to the start of 27.i also believe there may have been some missed comms and the other plane did not hear us say we were on final for 27.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor with student reported that the electrical system failed in the traffic pattern. Flight crew returned to the departure airport.
text: student was flying pattern, when deploying flaps after turning final electrical system failed including comms and transponder. attempted to load shed, reset breakers, and squawk 7600. instructor told student to initiate go around and climbed out and departed pattern and airspace westbound, see and avoid along with portable adsb receiver to avoid incoming traffic from the southwest. instructor contacted tower via cell enroute returning to redacted. should have remained flying in pattern until able to reach tower via cell before returning to redacted.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported a NMAC in the traffic pattern at a non-towered airport with an aircraft that was not communicating on frequency.
text: coming in for a landing from the northwest, we made radio calls at 10 6 and 3 miles stating how we were coming into the airfield at x04 entering the traffic pattern and listing for other traffic. we were established in the downwind when a traffic alert went off. at that time they were 1 feet above us and immediately behind us so close the adsb screen showed them on top of us. we made a radio call and as we started to turn away from the traffic since they were behind us and closing fast the other aircraft aircraft y made their first radio call stating they were making a 360 for traffic and spacing. no other radio calls were made by that pilot during his landing at the airport. i spoke with another pilot once on the ground stating we almost got hit in the traffic pattern by an airplane mot making radio calls.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot reported becoming aware after landing of a possible NMAC in the vicinity of BRD airport.
text: enroute to brd and decided to fly over a friends home. i was aware that there was a helicopter nearby. as i descended over the lake to maintain a safe distance from shore i identified what i thought to be the helicopter landing behind a tree line. i then verified that there was no active traffic on the ads-b traffic page on my gps and cross referenced the same on my efb application. i continued to scan outside for traffic as i approached and flew over said friends home without seeing any traffic. i then proceeded normally for landing at brd. upon arriving at friends home after landing i was informed by people on the ground that the helicopter was in fact in very close proximity at the time i flew over. the estimated near miss distances i have recorded here are based on their feedback.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: C172 pilot reported several systems failures and smoke in the cockpit during cruise and diverted to a nearby airport.
text: while enroute to redacted, approximately 12 miles east of redacted, the aircraft lost mfd (multi-function flight display), com 2, gps and autopilot. i requested vectors to redacted in efforts to land and troubleshoot. while on a 240 heading with instructions to descend to 3, 500 i began to smell electrical smoke in the cockpit. upon recognizing the danger i advised air traffic control, and diverted to redacted. on right base to land runway xx into redacted the interior and panel lights dimmed and the flap motor made a grinding noise when engaged. landing was uneventful, normal taxi and shut down.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot reported an NMAC with another light aircraft in the pattern at LAF airport.
text: my instructor and i were flying a left downwind for runway 23, while aircraft y was flying a right base/downwind, air traffic control asked us both to look for traffic aircraft y advised having us in sight, we could not locate them. a little while later while on downwind, adsb in showed them head on, same altitude. shortly, we got them in sight on same altitude, around 500ft horizontal distance. we immediately banked right, so did the aircraft y. after passing aircraft y talked to the tower frequency 'i don't know which runway they were headed to.'

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: Hawker pilot reported engine failure during climb out. Flight crew diverted.
text: aircraft x, departed redacted. initial step climb was uneventful, with level offs at 6, 000 ft msl, 9, 000 ft msl, and 11, 000 feet msl. climbing through 15, 000 feet msl an audible bang was heard from the number 1 engine, followed by a reducton in thrust and a yaw to the left. we stopped the climb at 15, 000 ft msl to troubleshoot, and advise air traffic control of a potential issue. during troubleshoot, there was no control of the engine and itt (interstate turbine temperature) spiked to 930 with an n1 of approximately 41% with no thrust. given the audible bang and lack of engine control, we elected to run the engine shutdown or failure in flight checklist, and requested priority handling. given information from air traffic control, we concluded redacted was the best option to divert to with adequate runway lengths, emergency equipment, and weather. communicated with air traffic control to complete the diversion and communicated with passengers. after completion of the engine shutdown or failure in flight checklist and diverting, we performed the one-engine inoperative approach and landing checklist. we received vectors for the instrument landing system xxr into redacted, and used crm to the fullest extent possible. landed runway xxr, exited at 1 and stopped on 2 to allow emergency equipment to inspect the aircraft. after inspection, no external damage was observed and we were released to taxi. we continued our taxi to the ramp.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: C-172 Flight Instructor with student reported brake malfunction during landing rollout.
text: on day 0, i was training with a student practicing instrument approaches. upon landing with clear skies good visibility and hardly any winds, the airplane started going towards the left . we tried applying the right rudder but hardly anything happening . finally the plane touched down and we tried to apply brakes but we had a complete loss of the right brakes . the plane would not stop .i allowed it to roll and finally i could get it to stop and was able to clear the runway safely without any injuries or damage to the airplane. it slightly went onto the grass which helped us to slow down. then i used the left rudder and brakes to exit the runway safely then shut down. the airplane was then towed to the ramp . fsdo was contacted and it was closed as mechanical issue.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported unintentionally flying a UAS in a TFR due to not seeing it on the map resource used.
text: on day 0, around xa:15 i inadvertently flew a small unmanned aircraft (drone) into a tfr zone near location x area.drone make and model: mavic proit wasn't an intentional violation but rather a chain of events, explained below, that impacted my assessment of the environment leading to an inadvertent flight into tfr area.i was aware of the tfr's, but they were supposed to be in effect later that day, starting at xh pm. i wasn't aware that there was a separate tfr for that location for a separate time frame.it wasn't a planned flight, but rather an on-the-spot decision. before the flight, i quickly checked current tfr's in garmin pilot application on my personal phone. i also confirmed that the phone had cell signal. i didn't see any tfr's for that area which led me to believe that the only applicable tfr's were supposed to start later. later that day, after the incident, i discovered that tfr layer of my app was turned off.additional factors that impacted my judgement were related to the environment and the surrounding setup. it was a public area, no checkpoints on my way in, people camping on the side of the road, no fencing or posting, no warning signs, and the territory around the launch pad was surrounded only by the short posts with a simple rope over them. an inflatable blimp / balloon was floating high a couple of miles north of me. i was rushing to get out of the location as the area was about to close which led me into not performing a more thorough check. normally, this type of drone would not take off in a tfr area. i believe what happened, as the drone spent in storage an extensive period of time, tfr database was not updated. the specific phone (not my personal phone), the drone was operated on, didn't have internet connection. the drone didn't give me any warnings or notifications.it was not my intention to flight into a restricted zone, but i totally recognize the lack of thoroughness on my part in preparation for the flight. i also realize that the above-mentioned factors cannot be an excuse. the drone was above me at all times with elevation perhaps around 50 ft. it wasn't above any other people or vehicles. there were no movement in any direction, no attempts to approach any objects, and no intentions to do so. i will take corrective actions to my environment assessment procedures so incidents like this will never happen in future. i will also ensure that decisions to fly are always carefully weighed and thoroughly planned regardless of the time constraints and limitations.i will also consider taking specialized courses for drone pilots to comply with all applicable rules and regulations.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance
synopsis: A Tower Local Controller reported they cleared an aircraft for takeoff with a taxiing aircraft crossing the departure end of the runway.
text: i was working local control. it was very busy. there was training on ground control, training on clearance delivery, a cic (controller in charge), and several other controllers in the tower not on position. the ground control coordinated a crossing at the departure end of the runway for a gap that was 2 miles away (2 min flying time). i told them it was approved and i would have a jet in position for the crossing. at the appropriate time, i placed the jet in luaw (line up and wait), and used a memory aid hung over the departure strip to remind myself of the downfield crossing. i went to other sequencing tasks, and was alerted by several controllers in the tower that the jet was rolling before the cross was complete. i cancelled the jets take off clearance in time, and they exited prior to the crossing aircraft. upon review of the tape, i did in fact clear the jet for take off. i am unsure how, and have no recollection of doing this. the s.a.i.d. (surface area information display) for the local control position was out of service. there were numerous distractions in the tower environment, including conversations about the current shutdown, double training, and lots of background noise.i do not know how to prevent this other than limiting personnel in the tower cab to only essential people who are on position. the stress of not knowing when i'd be paid was a contributing factor. i was working my 3rd unpaid overtime shift since the shutdown began when this incident occurred

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported receiving low altitude alert from ATC during approach. Flight crew returned to glide slope and landed safely.
text: the first officer was hand flying the instrument landing system 19l in challenging weather conditions. we broke out of the overcast layer around 1500' and the 1000' call was made at the appropriate time. since we had the runway in sight, my attention was divided between the outside runway environment and the flight instruments. while my attention was outside and prior to the 500' call, iad tower issued us a low altitude alert. this immediately brought my attention inside and i noticed that we were about a half dot low on the glide slope, but correcting back to the glide slope. when air traffic control asked if we had the runway in sight we stated that we did, and that we were showing we were on the glide slope. no further communications from the tower were received due to this, and the flight continued towards the gate uneventfully.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Object
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a tire failed during landing possibly due to FOD on the runway.
text: during taxi in after landing xxr in redacted, approximately 5 min after landing and crossing runway xxl, we turned onto [taxiway] 1 and heard and felt a loud bang followed by what felt like a flat tire. we came to a stop approx 100 yards after the sound and notified ground control that we may have a flat and requested operations to come take a look. operations confirmed that both left main tires were in fact flat, which began our coordination with operations, maintenance and the airport to deplane everyone and get the tires replaced. the landing and rollout was uneventful. there was a crosswind but plane was not side loaded, and touchdown was mostly smooth with normal braking after autobrake (3) was disengaged. the taxi in was normal speed and braking, on centerline the entire time. once turned on taxiway 1 it felt as if we hit something and the plane jolted accompanied with a loud bang, followed by the flat tire feel. later this was confirmed by maintenance that the 2nd tire may have failed under the weight of the aircraft and that is was we felt. according to maintenance a puncture on the first tire indicated we may have ran over something but nothing was found by operations on the taxiway or runway. all tires were in good condition during pre-flight in redacted. through flight attendant and ops coordination, air stairs were connected and passengers were deplaned safely into busses. maintenance replaced both tires on the taxiway and we (the crew) were shuttled to the terminal to continue operation and left the plane in the hands of maintenance.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a conflict after landing at SFO airport requiring the Captain to immediately stop the aircraft.  The conflicting aircraft was sent on a go-around.
text: this is kind of a two part report regarding approach and runway crossing in sfo. we briefed the arrival into sfo before tod and made sure to talk about the alert bulletin regarding sfo flight management system bridge visual. norcal assigned us the flight management system bridge visual for 28r as expected and briefed. we were vectored off the bdega arrival and onto a downwind over the bay for the flight management system bridge visual 28r. norcal started to turn us in to join the flight management system bridge visual but then simply stated 'join the localizer 28r and to look for pairing traffic.' this was a surprise to us as we were told and anticipated the flight management system bridge visual. caused a busy moment in the flight deck as we clarified which approach and were descending, turning and looking for traffic all at once. in order to make things simpler the ca asked norcal for just a regular visual approach for 28r which was granted and flown. after a safe approach and landing sfo tower told us to 'roll to quebec and cleared to cross 28l and contact ground.' as we started to cross 28l multiple red lights illuminated on the runway. ca saw it immediately and stopped and queried tower. they confirmed we were cleared to cross and at the same time sent aircraft y flight on approach for 28l around. shortly after the red stop lights extinguished and we continued to cross without incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A319 Captain reported an ECAM during takeoff resulting in a rejected take off and subsequent taxi back to the gate.
text: report, briefing, ground ops, pushback and taxi were uneventful. on takeoff roll at approximately 70 kts, ecam message eng 1 compressor vane. ecam directed eng 1 thrust idle and then eng 1 master sw off. transferred control of the aircraft to captain, and captain performed rejected takeoff. cleared runway and conducted rto (rejected takeoff) qrc and ecam, shutting down eng 1. coordinated with tower, ground and ramp to return to gate. an emergency was not declared. taxi back to gate, parking and termination were uneventful. crew post flight debrief and lessons learned conducted to include discussion with fas. verbal debriefs with dispatch, maintenance control and chief pilot. post flight mx (maintenance) troubleshooting conducted with maintenance control.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 Captain reported receiving an Oil Filter Bypass indication for the left engine during climbout.  The crew decided to return to the departure airport after receiving a second warning.
text: upon resuming climbout of redacted after a brief level off, at 15, 000 feet we got the oil filter bypass indication for the left engine. i continued flying and worked air traffic control as i assigned the first officer to start the qrh procedure. when we were able to extinguish the indication per the qrh procedures, i then transferred control and air traffic control duties to the first officer as i attempted to contact dispatch and maintenance control (per qrh procedures). as we were flying at a reduced thrust (about 74% n1 on the left engine) i stopped climb at fl250. it seems this altitude was too low to facilitate communications as the transmissions were unreadable. we were flying towards inclement weather throughout the eastern u.s. so i made the decision request priority handling to return to redacted. during the course reversal turn we got a 2nd bypass indication which required thrust to reduce to about 63% to extinguish indication. after having notified dispatch, briefed fa's, pax, and briefed the approach, i resumed pf duties. during final approach course intercept we got a 3rd bypass indication requiring thrust to reduce to about 33% n1 on the left engine. we proceeded to land without incident.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported tower directed a missed approach due to ground vehicle on landing runway.
text: visual approach 26r. tug driver cleared to cross 26r, tower initiated go around about one mile final. go around errors, initial call outs fine, received multiple headings from tower which disrupted the level change clean maneuvering. flaps were selected to flaps 5 while still climbing, shortly after level change clean maneuvering was set. the rest of the sequence was normal. compressed timeline back to approach, completed an after takeoff checklist but not a descent checklist. aircraft was landed 26r auto brakes off. manual braking was used for a safe exit on the high speed.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a trailing edge flap asymmetry lock out issue during an ATC instructed go-around.
text: during approach to [runway] xx at redacted, with first officer as the pilot flying, and at approximately 200 ft. agl, air traffic control instructed us to go-around due to an aircraft on the runway. normal go-around procedures were accomplished and after i selected gear up i noticed the flaps were indicating: rt. side 30 degrees and left side approx 27 degrees. the gear warning horn sounded but all else appeared normal. after advising air traffic control of the situation, air traffic control provided priority handling for us and vectored us while i accomplished the qrh procedures which entailed moving the flap handle to 25 degrees. no change in flap position occurred. the flaps were not oversped during the maneuver, all appropriate checklists were accomplished and first officer landed the aircraft without further incident. emergency equipment examined the aircraft after we departed the runway and found nothing unusual so we taxied to the gate while they followed.cause: trailing edge flap asymmetry lock out during go around re-configuration.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: B757 pilot reported an equipment malfunction during cruise affecting the airspeed indicator; autopilot; auto throttles and gear monitoring indication.
text: we were at fl350 after approx 2 hours flight we started getting intermittent overspeed warnings with the high speed zipper fluctuating up and down. after about 10 min overspeed wearing stayed on with the zipper down to 245 knots. after another 5 min landing gear vmo/mmo advisory message came on. the auto throttles came back trying to slow the airplane to below the zipper. we had to disconnect the at's (autothrottles). we called dispatch on satcom and had them patch with maintenance. mx (maintenance) said there might be a switch in the e/e (electronics and equipment) compartment that was causing the problem. i was not going to send a crew member down in there. i discussed diversion options and dispatch asked if we could return to redacted. i asked the crew and we agreed that was the best option. i was flying manual throttle. when we were given descent from fl360 to fl340 i used level change and the command speed dropped to 245 and the autopilot pitched up starting a climb trying to slow. i disconnected the ap (autopilot) and we got clearance to fl 280 out of rvsm. we notified air traffic control we had an autopilot problem and were hand flying. later we got a lower altitude i used vertical speed and afds (autopilot and flight director system) showed proper guidance so i was able to reengage the ap. when we descended to 10000 ft and 250 kts we were below the zipper and i was able to reengage autothrottles. the approach and landing were uneventful. however the lnd gear vmo/mmo advisory stayed on. my crew did a great job during this event. very professional.cause: equipment failure.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they received a terrain alert while descending prematurely on a visual approach.
text: terrain activation alert. while cleared for visual approach backed up by instrument landing system xx redacted, pilot flying descended to moca (minimum obstacle clearance altitude) 3600 and received a terrain voice alert for approximately 1 second. immediately disconnected autopilot and climbed. after the initial alert, terrain didn't repeat. proceeded with the approach and landed safelysuggestion: remain above altitudes on approach plate

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown
synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported a gate agent attempted to open the cabin door after the door had been armed. Escape slide did not deploy.
text: about a minute after door closure and arming, a gate agent attempted to open the door from the outside. in doing so, it disarmed the door, but she did not open the door, she walked away from it.person a, whose door it was to arm, immediately contacted me to tell me. i went back and saw the door was disarmed but the red streamer was still in place, then i looked through the assessing window to see the agent shaking her head and walking from the left side of the jet bridge to the right. i called the captain to see if he knew of any reason why the agent would be attempting to open our door. he did not but said he'd make a call. i instructed person a to arm the door again so that all doors were properly armed. i watched and crosschecked her. i then noticed a comment in crew app that maintenance wasn't done and needed to reopen the door. i called the captain and he said ok. but it was news to him. i instructed fas to disarm and cross check. the door was reopened. maintenance came on for just a few minutes then left. doors were armed and crosschecked again.sometimes i think maintenance tells the agents they aren't finished and need to reopen the door before any of the crew knows about it because after door closure, we immediately are arming and disarming... not looking at our crew app.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown
synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported the escape slide may not have been in the proper position during their flight.
text: the aircraft door closed at redacted airport, as the purser i made the door arming announcement. i could immediately tell the slide was just a longer and little more rigid than i've ever seen before. i armed the door, but it felt different this time. i cross checked and was cross checked. the flight departed and arrived without incident. i made the door disarming announcement for arrival. and when disarming the door, the slide material just felt super long. i can't describe it other than it just felt like it was further out of the housing than i've ever seen before. it was dragging on the ground and there was no way to secure it higher up into the housing. i was cross checked, and i cross checked and made the all call. i was still unsatisfied with the length of the slide, but there was nothing i could do. i was very cautious with watching the gate agent opening the door as the slide is dragging on the ground. once the door was open, customer started to come to the front for deplaning. customers with children were trying to get a view of the flight deck. meanwhile, the cleaners were trying to clean forward lavatory, wheelchairs, a umnr (unaccompanied minor) was onboard. there was a lot going on with deplaning. i notified the captain as soon as was possible. but by the time i had mentioned it to a current captain, the new captain and first officer were already on the jetway, so i mentioned it to them as well. i just said the slide seemed a little lower than normal and i didn't like the way it looked when the gate agent opened the aircraft door and that it should probably be looked at.i had an unaccompanied minor with me at the top of the jetway at the gate reader i did the handoff to the gate agent, i immediately saw the crew for the next flight. i asked the next crew who was in charge of the 1l door/ purser. the gentleman said it was him and i informed him of the slide length/ dragging on the ground situation. i also told him that i mentioned it to his captain and first officer.the texture of the back of this particular slide felt like this rubber griping material that i've never felt.i don't know what it would take for an isd (inadvertent slide deployment) to happen in regards to any slide dragging on the floor, and i'd hate to see that happen to anyone or myself for that matter so i wanted to send this report. just to bring awareness of the situation.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown
synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported a delay deplaning passengers after flight attendant did not disarm door correctly and the escape slide partially deployed. Flight Attendant cited fatigue and illness as contributing factors.
text: i had an incident with the main door procedure upon arrival to redacted. i was finishing the end of a 6 day work schedule. the day prior to the incident (day 0), i returned from out of base work and was not feeling well. i went to the room and took some otc pain meds and tried to rest. due to the aches and pains, i tossed and turned until the pairing notification came through on (day 1). my report time was xb:30. i arrived at the airport parking lot at xa:30. i scanned parking lot permit to allow myself time to make it to the terminal on time just in case i needed to stop by the restroom. upon arrival to redacted and the seatbelt sign went off, removed myself from the jump seat, turned the lights on, waited for the jet bridge. as the jet bridge moved towards the main door, i made the announcement: prepare doors for arrival and cross check. i was feeling lightheaded and still in pain. i reached for the main handle and pulled it towards myself and immediately realized that was incorrect. i pushed the handle down and pulled up the lever covers and disarmed the door. this was an attempt to correct the error. the ga (gate agent) came to open the door and a portion of the slide had deployed. i immediately informed the captain and the first officer (first officer) of what happened. the captain contacted maintenance. maintenance was able to adjust the slide and the passengers were able to deplane after about 30-40 mins delay out of the main door. i remained in the galley until the door was opened. after the door was opened, i thanked the passengers for their patience as they departed. there were no injuries.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: PA 28-180 reported a loss of electrical power and comm radios at cruise altitude. Pilot diverted and landed safely.
text: on day 0, i picked up my plane (piper archer pa28) in redacted where it spent the past couple months getting a fresh paint scheme. i intended to fly it visual flight rules back to its home base / hangar at redacted.unfortunately, i encountered an electrical failure en route. both radios went dark. transponder was still working, though, so i entered 7700 and headed for redacted which was visible off my right wing. did a circling descent south-east of the field and landed on runway xx. taxied to ramp. called and talked to local mechanic shop, which then tugged the aircraft to their shop for investigation and repairs.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot enroute to DWA airport reported an NMAC with an air carrier aircraft that was descending on arrival into SMF airport.
text: flying from redacted to dwa at 1300-1400 msl, i encountered a large aircraft (i think aircraft y) at xa:28 at about 500 ft above me to the northwest. i was below the smf class c airspace at 1300-1400 feet.when i saw how close it was and that it was descending rather than staying at its current altitude, i descended to 1000' msl and during this evasive action, there may have been a class c incursion at that point because i turned slightly south while descending to continue avoiding the aircraft.i was not talking to neither norcal air traffic control nor smf tower and was instead listening to dwa ctaf.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: SR22 pilot under training reported the aircraft would not rotate during takeoff prompting a rejected takeoff. Before the aircraft came to a stop; it veered to the left uncommanded resulting in a runway excursion.
text: i was on an instrument training trip with my instructor. we had flown all day with several stops along the way to fly approaches under the hood and stop for fuel and food. the goal of the trip was instrument flight rules training and an ipc (instrument proficiency check). i have been getting an ipc every 6 months for the past 5 years or so.early the next morning, we departed redacted and stopped in redacted after flying an approach at redacted. we refueled and had lunch and filed a flight plan to redacted for a missed approach and then a fuel stop at redacted before heading to redacted. the weather for the entire trip was cavu with light winds and clear skies. i did the normal pre-flight and runup and everything was normal. i did my normal takeoff briefing which sets an expected takeoff distance, land straight ahead if lose an engine under 600 feet, the caps deployment height, and then pull caps if between 600 feet and 2, 000 feet. air traffic control cleared us for takeoff on runway xx and we began our takeoff. engine instruments all were normal but it was taking longer than usual to achieve rotation speed. the runway was 4, 300 feet so i then decided to abort the takeoff. i pulled power to idle and applied heavy breaking. it looked like we would stop before the end of the runway but all of a sudden, the airplane veered to the left onto a grassy area next to the runway. i had no idea what happened or why it went to the left. i then thought that perhaps we blew our left tire. we ended up on the grass but we did not hit anything on exit. the tower asked if we were ok and we said we were. i tried to move the airplane in the grass but the grass was pretty thick and we couldn't move. i shut down and waited for assistance. airport ops came and they were able to move the aircraft with a tug. on inspection, we did not see any damage to the aircraft and the tires were inflated. it is unclear why we veered to the left and exited the runway. i spoke to a mechanic. the initial thought is that it could be that the emergency brake was partially engaged even though the handles was in the down position and this may have caused the issue getting to rotation speed. the left brake may have then failed which caused the veering to the left. a mechanic will take a look to determine the cause.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC near CXO airport.
text: i did a visual flight rules cross country to redacted and planned to go to redacted for landings winds were gusting 23 kts so i decided to do maneuvers 30 miles to the west of cxo. about the midway point between cxo and 60r. completed my commercial maneuvers and headed back to cxo near the south end of the lake. i made my 15 mile call received my squawk and instructions on how to enter the delta and pattern (redacted, 105, north loop, right downwind 14) i repeated back and after i put my squawk code in, i turned my focus back to the outside my peripheral vision caught aircraft y moving from right to left in the top left of the windscreen about 50 ft above me. i had no time to make evasive action. i was flying with a stratus connected to my ipad so i could see traffic around me. i was not watching my ipad at the moment due to contacting tower, inputting code in transponder, and navigating toward the 105. i never saw them until they were headed towards me as they were turning over the top of me.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported losing control of the UAS during flight. The reporter regained control of the UAS by switching flight modes on the controller.
text: while i was operating my uas at a 360-foot cruise altitude, the aircraft started losing link to the controller and performing uncommanded maneuvers. i immediately selected another 'mode' within the controller and commanded the uas to return home. i noticed that the drone was over an area that just skirts the edge of redacted class d airspace, as well as power lines, neither of which i did seek approval for.i'm pretty sure this happened because i just switched between cinematic mode and normal mode. i have since retested the drone, and it automatically responds, with no other anomalies.should i find this aircraft acting up again, i will return it to the manufacturer for repair.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported flying in controlled airspace without authorization.
text: earlier today at approximately xa:45 local time, i was flying a small uas for the purposes of filming my company's office building for company promotional material. i inadvertently flew in the sfo class b airspace and over a busy highway without receiving prior authorization from air traffic control. this oversight was due to impulsivity and a misconception about airspace regulations, leading me to believe that a low-altitude line-of-sight flight was permissible without prior authorization at this distance from the airport. impulsivity contributed because i did not properly check regulations and airspace boundaries before initiating the flight.to improve my knowledge of airspace regulations and operation of unmanned aircraft systems, i have completed the faa part 107 small uas recurrent training. i have also scheduled a 1-hour ground session with my cfi to go over safe operations of uas near complex airspace. in addition, i have ensured that all of my required registration documentation is up-to-date and located in the case of my uas. i have also labeled my uas with the faa-issued registration number, in compliance with regulations.for any future flights near controlled airspace, i will request authorization well in advance through aloft air control's 'further coordination' tool.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Air taxi helicopter pilot reported an NMAC in Class G airspace requiring evasive action to avoid a possible collision.
text: in cruise flight en route from to redacted, i spotted another aircraft head on at or near same altitude. i performed a right descending turn to avoid the other aircraft. i had been scanning inside and out for this traffic in tcas, no target forward of our aircraft was visible on tcas at the time and i had announced this to the crew and that i had other targets west across the river from us so i know it was working. tcas did alert at the last split second as i was already in the turn. it appeared the other aircraft started a climb at the same time i spotted the aircraft and started my turn and descent. when we departed redacted we heard the other aircraft check on radio and report they were inbound to the hospital from the east. radio comms advised them that we had lifted from redacted en route to base. they reported we were coming from the east had us on edge looking for them we knew our paths would cross at some point. with the position of the sun and haze and the fact that this aircraft was coming near head on made it very hard to see.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation - Altitude Crossing Restriction Not Met; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: A B737 Captain reported the B737 FMS routinely descends below the PERKN crossing restriction on the CAVLR6 STAR to IAD; and expressed concern that the profile on this STAR is too steep for B737-800 and -900 aircraft.
text: i have had numerous different b737 aircraft not abide by the crossing restriction of fl220 at perkn intersection on the cavlr6 star. we were level at fl220 with the a/p (autopilot) on, in vnav and lnav. we were given a descend via the cavlr6 landing north clearance from air traffic control. we set 9000 feet in the altitude alert window. approximately 1.0 miles prior to perkn, the airplane started a descent out of fl220 to begin the descent on the cavlr6. we crossed perkn at fl21.8. i have also talked to a lot of my first officers and they say they see this a lot too. for some reason, and it appears that it might be the older-800's and older -900's that do this the most often. this star is too steep for the 737 and many times, the airplane starts down out of fl220 early to get on the path that it thinks it should be on. there is usually a steep descent after perkn message that pops up, again, particularly on the older -800 and -900 aircraft. the max seems to do a good job on this arrival.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported after recovering from GPS jamming they had reduced navigation capabilities.
text: departing tlv we ran the gps interference supplementary checklist. the first couple pages worked great and we departed tlv. entering romania airspace we picked up on page x of the checklist, where we selected:gps interference is no longer known or suspected, and the gps has recovered * yes. then when getting to page y:either of the following is true- gps interference is not known/suspected during departure airport operations, but is suspected during other phases of flight.- gps interference continues after departure airport operations and/or the gps has not recovered* nothe remainder of the xx pages indicated the checklist is complete. the problem is that page xy is where we turn everything back to normal, and resume gps updating. this page is not completed, leaving the airplane in a reduced anp status for the duration of the flight, including the oceanic crossing. we completed the items on pages xy and xx and called the checklist complete. after resuming gps updating, our anp dropped from 0.4 to 0.04. the remainder of the flight was completed without incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported engine malfunction during climb out. Flight returned to departure airport and landed uneventfully.
text: on climb out around 15500 ft we got an oil filter bypass light. we continued the climb and ran the checklist. the checklist directed us to retard the throttle until the light went out. it finally did around 78% and we contacted mx (maintenance) and dispatch per the checklist. our vhf patch was not very good and thus couldn't have a good conversation with mx. after realizing we were going to be thrust limited and we were going into weather at redacted we decided to go back to redacted. in the turn back to redacted the light came back on and we had to reduce the throttle further to 62% to get the light out. realizing the engine was getting worse we requested priority handling and proceeded back directly to redacted. the return was normal until we got to around 7k and intercepted final. at that point the light came back and we had to pull the throttle to around 35% to get the light out. we started the apu as it seemed like that might be needed if the engine failed since the issue was getting worse. we landed without incident, had the fire trucks check us out and proceeded to the gate.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: B787 First Officer reported the nosewheel steering system malfunctioned during taxi-out to the runway requiring the aircraft to be towed back to the gate.
text: while taxiing onto runway captain was making 90 degree left turn on the runway when nose wheel steering stopped working. airplane nose was stuck at full left and pilots were not able to straighten it to light up with centerline. captain was able to stop the airplane and keep it on the runway although we veered off the centerline to the left. we communicated with air traffic control and tug was requested. maintenance was able to inspect nose wheel before we were towed back to the gate. airplane was grounded. no further issues.

anomaly: Deviation - Speed All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: A319 First Officer reported gusty winds caused an unstable approach at 50 feet resulting in a bounced landing and flap overspeed during the go around.
text: i was operating as the pilot flying (pf) flight abcd from redacted airport to redacted airport. the captain was the pilot monitoring (pm). during a go around, the aircraft incurred an inadvertent flap over speed.inbound to redacted, d-atis was reporting gusty winds out of the northwest. the pf noted speed trend arrow fluctuations of +/- 15-20 kts. approach control cleared flight abcd for the visual approach. at that point, the autopilot (ap) and auto thrust (at) were engaged. the instrument landing system to redacted runway xx was loaded into the flight management system. once cleared for the approach, the pf armed the approach. once the localizer and glide slope were captured, a mostly stabilized approach was conducted to runway xx at redacted. prior to the final approach fix, the ap was disengaged to steer clear of the wildlife area near the redacted intersection. at approximately 50' resolution advisory, the vertical descent rate increased rapidly. this was noted by the quicker than usual auto altitude callouts from the a-319. in an effort to arrest the rapid descent, the pf applied aft side stick pressure. in an effort to prevent a tail strike, the pf neutralized aft pressure when it became apparent that further back pressure would not arrest the descent. flight abcd made contact with runway xx and bounced.the pf advanced the thrust levers into the toga detent and verbally called out, going around, toga, flaps 3." i heard the pm confirm toga was set, and retracted the flaps to position 3. the pf did not immediately pitch the aircraft up into the flight director command bar or retard the thrust levers into the climb detent due to several factors. first, after the bounce, the pf needed to restabilize the aircraft. second, the aircraft was at its lowest energy state after making contact with the runway. third, the gusty winds were causing airspeed and pitch fluctuations. after the aircraft was stabilized, the pf began a climbing left turn to void the prohibited area surrounding the redacted waypoint. the pm retracted the landing gear without the procedural callouts of, "positive rate, and gear up.air traffic control confirmed that they saw flight abcd on the go and instructed us to turn to a heading of 270. as the pf continued the climb and turn to the 270 heading, he noticed the airspeed was rapidly increasing toward the barber pole on the airspeed indicator. at this point the pf became task saturated and the rest of this narrative is to the best of his recollection. the pf retarded the thrust levers into the climb detent and verbally called out, "climb". the pm responded with climb set. next, the pf mistakenly called out flaps 2. this is contrary to the taught procedure of going from flaps 3 directly to flaps 1. i believe the pm then mistakenly also retracted the flaps to the #2 position. simultaneously, we began leveling at 2, 200 feet, which was set as the missed approach altitude when the pf called for flaps up and the after takeoff checklist. at this point the pf engaged the ap. the pm stated the after takeoff checklist was complete. air traffic control instructed flight abcd to climb to 3, 000 and turn to a heading of 260, which we complied with. air traffic control then directed flight abcd to turn to a heading of 180 and maintain 250 kts., which we complied with. the pm stated he would activate the approach phase in to flight management system. the pf concurred. the pm then extended the center line of the approach off of the final approach fix in the flight management system. air traffic control continued vectoring flight abcd toward the extended centerline of runway xx. flight abcd was eventually cleared for the visual approach to runway xx. a stabilized approach to a crosswind landing was conducted on the second attempt. flight abcd cleared the runway and taxied to the gate without further incident. once at the gate, the pm stated that while retracting the flaps from the #3 position to the #2 position, a transient over speed of approximately 5 kts. occurred. the captain/pm entered the over speed into the logbook. he later stated he submitted a report.the primary causal factor for the flap over speed was the pf/ first officer's delay in pitching up into the flight director command bars. a secondary factor that caused the overspeed was mistakenly calling for and retracting the flaps to position 2 from position 3, when the correct procedure calls for flaps position 1 from position 3. a collateral causal factor was the complexity of the airspace and gusty winds out of the northwest. the pf became task saturated ensuring the prohibited area was avoided. recommend more training in proper go around procedures in more complex airspace."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A320 flight crew reported low oil quantity indications on initial climb and return to departure airport.
text: going back about a week before this event happened, i flew to redacted and saw aircraft x at a remote ramp. contract maintenance met us at the airplane that we flew in and i asked what is going on with aircraft x? the contract maintenance guy said that the right engine was just changed and a carbon seal let go and the engine lost 5 quarts of oil from the time it left the departure airport. about a week later, now i was flying aircraft x. i looked at the history in the logbook to confirm my memory about the airplane & right engine. i briefed the first officer (first officer) about the history during the cockpit prep and the brief. not only did we check the oil quantity at the gate, we also checked after starting the engine and before takeoff to see if there was any major change in oil quantity. everything was normal until about 7000 feet when we got an advisory for low oil quantity (4.5 quarts) on the right engine. i asked the first officer to tell air traffic control we want to level off at 8000 feet. by the time we got to 8000 feet the oil quantity was down to 2.0 quarts. i had a strong feeling that we were going to lose the engine soon, so i told the first officer to tell air traffic control we are returning to the airport.we went through all of the procedures for returning back to the airport. we were an overweight landing so we did the overweight landing checklist. during the descent the oil quantity did rise to 6.0 quarts, but i figured it was due to the engine being at idle and not at climb power anymore.on final for the runway the oil quantity went up to about 12 quarts. by the time we parked at the gate the oil quantity went to 17 quarts. we wrote up the right engine for the oil quantity indication and the overweight landing. i then spoke to dispatch.after we switched airplanes, our gate was right next to aircraft x and we could see maintenance had opened the right engine cowling and he was putting absorbent pads on the ground to soak up the fluid (i am assuming engine oil). i didn't ask for the first officer to run the low engine oil advisory checklist because this engine had prior history of oil loss.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: Hawker 900XP pilot reported engine failure during climb out and return to departure airport.
text: aircraft x departed redacted. initial step climb was uneventful, with level offs at 6, 000 ft msl, 9, 000 ft msl, and 11, 000 feet msl. climbing through 15, 000 feet msl an audible bang was heard from the number 1 engine, followed by a reduction in thrust and a yaw to the left. we stopped the climb at 15, 000 ft msl to troubleshoot, and advise air traffic control of a potential issue. during troubleshoot, there was no control of the engine and itt (interstage turbine temperature) spiked to 930 with an n1 of approximately 41% with no thrust. troubleshooting resulted in no regain of engine control.given the audible bang and lack of engine control, we elected to run the engine shutdown or failure in flight checklist, and requested priority handling. given information from air traffic control, we concluded redacted was the best option to divert to with adequate runway lengths, emergency equipment, and weather. communicated with air traffic control to complete the diversion and communicated with passengers. after completion of the engine shutdown or failure in flight checklist and diverting, we performed the one-engine inoperative approach and landing checklist. we received priority handling into redacted, and used crm to the fullest extent possible. landed runway xxr, exited at 1 and stopped on 2 to allow emergency equipment to inspect the aircraft. after inspection, no external damage was observed and we were released to taxi. we continued our taxi to the ramp. post flight inspection revealed no visible external damage.cause: engine seizure/failuresuggestions: this was an event that occurred without prior indications of an impending failure.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation - Speed All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported momentary loss of aircraft control while flying through turbulence over FILPZ intersection at 12;000 feet.
text: flight was in cruise phase at 12, 000 ft, with fluctuations of airspeed +/- 15 kias, +/- 1, 000-1, 500 fpm variations, lateral rolling, and stall protection caution on eicas. landing went without further incident. negative injuries, negative damage to aircraft. all personnel notified as appropriated per fom.cause: severe turbulence encountered during cruise phase over filpz on filpz4 arrival at 12, 000 ft.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation - Speed All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot reported while in cruise flight experiencing severe turbulence resulting in a gain and loss of altitude and airspeed.  The flight crew was able to regain control of the aircraft and landed safely at their destination.
text: we were flying back from cho. at 12, 000 feet, we experienced severe turbulence with +/- 1500 fpm and +/- 15 kts airspeed. we were imc and no precipitation was shown on on-board radar. there was no injuries or damage reported and the flight continued as normal.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance
synopsis: Air carrier Technician reported that while they were troubleshooting post flight reports; they were distracted by management due to time pressure.
text: aircraft x had a return to gate event on a live flight. i was assigned with person a to troubleshoot the fault. during troubleshooting i discovered roughly 30 faults and warnings on the pfr (post flight report). it was a very difficult discrepancy to troubleshoot. what made it even more difficult was the fact that i had my supervisor, person b, trying to give me technical advice with minimal knowledge of the fleet type. he came out to my aircraft twice and had also chimed in on a phone call to my lead with technical advice. i was calling, my lead to tell him to inform management it was best to find a swap for that flight. when person b was at the aircraft he made multiple suggestions which all were 'shooting from the hip' ideas. he suggested finding a circuit breaker to reset, the possibility of a hydraulic leak, and the best one yet, the possibility that the engine idg (integrated drive generator) plug was arcing. roughly 30 minutes prior to the gate call he was in the work center telling us that he is unfamiliar with airbus and trying to learn. he also was asking for updates on our troubleshooting and asking about our expectations. all of this was unnecessary pressure and clouding of our judgment. lastly our manager, person c, bypassed his supervisor person b, and both of the leads to drive to the gate from the hangar and ask us technical questions and ask for updates. he stated that his update from person b was unclear, and he as well wanted to know if we tried a circuit breaker reset after i showed him a printout of the 30 faults on the pfr. this is a normal thing here at redacted. we constantly have management (commonly including managers) and supervisors bypassing the chain of command for updates and trying to help us work aircraft with only revenue and cleared deferrals in mind. this has to stop.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance
synopsis: Air carrier Maintenance Inspector reported they verified the torque of the main landing gear retract actuator mounting hardware and was later notified that the actuator was installed incorrectly.
text: aircraft x came in as a drop in aircraft for maintenance with a leaking mlg retract actuator. once the actuator was replaced and installed by the day shift crew i varified the torque of the mounting hardware. i was later informed that the actuator was installed 180 degrees backwards.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: Flight Instructor in a light sport aircraft reported while in the VFR traffic pattern the engine quit resulting in the flight instructor taking the controls and landing safely at the airport.
text: normal training flight, went to work on maneuvers in the area. no issues arose then. went to redacted to work on touch and gos. no issue the first 3 times. on the 4th, tower instructed us to do an early crosswind and we complied. once about midfield, engine quit. i took controls from my student and attempted to restart engine with no luck. told air traffic control our engine failed and we need to land xx l. tower cleared us to land, and we landed just before taxiway 1 and taxied off the runway at taxiway 2. after we taxied off, tower asked us 'how many souls, how much fuel.' we shut down the plane and wait for airport ops to come to us. once out of the plane noticed dripping coming from the engine. upon closer inspection, found that it went down the underside of the aircraft. i suspect a coolant tube popped off. air traffic control was professional and cleared the area for us, appreciate them immensely. student was ok, instructor ok.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Fuel Issue
synopsis: Mooney M20M pilot reported a rough running engine; followed by complete power loss; due to fuel mismanagement and starvation. The aircraft was able to land safely; without power; at a nearby airport.
text: i advised air traffic control when the engine faltered. i turned on boost pump and engine smoothed. after a short period i turned off the boost pump and engine continued ok. however, in another minute or so, engine faltered more seriously. i requested priority handling and air traffic control vectored me to redacted, where i landed safely without power. after lengthy phone consultation with my mechanic he believed i had a fuel quality or supply issue. upon investigation i found i had run a tank dry.how did this happen? this aircraft is heavy, with only 840lbs useful load. in addition, it has stc's extra fuel capacity of 118 gallons (708lbs). as a result, we (aircraft owned with others) try to fill to 60 gallons. the only way to measure this is with strapping tables supplied by the previous owner. i was about to switch tanks when this incident occurred, believing there was 5 gallons in the left tank. after requesting priority handling, i did switch tanks but when that didn't provide an immediate fix i switched back to the tank that later proved to be empty. this was a mistake---i should have realized there could be vapor in the line. in my defense, i never considered i had an empty tank. when i added fuel at redacted, i learned that the strapping table for that tank was 2-3 gallons high.this incident has prompted much discussion among the owners. we will all be more conservative in fuel planning and monitoring. it has raised an issue of whether the jpi (j.p. instruments) fuel totalizer is reading a gallon or so too low. we use that to add fuel at the end of a flight and any error could accumulate, though not to a large amount because of the cross check provided by the strapping table. life was simpler when we had a bonanza and filled the tanks after each flight.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: Flight Instructor and Student Pilot reported landing safely after experiencing an electrical fire in their Cessna 150.
text: my instructor and myself were flying on an instrument flight plan from redacted to redacted to do the practice instrument landing system xx go missed then back into redacted with the rnav xy. my instructor had the controls to demonstrate the approach and the steps for the instrument landing system. we were on vectors to final descending from 4000 to 3000 cleared for instrument landing system xx to redacted. we had the cabin heat on periodically through the flight and 3 miles before the faf my instructor noticed extreme heat by their feet which i didn't experience on my side and then a puff of smoke emerged from below the panel on my instructor's side. they then let redacted approach know that we were experiencing an electrical fire and that they were going to shut off the electrical equipment. they proceeded to follow the checklist shutting off the electrical equipment making sure cabin air and heat were off. once the fire appeared to be out they turned the battery, alternator, and avionics on one at a time slowly to ensure nothing reignited to contact redacted approach. we were then switched to redacted tower and given a landing clearance then landed.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Fly Away (UAS)
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported flying at night without anti-collision lights; without a LAANC authorization; and losing control of the UAS. The UAS landed on the roof of a building and was recovered.
text: i was attempting to capture nighttime aerial photos of a building while following dji's flight parameters. the dji app permitted flight up to 200 feet agl, and i assumed that this limit complied with local and federal regulations.during the flight, i momentarily lost control of the drone, and it unintentionally landed on the buildings roof. fortunately, there was no damage to the property or injury to anyone.i immediately reported the lost drone to dji, who confirmed the incident and arranged a replacement. they did not mention any legal implications.the following morning, i contacted the buildings security team and the police. they successfully recovered the drone. i sincerely apologize for this incident. i take full responsibility and will ensure full compliance with faa regulations and local airspace restrictions in all future operations.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported forgetting to inform ATC of the conclusion of the mission as required by their COA.
text: after landing, the rpic forgot to contact redacted atct about the end of the operation. the rpic does not have a post-landing checklist that would have prevented the mistake.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported inadvertently flying about 400 feet AGL due to not recognizing change from feet to meters on the transmitter.
text: was flying my exo blackhawk 3 pro to take some pictures. it was very bright sun. somehow my controller changed from ft to meters and i ascended to 200. i thought it was feet and didn't notice till post processing of the flight that it was 200 meters instead of 200 feet. actual altitude was 658.23 feet. i have added a checklist item to verify metric vs imperial.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Airborne Conflict; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Tower Local Controller reported a pre-coordinated UAS flight deviated from its published procedure into the path of air carrier traffic on final approach; requiring the Controller to direct a go-around to avoid the UAS.
text: i was working local east and responsible for runway xxr. the city had just closed xxc for scheduled maintenance. the tracon called and said a flight check was going to be too close to the final for xxl so all of the arrivals were going to come to xxr. within 5 minutes or so of that information reaching me the front line manager (flm) came over and said that a drone had been authorized to come up and operate in an area just west of the approach end for xxr. west of taxiway 1 is what i was told. 1 is the parallel taxiway to xxr and is approximately 500 ft west of xxr. i thought to myself, boy that's real close to my runway especially if all the traffic is coming over here. almost immediately the drone departs in the area and starts flying around. within a minute of that the drone starts to deviate from the plan and appears to be outside the approved area and now directly over the final. the drone appears to just higher than the tower so approximately 400ft msl. i told the first plane that was on final about the drone coming up to his flight plan. when the drone stayed on the final and the aircraft was on about a 3 mile final i sent the plane around. the supervisor started to call the phone number we had for the drone operator and was told that that's not them. so now we had an unauthorized drone on the final. three more aircraft were sent in for an approach to that runway and i had to send each of them around as we couldn't get a hold of the drone to move them out of the wayrecommendation: if we are going to approve drone operation so close to a runway we need to stop using that runway until the drone is back on the ground. we need to think about what could possibly happen if the drone operator does not follow directions, which is becoming more and more common here

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Illness / Injury; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a Cabin Altitude warning light during cruise. Crew referenced QRC; started an emergency descent and landed uneventfully.
text: shortly after starting a vnav profile descent into redacted on the redacted arrival out of 38, 000 we received a cabin altitude warning light and warning horn. quickly glanced up at the cabin
