synopsis: Air carrier cargo Captain reported a rejected takeoff due to temporary loss of directional control.
text: as i advanced the thrust levers to 40% n1 and declared 'engines stabilized' i observed that the number 2 engine spooled up slightly more than the number one engine, i prematurely touched the toga button with my right pinky finger. upon accelerating past 30 knots, i noticed the aircraft deviating left of center despite positive control with the control tiller, and realizing the airplane was not stabilized, i decided to reject the takeoff at approximately 40 knots.problem was identified as i noticed the airplane veering left of the centerline despite positive control with steering tiller at about 30 knots.cause: prematurely (accidentally) touching the toga button with my right pinky finger.response was rejecting the takeoff and told my first officer to inform air traffic control that we rejected due to loss of directional control. i then stopped on a taxi way (after being instructed by the tower) safely clearing the runway.suggestions: being extremely careful when advancing the thrust levers especially in wintry conditions such as with unknown runway conditions like blowing snow, ice and gusty winds.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported the Purser told them they had an NMAC on initial climb.
text: yesterday shortly after takeoff from redacted we had what i was told by the purser was a near miss. meaning the pilots had to abruptly pull upwards in order to avoid being hit by another aircraft. we were still seated due to turbulence but we had already passed 10, 000 ft because the purser was in the middle of his announcements when this happened. i remember myself and the other flight attendant in the back looked at each other in shock and held onto our jump seats. it felt like a roller coaster almost so we automatically knew it wasn't turbulence. it felt like when you are driving and have to swerve quickly in order to avoid hitting something/being hit. the pilots pulled upwards bringing the aircraft higher in such a quick manner that we were instantly concerned. after finishing the inflight service announcements the purser called us and asked if we all felt that and if we were okay. we told him yes we felt it and luckily we were all still seated so we were physically okay. later on towards the end of the flight the purser came back and told us that during a lavatory break the captain had told him that we had a near miss with another aircraft and that's why they had pulled up like that so abruptly. the captain also told him not to mention anything in front of the passengers. the purser then told us not to say anything to anyone and to keep it between ourselves/the crew. we were both stunned and couldn't believe what we were hearing. after landing i was expecting the pilots to at least debrief us since all passengers had deplaned and we were keeping the aircraft for our return flight to redacted but they did not. i even waited in first class for them to open the flight deck and come out to and talk to us but they never did. i was still in shock and shaken up so i just went to the lavatory in the back and just cried. i was so scared and feeling so many emotions and didn't want anyone else to see me cry. i am grateful that the pilots were able to get us there safely but it was off putting when nothing was said about the incident after the flight. it does not make me feel safe or comfortable knowing what happened and not being able to discuss it with the pilots after the fact.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS)
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported conducting a UAS flight in controlled airspace without authorization.
text: so i had a strange, interesting, and confusing situation on day 0, between xa00 and xd:00pm. no harm or no foul has arisen from this situation, but i feel i obviously need to report it. so up in location x here, there is an area just to the north of location x that puts on an event.i brought one of my drones, to make a little video for myself, and social media. before going to this event - i have seen multiple previous drone and aerial videos of this exact event, at the same location, from not only this year, but from years past, and multiple media sources. all available and visible on their website. i was not operating in a commercial capacity, strictly for unpaid, personal social media content, if it matters. so once i was out on location x i opened up my app, i have multiple apps, but mainly use drone buddy, because it shows humidity, wind stats, sunrise sunset all relevant information and airspace conditions. so i checked my app and everything was in the clear. when i fired up my mavic 4 pro, no warnings no nothing outside the norm. so i put up to the south of location x, recorded a 13 minute hyperlapse, a couple low altitude short videos and pics - all of the rest of the media that i acquired during my time on location x was taken with a handheld stabilizer camera. i am very worried that i ended up putting my drone up in restricted airspace potentially? i am very worried i did something wrong.i am a proud us citizen with a profound love and respect for our military.i got no warnings, no notifications on my drone or software. got no warnings or notifications on my drone buddy app. nothing.i had no idea how close i was to location y until we left, heading north, towards location z. when i got to the stop sign and i realized that i had only driven a couple miles and i'm looking at equipment behind a fence. i know something isn't right. to start off with me and my wife went down to location x for lunch first. i had no idea how close i was to location y. immediately upon seeing how close i was to location y i pulled over by the new structure being built, located the authority for the airspace, and called person a, to see if there's anything i need to do, tried calling multiple times and left a message - before i left the area, headed for home.so i'm self-reporting this incident which i feel is the correct thing to do here. obviously the last thing i want is any sort of trouble or problems.upon returning home - home, i researched what i need to do, immediately. i think i may have panicked for no reason - according to everything i can find here - i was not in restricted airspace, but warning space.being an moa - with no visible air traffic whatsoever - i think i'm ok? the before you fly app shows that the area i was over - directly over location x - is well outside the restricted area. so my initial panic set in, when we left location x, heading back towards location z... and seeing a fence line with equipment on the other side was deeply troubling. so i then checked what multiple flysafe and before you fly apps show - i have now triple checks here on my before you fly app on mavic 4 pro, and mini 5 pro controllers - it shows the area of location x i was flying over is free and clear, with the immediate base showing as restricted.on my matrice 4t controller - it shows the overall area being a warning zone, with the immediate location y being an enhanced warning zone.all 3 controllers are reading that there is no restricted zone where i was.i have pulled up the immediate area over location x on both forms of the faa airspace maps - both show that - i feel somewhat confident i did not encroach into any area i was not allowed to fly. i am still sending this - because it is the right and true thing to do, to make you aware.hope all is well - and i hope you see i take this very seriously. the last thing i ever want to do is be out of compliance in any way.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Airborne Conflict; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: SCT Controller reported chronic communications issues; airspace complexity and design; staffing; along with procedural failures resulted in near collision events at LGB. Controller recommended airspace reclassification; and staffing and equipment improvements.
text: i was working lgb departures. we had frequency issues and were using ecs (emergency communication system) frequencies. i was having trouble communicating with aircraft. this aircraft x departed lgb didn't come over to my frequency almost collided with several aircraft and then lgb tower switched him over. lgb continues to be a dangerous place to fly in/out of. we added the frequency issues, bad staffing, meaning no help whatsoever, and a very complex airspace with no protections. i have said this before and i will say it again. we will have a midair in this area. the bad equipment, frequency congestion, bad staffing (less eyes on the scope) and no one to help coordinate on a landline, and lgb tower also being so busy and i'm sure understaffed we have created the perfect environment for a disaster. recommendation: class c that actually protects arrivals and departures. staffing!, we need to find a way to communicate with aircraft and not get step on.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: B737 Captain reported accepting an aircraft with a deferral he didn't feel was entirely safe.
text: aircraft x was dispatched with minimum equipment list 28xxx for the #2 spar valve light, which stayed bright (indicating 'in transit') when the cutoff lever was moved to cutoff. i've had several deferred valve lights recently, this one caught my attention. the minimum equipment list allows dispatch but requires a mechanic to verify operation of the actual valve 1x/day. i called the dispatcher, who patched in maintenance control then the chief pilot and a lead mechanic. none was able to give greater technical insight than my ground-school understanding of the fuel feed system. all of them reasoned that boeing, the faa, air carrier x, and the union have all signed off on this deferral, and the chances of the valve failing to begin with are pretty small, not zero, but small. with all due respect, no one disagreed with my concern, that just because the valve worked when a mechanic checked it doesn't mean it will work now - and while that is always the case, the lack of an indicator light could lead, in the event of an engine fire, to the possibility of the loss of redundant shutoff valves between the fuel tanks and the burning engine. not having that information during an emergency could cost the pilots critically. i accepted the aircraft, but in retrospect, not being able to verify the position of the valve seems like unnecessary risk. the analogy i offered is that i would not accept an aircraft with no gear-down indicator light even if the mechanics verified operation of the gear down-locks before every flight. sure, the valve probably won't fail, and the gear will probably come down, not being able to verify it is the problem. our first mandate is safety. everything else comes after.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A321 Captain reported that they accidentally released the brakes early while parked at the gate and the aircraft rolled forward.
text: the flight deck environment had been quite busy during preflight preparations as a flight deck jumpseater was conversing with us and another cabin jumpseater in the flight deck while we were accomplishing and the various tasks necessary to ready the aircraft for departure.about 7 mins prior to departure time, ramp indicated ground to flight deck, ready for brake release and pushback" i told them to "standby" as we had not completed the before push checklist. while getting the flight deck jumpseater settled in and organizing various papers and things on the console, i accidentally released the parking brake and the aircraft moved forward slightly. realizing my error, i immediately reset the brake. once the before push checklist was complete, i contacted the ramp and they replied that "they were ready a couple minutes ago when they first called us, but then they felt and heard a shudder. not knowing what it was, they called a ramp supervisor to troubleshoot what it could have been and inspect the tow bar to make sure everything looked ok." i advised them that i had accidentally released the brake a few mins earlier and maybe that was the cause of the shudder they felt and heard. they seemed to agree but went ahead with the inspection anyways. they decided to swap out the tow bar just in case, and we pushed back with no problems."

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported uncommanded aircraft movement after brake release at the gate following unclear communication with ground personnel. Captain reapplied the parking brake.
text: inbound aircraft arrived at gate xx later than scheduled. flight crew prepared aircraft for departure in a timely fashion. upon making contact with ramp agent via interphone, the ramp agent sounded agitated and spoke in a rushed manner. ramp agent requested the flight crew to 'release brake we need to reset something'. ca said 'parking brake released' and released the brake. the aircraft was not chocked and started to move. ca immediately reapplied the parking brake. the movement prompted the ca to query the ramp agent regarding whether or not the aircraft was captured. the ramp agent responded by saying 'sorry it was not captured it is slippery outside' . the ground crew then removed an apparently disabled tug from the safety area and pushed the aircraft normally with a new tug.cause: during this event, i was heads down as i had accidentally entered the operations frequency twice in the standby and needed to relocate the correct ramp frequency. due to the fact that i split my attention between this task and listening to the ramp conversation, i did not catch all the details which reduced my situational awareness and ability to back up the captain. the ramp agent was somewhat difficult to understand, was rushing to replace the disabled tug, and did not give any reason for the brake release instruction that would have caused the flight crew to question if the aircraft was secured. the ramp agent requested that the captain release the parking brake when the aircraft was not otherwise secured, likely due to pressure for an on-time departure.suggestions: in the future, i will question thoroughly any instructions from ground crew to release the parking brake for any non-standard reason. i will make sure the captain verifies with the ground crew that the aircraft is secured prior to any non-standard brake release instructions.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Wake Vortex Encounter
synopsis: Phenom 300 First Officer reported landing with the yaw damper engaged after being distracted by a wake turbulence encounter on descent into LAS.
text: landed with the yaw damper engaged after my normal flow was disrupted by wake turbulence avoidance. we were in trail of a heavy and had been clipping his wake down the approach, so i chose to hand fly and stay a dot high to avoid further wake. due to being high, i was having to pay extra attention to maintaining stable approach criteria and forgot to turn off the yaw damper. landed uneventfully and turned off the yaw damper upon realizing it was still engaged, during the rollout. suggestions: could have asked for s turns or slowed to final earlier instead of having to fly a dot high, this would have removed the need for extra focus on staying within stable criteria during the final several hundred feet of the approach.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Inflight Event / Encounter Other / Unknown
synopsis: Fractional jet Captain reported GPS jamming during cruise in international airspace. The GPS signal recovered after a period of time and the flight continued to the destination.
text: during our flight we encountered almost constand gps jamming. the ads-b out fail and the synthetic vision system fail amber eicas came on every 2 minutes at an average. this happened just before the rixen waypoint to just after the tugta waypoint. we had briefed the possibility of jamming and/or spoofing before the flight and were well aware of the areas on the map where this could occur. the aom checklist was executed.suggestions: it is important to study the map and flightplan before the flight and brief this and the checklist thoroughly, so as not to be surprised when the jamming actually happens.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a GPWS terrain warning on approach to ROA. Crew executed missed approach and returned for another landing.
text: cleared for the visual 24 into roa, crew was on vertical and lateral guidance, essentially just flying the rnav visually. crossed hiban at 3700 and continued down towards the runway. shortly after initiating the descent we received a terrain terrain" warning, even though we were on vertical guidance. we executed an go around and elected to attempt the approach again, this time not accepting a visual. we landed safely with no further incident the second time around.suggestions: we were a little fast, (about 180 kts.) so the descent rate needed was a little higher than it would have been otherwise, which could have possibly tripped the warning. second attempt we made sure to slow down and configure early to utilize a shallower descent rate."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: B-777-300 pilot reported autoflight EICAS messages during descent along with aircraft roll oscillations without pilot input. On final approach the aircraft automation returned to normal.
text: preflight, start, taxi, takeoff, departure and enroute phases were uneventful. on the redacted arrival to runway xxl at redacted, while descending through approximately flight level (fl)180, an autothrottle discrepancy eicas message was displayed. the auto-throttles became inoperative and did not reset.shortly thereafter, at approximately fl170, a thrust asym compensation eicas message appeared. the thrust asym compensation checklist was completed and appeared to reset the system, however, the auto-throttles remained inoperative.at approximately fl160, the thrust asym compensation message returned. within a few seconds, the aircraft began rolling left and right up to approximately 30 degrees of bank. the captain (pf) disconnected the autopilot in an attempt to arrest the roll oscillations. despite opposite control inputs and autopilot disconnection, the aircraft continued rolling for approximately 2-3 oscillations before returning to wings level. the thrust asym compensation message would not reset again.approaching the redacted [vor] hold at approximately fl110, the autopilot was re-engaged. the aircraft appeared to respond normally, with the exception of the auto-throttles. flch mode and 220 knots were selected and indicated normally.shortly after leveling at fl100, the aircraft again began oscillating in roll. no yaw oscillation was observed. the autopilot was disconnected, however, the aircraft continued to oscillate and did not immediately respond to pilot control inputs for several oscillations. the flight control diagnostic page was selected. control surface indications corresponded with the roll oscillations, and no rudder movement was observed. after approximately 2-3 additional oscillations, full manual control was regained and the aircraft returned to level flight.approximately 5 nm prior to entering the redacted [vor] hold, the captain (pf) directed the first officer (pm) to notify air traffic control and request priority handling for an approach to runway xxl at redacted.while descending through fl90, all mode control panel (mcp) modes appeared to become inoperative. no modes could be activated. no mode indicator lights were on. at approximately 5, 000 feet, on an 14-mile base leg for runway xxl, mcp functionality appeared to return. loc capture and approach mode functioned normally. auto-throttles became available and functioned normally through landing.a normal landing was accomplished. ground control directed the aircraft to stop on taxiway 1 and contact emergency services. while stopped on the taxiway. the first officer transmitted that no additional assistance was required. the aircraft taxied normally to the assigned gate and was shut down without further incident.causal factors are unknown at this time, without additional information from maintenance post-flight data from the aircraft.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict NMAC; Deviation - Altitude Undershoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance
synopsis: B737-800 pilot reported executing a missed approach due to flap malfunction; during which they had an NMAC with a departing aircraft.
text: while conducting the rnav (rnp) z to runway xxr at redacted we experienced a trailing edge flap disagree and flap asymmetry with our left trailing edge flaps indicating 10 deg and our right trailing edge flaps indicating between 10 and 15 degrees with flaps set to 15 degrees. we requested priority handling and executed a go around receiving radar vectors east of the field at 9000' msl. while performing the checklist and coordinating with dispatch and air traffic control we received a tcas traffic advisory followed very quickly with a tcas resolution advisory for traffic 500' below us and converging. we complied with the resolution advisory climb command with gear and flaps down at approximately 180 kias until clear of the traffic. we queried air traffic control about the traffic conflict as we were under positive radar control and dealing with a flight control malfunction. they stated that they gave us instructions to climb to 10k but the transmission was stepped on. we never received or responded to any traffic call outs or instructions from air traffic control to climb. we never saw the aircraft and it passed as close as 200' on tcas. we completed our checklist and landed uneventfully on runway xy. cause: air traffic control did not clear our flight path resulting in a near miss.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ATC low altitude alert during descent into JFK due to incorrect altimeter setting.
text: descended below cleared altitude due to wrong altimeter setting.cause: wrong altimeter setting, causing a missed level off alt of 1500. was alerted by air traffic control of low alt. usually i write down atis identifier followed by last 2 digits of altimeter setting. the setting was supposed to be 29.64. i mistakenly wrote .96 instead of .64.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance
synopsis: A319 First Officer reported initiating an emergency descent in response to an excessive cabin pressure warning. Flight diverted to nearby airport.
text: climbing out from redacted, we were filed for higher and leveled at fl340. soon after we get an ecam for excessive cabin pressure followed by a rapid descend on the ecam. we performed our memory items. masks donned and rapid descent initiated. descended to 10, 000 feel, and vectored off the airway about 10 degrees and notified air traffic control of our issue and our direction of flight. we handled the on going ecam messages all the way down and advised air traffic control of our diversion to redacted. we informed dispatch, flight attendants and passengers about our issue and new destination. none of the passengers oxygen mask dropped during this event and no one was hurt or harmed. we notified air traffic control that we did not need any medical assistance when we arrived in redacted. we landed in redacted and again asked if anyone on need any medical assistance which no one needed. we taxied to the gate. deplaned the passengers and met with maintenance. maintenance ran some test and minimum equipment list system 2 of our pressurization system. we then carried on, boarded the passengers, made sure all paperwork in the logbook was correct and continued.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: GippsAero GA8 Captain reported the aircraft trim wheel was stiff and only allow movement in a limited range. The Captain returned to the departure airport and landed.
text: the incident took place at redacted. during the climb out after the initial takeoff, the trim wheel was very stiff and would only move within a limited range. i leveled off at 1000 feet heading west before i turned back towards the airport and made the appropriate call with tower. i also alerted base that i was returning to base. i landed without issue. i then taxied back to maintenance and shut down the plane.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: ERJ-145 flight crew reported wing anti ice failure while descending on downwind. Flight crew reported this failure is a recurring issue with this aircraft.
text: on descent into redacted while being vectored to the downwind for runway xx, we received a wing anti/ice fail". we were in imc with an oat of between 0 to 3 degrees celsius. i continued to fly the aircraft and i instructed the first officer to run the qrh, as he had stated he flew this aircraft last week and had the same issue. after selecting the ice detector override knob to "all" and i advanced the thrust, the caution went away for approximately 60 seconds. upon the caution's return we continued the next steps of the qrh and the i advocated to request priority handling. we quickly agreed as a crew and requested priority handling with redacted [tracon] approach control to allow us to receive priority in exiting icing conditions and so i could have the ability to request whatever i thought we needed to safely arrive in redacted, as well as having a failure of an aircraft system. the next qrh step required us to push out then push in the wing anti ice button. the caution disappeared for approximately 60 seconds before returning. at this point, i decided we couldn't rely on the indication and to run the qrh as though the message persists. we requested minimum vectoring altitude and a wider base to final from air traffic control to avoid icing conditions and remain within qrh limitations of 30 degrees of bank and 190 minimum airspeed for flaps 0 and 9 degrees. after transmitting this request the caution went away. we were on our final vector for final when it returned. we agreed that there was no ice accumulation to warrant the "ice accretion" steps and we continued with the approach. around this time, i had my first officer notify dispatch. due to the possibility of icing, i did not delay the approach and talk to the flight attendant, as we were already below 10, 000' and we were more focused on getting the aircraft on the ground.the airport did set up priority handling vehicles as a precaution, and the first officer gave them all pertinent information while i contacted maintenance.we landed without incident. my first officer did a walk around and noticed no visible signs of damage to the leading wing edges on his post flight inspection.honestly, maintenance should have had the captain write it up on the date when my first officer had this issue the last time and we wouldn't have had an issue on this day.it sounded like, from the first officer's recollection, this aircraft had this issue before with the same aircraft in moderate icing. when his captain called maintenance after the flight, maintenance convinced him one way or another to not write the airplane up. when i called maintenance, they said i didn't have enough pressure and even though the temperature shows in the green on the environmental control system, page, it doesn't mean there's enough pressure. i understand this concept, but i was flaps 9 doing 240kts. i've never had an anti ice fail in this situation, and i even tried having the spoilers open to see if that would give it enough pressure with the advanced thrust setting which did not seem to help."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe
synopsis: Air carrier Technician reported that while closing the right-hand engine thrust reverser on a B737 MAX 8; they noticed a noise as the half was coming down and found the aft latches had bent at the top of the limiter assembly.
text: while closing the right hand engine #2 thrust reverser half we noticed a noise as the half was coming down. the t/r (thrust reverser) half was then opened to assess the cause of the noise, and we found that the rh limiter assembly that connects to the aft t/r latches had bent at the top of the limiter assy.i've been told by other technicians that this has happened before and that we have replaced many of these limiter assemblies due to this issue. if we could put this as a warning in the amm (aircraft maintenance manual) or bring awareness to this problem in the form of training that may help. an alteration to the design of the limiter assembly and its connected components might also help to mitigate future problems with closing the thrust reverser halves.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported turning to an assigned ATC heading during the climb on departure from GEU and then receiving a low altitude warning from ATC. The pilot received a revised heading and altitude and completed the flight to the destination.
text: incident was with geu from xa:35 till xb:15….phx departure about xb:15 to xb:50.flight was from glendale to redacted geu to redacted when i called for clearance there were at least seven aircraft already lined up for takeoff. he stated it would be a while for the clearance. i stated i had no place to go and asked and got taxi clearance. time from taxi to take off was at least 30 minutes. during this time there was only one controller working ground and tower, including doing the clearances. many people that called inbound were told to remain clear of the class delta and orbit. aircraft continued to land and aircraft departed slowly. as i neared the end of the runway, i was given my clearance. it was cleared to redacted, mrbil, yotes redacted [vor], maintain 3000 expect 10, 000 3 minutes after, i was given a squawk code and departure frequency. i do not remember if a heading for takeoff was given at that time or not. i think not. when cleared for takeoff i was given and i heard turn to a heading of 035, i read back 035. on takeoff the controller commented about starting the turn and referenced a direction that i do not remember. i stated i would turn at the end of the runway. i did drift slightly to the right of runway on takeoff. he then changed me over to phx departure. i called in and stated the altitude i was leaving, the altitude i was climbing to and that i was on a heading of 035. the controller then stated that he had a low altitude warning to turn to a northwesterly heading and to climb immediately to 3000 feet. i complied and looked out the window and tried to determine where the terrain was. i also later looked at the chart to see if there was some tall structure that could cause the warning there was none. i continued to step climb on headings with the controller.i talked with phx approach. he never stated that any separation was lost with any other aircraft and while i was flying, i did not ever see on adsb or visually any other traffic. i did state that i wanted the tapes at geu tower. he stated he could not do that. i said you can't get the tapes at geu, he said he couldn't. i said i should call geu and he said i would have to file some special govt paperwork request to get them. i of course wanted the tapes to verify what heading the tower had told me to fly. he then asked why i turned to the heading that i did. i said because that is the heading the tower gave me. basically, he was not going to do anything to get the tapes at geu tower. i also stated that this had been my first time instrument flight rules out of geu, that i had never gotten clearance to the north on an instrument flight rules departure and that i had never departed even visual flight rules to the north. i stated if i had, i may had recognized if this was not a typical heading. i had nothing to compare it with any other departure, if it may have been an incorrect heading. i also stated that when the geu controller had been worried about which direction i was going at the end of the runway, it would have been more helpful to hear from the controller something like 'verify turning to heading such and such. this would have given a better check to the assigned heading.i stated that i had been startled when the controller gave the low altitude alert, he stated so was the controller. i asked where the terrain was? he stated that it most likely broke a mva. he started to explain how a controller had to open an area for a heading if it is to be used. while phx area is hilly, in the immediate area the terrain was flat. as i said before i looked at the charts closely later and did not see any high structures.other circumstances: glendale is a very busy airport with traffic. it is tightly confined with luke airport to the west, phx class bravo to the east and goodyear to the south. it is a very irregular shaped class delta. there was only one controller working clearance, ground, tower. he was saturated. i heard the controller give another instrument flight rules clearance shortly after i got mine and before my takeoff. during this time, hecleared an aircraft to my same destination, redacted. i am like is someone else going there. i listened a bit more and the aircraft was doing training and not going to redacted and the clearance was corrected. i recognized the controller's voice. he creates a bit of a hostile environment on the radio. he likes to correct pilot errors, but when he makes an error he just moves on and doesn't say anything or apologizes for it. i have spoken to other pilots on the field. they all agree he is difficult to work with. you never know what kind of mood he is in.finally, if i turned to the wrong heading, i will take responsibility for that. however, if the tower gave me the wrong heading, i would like to get the answer. i got the feeling that phx departure and the supervisor on the phone call wanted me on a 350 heading. did the controller or i mix up the numbers. did the relay from phx departure give tower the wrong heading or is there a standard heading that is always given for that area of departure. i don't know, but it seems nobody wants me to hear the geu tower tapes

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: PA 27 instructor and student reported a hydraulic system issue while in the traffic pattern; which resulted in a landing gear and flap malfunction. The pilots completed the alternate landing gear procedure and landed safely.
text: smelled a strong hydraulic fluid in cockpit after gear retraction on 2nd takeoff. smell went away after one lap, we thought it was a factory causing the smell. 3 more laps in the pattern occurred with no incident. on the 5th lap, landing gear did not come up or down when moving the gear handle in either position. did a low pass, gear appeared to be down per redacted tower. then selected gear down, followed the emergency gear extension procedure in the poh. gear came down after 45-50 pumps. landed without flaps due to flaps also being hydraulic.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: A Citation First Officer reported descent below glidepath on initial approach and a Low Altitude Alert from ATC.
text: flight was normal and vectors to instrument landing system xxl was programmed into the flight management system as usual. the flight was vectored to final and intercepted the final approach course. the crew was advised to maintain 3000 until redacted which is 9 miles from the xxl threshold. normally the proline 21 avionics automatically switches from long range nav (pink needles) to short range (green needles), but for some reason this did not occur when expected. because vectors to final was selected, only redacted(point prior to the faf) and subsequent fixes were displayed on the moving map. the flight management system generated glidepath came down and the captain asked why the autopilot did not intercept the glidepath. he then initiated a descent to capture the glidepath. shortly after, the tower called with a low altitude warning and a go around was initiated. we were vectored around for another approach and landing which was uneventful. i as the non-flying pilot knew something was wrong but could not determine what was causing my confusion. both pilots lost situational awareness regarding our exact position ultimately as a result of selecting vectors to final.neither pilot referred to the moving map display on their ipads and neither pilot looked at the standby horizontal situation indicator which was presenting instrument landing system information. even more importantly, dme position was not compared to the approach chart.there were several lessons learned from this experience. always program the full approach so that all points on the approach will be displayed on the map. don't depend on cockpit automation. manually select short range nav if this information is needed before automatic switching occurs.always use any available information to ascertain position. bottom line, get back to the basics and listen to that uneasy feeling. don't continue a bad approach.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: General aviation instructor reported a near miss with another aircraft; when the other aircraft entered the runway and departed; while the instructor's aircraft was on final approach at MKT; a non-towered airport.
text: on day 0 at approximately xa:30, ip person a and student person b were inbound to land at mankato (mkt) from a flight lesson in redacted, flying in aircraft x. runway 33 was the active, and we had entered the pattern via a midfield cross. flying the pattern was uneventful until the final leg.as we turned on final, my student made a radio call stating our position. we had traffic in sight (aircraft y) that was holding short of runway 33. it was a calm and clear day so our groundspeed was probably around 70-80 kts. we heard aircraft y make a call stating that they were departing on runway 33. in my mind i thought 'wow that's cutting it close but they could probably make it', but then, i didn't see the aircraft roll across the hold short line after making their departure call. i then thought 'maybe they just now saw us on final and are waiting for us to land', but i still maintained vigilance that they might depart anyways. right after i had that thought, they rolled past the threshold line onto the runway for takeoff. by that time we were less than a mile on final. i had person b stay on the controls and fly the plane while i watched the traffic outside. we saw them start their roll, but determined we would not be able to land safely without creating an incursion, so we executed a go around. we side-stepped to ther right to avoid catching up to or overflying the departure traffic, but could only side-step so much as there was other traffic on the upwind leg of the pattern (mankato has an upwind leg for traffic sequencing reasons). at one point we were only separated by 100 feet, and i could no longer maintain visual contact with aircraft y due to our nose-up attitude for the go around and our spacing being so close. i'm not sure what our altitude was when we executed the go-around, as i was keeping my eyes outside watching for traffic.as soon as it was safe to do so, my student and i opted to break out of the pattern rather than turning crossdwind in order to recollect and re-assess the situation. when we landed, we each submitted a safety report. we also discussed the situation and determined that we had the right of way. we agreed that something we could have done better was make the go around decision sooner, which would have provided better spacing.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Ground Incursion Taxiway
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported some SFO taxiway markings and signage were unclear and faded.
text: while operating a part 135 charter flight in aircraft x at sfo, we were instructed to taxi from the ramp to runway 1r. ground control issued progressive taxi instructions, however, due to frequency congestion and perceived pressure from the controller to expedite movement, the taxi clearance was delivered rapidly.the airport surface environment at sfo is complex, with numerous closely spaced and angled intersections. taxiway markings in the area appeared faded and were difficult to distinguish, particularly at high-workload intersections. signage and painted surface identifiers did not provide clear situational awareness in the moment.while attempting to comply promptly with air traffic control instructions and maintain flow, we inadvertently taxied onto the incorrect taxiway at one of the intersections. the error was recognized shortly thereafter through cross-checking the airport diagram and outside visual cues. we immediately corrected course and notified ground control. no loss of separation or runway incursion occurred.contributing factors included: complex taxiway layout at sfo. faded or unclear taxiway markings. high workload during taxi phase. congested frequency. perceived air traffic control pressure to expedite. time pressure associated with part 135 operations. crew resource management was utilized to identify and correct the deviation promptly. after recognizing uncertainty, we slowed the aircraft and verified position using the airport diagram before proceeding.human factors: time pressure. communication workload. expectation bias. reduced situational awareness due to environmental complexity.corrective actions / recommendations: when operating at complex airports such as sfo, request progressive taxi instructions early and advise air traffic control if unable to comply promptly. reduce taxi speed in high-density ramp and intersection areas. if any uncertainty exists, stop the aircraft and clarify position before proceeding. airport authority should evaluate taxiway marking visibility and signage clarity in the departure areas.

anomaly: Inflight Event / Encounter Object
synopsis: Government UAS pilot reported the UAS flew into trees during its RTH.
text: flying for government law enforcement agency on an operation and underestimated the return home time. the drone self-landed into some trees. no property damages and no injuries resulting from the crash.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: A Tower Controller reported they observed the TRACON Departure Controller turn a departing aircraft to a heading which caused a confliction with a subsequent departure.
text: aircraft x, a c172, was on an approach to runway xx at redacted. the radar controller assigned a climbout of runway heading for aircraft x. aircraft x was cleared for the option and executed a touch-and-go. once aircraft x was on the go i initiated a rundown for aircraft y, a c68a, on a heading of 170. the rundown was then acknowledged by the radar controller and i switched aircraft x to their frequency when aircraft x was about a half a mile off of the departure end of runway xx. i observed on the radar scope that aircraft x appeared to be drifting a couple of degrees slightly east of the runway heading that he was assigned, possibly due to wind. as a result, i called down to the radar controller on the recorded shout line with an approval request for a 150 heading for aircraft y to ensure more separation between aircraft y and aircraft x. the radar controller then said that he was going to 'crank aircraft x on a 090' heading. this did not make sense to me as a 090 would create even more of a conflict with aircraft y who was already on a 170. thus, i reiterated my approval request of a 150 heading for aircraft y and the radar controller replied 'approved.' i then switched aircraft y to the radar controller about a half mile off of the departure end of runway xx on a 150 heading. after both aircraft were switched to the radar controller's frequency i observed aircraft x, who was at this point about 2 miles south of the runway, turn directly towards aircraft y with targets appearing likely to merge at co-altitude. ultimately, a 170 heading was coordinated in the rundown for aircraft y and another more eastbound heading of 150 was coordinated and approved by the radar controller. the radar controller decided to turn aircraft x directly towards aircraft y creating a near mid air collision. lastly, i think that it is worth noting that the radar controller is a supervisor who is certified only in one position in the facility and received that certification with zero recommendations from a cpc in the building. i would like to recommend that all those in training whether they are developmentals or supervisors be required to receive a recommendation from a cpc before they are considered for certification.
