anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: C172 pilot reported a loss of power after takeoff while on crosswind leg of the pattern. Power was restored during return to a landing on the reciprocal runway.
text: momentary engine failure on crosswind turn of visual flight rules tower pattern. occurred at approximately 800' agl. once recognized, immediately performed a teardrop turn back towards the reciprocal runway, then requested priority handling and relayed intentions. no other aircraft in the pattern/active on airfield, immediately cleared to land. about halfway through descent to runway, engine restarted. performed a normal flaps 40 landing. taxied under own power back to parking.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT; Inflight Event / Encounter Object; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported main rotor blade contact with tree top on descent that resulted in rotor blade damage.
text: day 0 i was to perform a confined are landing in a field near the redacted airport and prior to the landing i did a site survey, walked off the the area from the tree line for rotor clearance on the left side and the front of the helicopter to ensure that i had rotor clearance on my blind side before doing the first landing. the tail section was clear of any obstacles and was not blocked. the tree line on my left side was my primary concern. i made a reference mark on the ground to place my right wheel. the video shot was to hover over the confined landing area and hold in a hover at approximately 100ft (agl) and then descend vertically slowly to the target area mark for the right wheel. the winds were typical winds variable from the northeast at about 15kts with occasional gust to 25kts. sky was clear and visibility was unlimited and no other aircraft was flying during this time. at approximately xa:15 i did the first landing without any problems, but from the inside the cockpit the pilots view from the right side looked closer than i was comfortable with, and decided to place my wheel chocks further to my right to provide more rotor clearance on my left blind side. the plan was still the same, lift straight up to 100ft(agl)and hold for several minutes then descend vertically slowly to the wheel chock marker that we had moved to the right about 15 more feet. during the second second landing as i was slowly descending is when i heard heard the sound of the rotor blade tip caps hitting the tree branches, i immediately raised collective and moved farther away to my right before landing.contributing factors:(1) strong left gusty cross winds, and pilot not accounting for the leaning angle of the helicopter that changed the pilots visual reference to the landing marker, and in order for the pilot to see it he drifted to the left and had the rotor over the tree tops as he slowly descended, causing damaged to the tip caps. (2) not having a safety ground crew person on the landing aera that would have better outside visual observations and a hand held radio to communicate with the pilot on rotor clearance, and to make corrections as needed. (3) customer pressure pushing to get the job done in one shot. (4) customer changed plan at the last minute from original location discussed a week prior to this new location causing the scope of work to change and making the crew become complacent in just trying to get the job done before dark.action taken: what seemed to be a simple photo / video shoot became very complex with all of the last minute changes, and the should have been stopped, regroup with better weather conditions and a very clear plan for all involved with distances actually measured and verified by another person with an actual measuring device and not just walked off by the pilot. my stride was most likely shorter than usual from being distracted by the camera person and putting me closer to the tree line than expected. preventative measures: a written plane of action and tail board meeting will be conducted for all persons involved with more clearer directions besides the standard safety briefing, and other concerns such as the effects of weather, visibility, winds, rain, dust, obstacles will be addressed, discussed and documented with a collection of signatures. the physical distance from the tree line and gusty winds was the contributing factor on this incident.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: Pilot reported WDR airport has many items that need attention and repair.
text: this is a general report on the overall safety and lack of basic upkeep at the wdr airport. we've for years had subpar equipment that has been tolerated and has been a contributing factor in past incidents that could have been fatal. it is a matter of time before there is an incident on field that could have been avoided.1) no wind reporting capabilities. the awos has been inoperative almost an entire year. before that it reported winds unreliable" for years, but at least it was something. it's shielded by trees in a bad location. suggest if there is ever a new one installed it is moved to another location. we often have 3 or even 4 aircraft on all runways making simultaneous approaches due to this lack of basic information that is critical to making an educated decision on which runway to use. especially dangerous at night when the glitchy lighting (will get to that soon) doesn't illuminate the wind sock and pilots are flying on hope on windy nights.2) runway lighting. half the runway and taxi lights do not work. obviously dangerous at night during surface movement. runway lights only work at max brightness, which washes out the pilot's ability to see the pavement. no way for pilots to adjust. an extreme black hole effect is created in the round out. results in hard landings more often than not from discussions with fellow pilots. taxiway signs and runway signs have burned out, making runway incursions prevalent. the runway lights also pulsate. all these lighting issues have been reported to airport authorities with no resolution. the papis do not work. we have obstacles that are unlit on the approach ends of 3 of the 4 runways and having no visual glide slope indicator (vgsi) combined with max brightness runway lights that affect vision is a disaster waiting to happen.3) pavement/runway markings are not visible. pressure washing or painting is long overdue. every stripe or number in the touchdown zones are nearly black as opposed to white. added to all the other issues, users of the airport are really being set up for failure and no one is listening. i'm fearful that someone will have a catastrophic accident before something is done."

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air traffic controller reported issuing a clearance to an aircraft and the aircraft turned early resulting in flight towards terrain; the controller issued an alert and climb to the aircraft. When at a safe altitude the controller turned the aircraft back on course.
text: i issued a clearance from redacted via flight data to aircraft x who had filed direct at 050. i issued the clearance at 070 for terrain. when the flight departed, they departed rwyxx with a left turn direct and did not intercept their route line from redacted to their destination but instead proceeded direct. this placed them about 1-2 miles south of the planned route and into a 090 minimum instrument flight rules altitude (mia). the aircraft was still climbing, about 065, when reaching the 090 mia so i couldn't issue any course guidance below the 070 box. i issued a low altitude alert, the aircraft began to climb to 090 and was in the 090 mia around 070 for about 2 miles. after they exited the 090 i issued 070 as their altitude. this airspace is normally owned by an redacted [tracon] approach control and i'm not sure i've ever worked this route at the bottom of my mias. i should have queried which runway the aircraft was going to use in order to anticipate this event.alternatively i could've issue routing of redacted redacted [vor] in order to ensure their flight on the planned route as redacted and redacted [vor] are co-located. the blanket safer thing would've been to issue 090 in the original clearance to ensure safety and given 070 when able during the flight after climb out.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: B767 flight crew reported a compressor stall on application of power that resulted in a rejected takeoff.
text: we were taking off on xxr in redacted. winds were 220@25g33. i was pilot flying. cleared for takeoff, i let the engines slowly spool up for a few seconds and asked for auto throttles. the auto throttles came up, i said check thrust and took my hand off the auto throttles. the captain now was in control of the throttles. the throttles were not even fully at our take off setting, we had slowly started moving and heard a very loud bang and i felt the aircraft shake violently momentarily. immediately the captain rejected the takeoff. all our engine indications were showing normal, we taxied off the runway to a secure spot and had crash fire rescue take a look at our aircraft before returning to the gate.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Speed All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: B737 First Officer reported that an auto throttle and flight director malfunction resulted in airspace speed exceedance
text: just after takeoff, in light rime icing and imc, i noticed we weren't climbing. we were at 2400 or so msl and flaps/gear up, shortly after the after takeoff checklist was completed. it took me a minute to notice that we were right at clean maneuvering speed and not climbing because of focus elsewhere on multiple calls from air traffic control with climb and vector instructions. the ca was hand flying the aircraft during this entire event.after we both managed to get situational awareness, i noticed the auto throttles had moved back to around 54% n1, which would explain the lack of a climb. the ca disengaged the auto throttles and we manually set the appropriate climb n1. at this point, the aircraft resumed climbing and the bug jumped to 250 knots at the appropriate altitude. however, upon acceleration, the fd (flight director) began commanding an erroneous pitch attitude. while still hand flying, the captain followed the fd momentarily until quickly realizing following it would cause us to exceed the flight management system speed of 250 knots. because of this, we momentarily accelerated to around 270 knots (around 7-8000 msl) until catching that the vnav function was commanding an incorrect airspeed. the ca quickly returned to 250 knots then disregarded the fd vertical guidance until we got well above 10, 000 msl. when we got higher and above the bad weather, we tried to reengage the auto throttle, but it started retarding the throttles again like it did earlier. ultimately, we reset both flight directors and the auto throttle, which restored normal function to both systems. at that time, we engaged autopilot and the rest of the flight proceeded normally. air traffic control did not contact us about our momentary speed exceedance. during this entire event, lnav guidance worked normally, so whatever the issue was ended up being isolated to the vnav vertical guidance and the auto throttles.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance
synopsis: B737 Captain reported that when they descended below their assigned altitude; they noticed a stabilizer out of trim warning and diverted to a nearby airport.
text: at cruise with autopilot and autothrottle engaged, i noticed the aircraft slowly descending 300 feet below target altitude. i pointed this to the first officer (flying pilot). the aircraft slowly started to climb back to target altitude. i then noticed the stab out of trim caution light on. i performed the stab out of trim (max) non-normal checklist. we coordinated with air traffic control to descend below rvsm airspace due to autopilot and autothrottles being turned off as instructed from the non-normal checklist. i contacted dispatch and coordinated to divert to redacted. the flight attendants were briefed on the situation and an announcement to the passengers - informing them of the situation and the divert to redacted was also completed. we landed at redacted without incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance
synopsis: B737 Captain reported EGT limits were exceeded during climb.
text: on climb out, it became evident that the number 2 engine egt was in the yellow with a peak egt observed at 928 and holding with the a/t (autothrottle) on. it never got to the red line. no other indications other than the egt gauge were observed. we disconnected the a/t, brought the thrust lever back, and into normal range. attempted to reconnect the a/t, and the egt on the number 2 engine quickly rose again into the yellow caution range. disconnected again, leveled at 10, 000', and arranged for holding on the approach for rnav xxl for a return to redacted. called ops in redacted and told mx (maintenance) and them that we are returning to redacted. called dispatch and maintenance control, who confirmed the spike and our decision to return to redacted. flew the approach with no problem with the a/t off. overweight landing was normal, taxied to the gate, and performed an aircraft swap.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the landing gear didn't retract which resulted in a return to the departure airport.
text: takeoff climb out of redacted gear didn't retract. all red and all green gear lights on. went to checklist. manual gear extension door was checked and it looked flush and locked down. ended up opening door and trying to close it to make sure it was down. tried this 3 times. gear would not retract. decided to return to redacted. requested priority handling as we were landing overweight. normal landing and taxi to gate

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported being informed that the de-icing procedures at BWI were inadequate and rushed and the flight crew requested another de-icing company to take over the process.
text: we were deiced by company x operations in baltimore. the entire process seemed inadequate and rushed. when company x operations was completed with their deicing, they simply said we were complete. when asked for the information, they only gave us the type and concentration. when asked for more information regarding start and stop times they didn't know. it was at that point, company y called the operations frequency and told us to call them. the company y supervisor then relayed to us in the interest of safety he had to report to us the inadequacies he saw take place." he then listed off entire critical surfaces to us that either were not even sprayed or inadequately sprayed. at that point, we went to the chief pilot and requested company y take over the deicing operation. it was done correctly. it was heavy snow to moderate snow at the time. this entire event was safety critical, and the outcome could have been disastrous had we not been told of our own operations' lax attitude toward deicing the aircraft."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 Captain reported a flap malfunction on final approach which resulted in a go around followed by a safe landing.
text: on approach to runway xx, flap handle was set to 30 and the flap position indicators did not move. a go around was conducted and air traffic control was advised. the checklist was run and a flap 15 landing was prepared for. dispatch, fas, and pax (passengers) were notified. fas were given a briefing. airport fire rescue was coordinated to meet us once we vacated the runway to do a visual check of the aircraft. we were vectored around to xyl. uneventful landing, inspection, and taxi to gate followed.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported a NMAC with a helicopter while on approach.
text: on approach into redacted for visual backed up with instrument landing system xxl, i was alerted to conversation between redacted tower and a helicopter who just departed redacted. the instructions for the helicopter were very open and ambiguous. around 1, 000 ft, i noticed on tcas traffic and an advisory pop up for the helicopter at our altitude and very close proximity. the traffic was heading parallel our course and i had a visual on him pass just off our right wing at our current altitude. i would call this a near mid-air miss.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Ground Event / Encounter Other / Unknown; Ground Incursion Ramp
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the lead-in line was confusing and hard to see during night time operations and inadvertently followed the wrong line before correcting back to the correct line.
text: upon entry to ramp from ek taxiway, entering spot 23 the lead-in line for taxiway ek ends suddenly and the new lead-in line for spot 23 is about 10 feet to the left. during night time operations, it is hard to see the new lead-in line and following the taxi line markings can lead to improper aircraft positioning due to its sudden ending. the transition from ek taxi line to spot 23 does not have a (in my opinion) sufficient marking for night time/low visibility operations.cause: night time operations mixed with taxiway lines being obscured and hard to maneuver with construction nearby. thankfully we mitigated this by having two heads up in the hotspot" and by taxiing in at a slow speed."

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A B787 flight crew reported temporary loss of control at the beginning of takeoff roll related to different engine spool-up rates resulting in a rejected take off.
text: aircraft x was a ferry flight from redacted to redacted. it was the second ferry flight of the day. ca and first officer were only crew onboard. from preflight, we had issues getting the actual fuel load on the jet updated by dispatch onto performance data and flight plan. taxiing out we exceeded our edct (estimated departure clearance time), because of delays in receiving a load close out. once we were ready, we were cleared for takeoff on runway xx and advised of arrival traffic. halfway through turn from taxiway to centerline of xx, tower advised traffic was short final. as ca lined up on centerline, he called toga. aircraft then veered hard right as engines spooled up. between 30 and 40 knots, ca initiated a rejected to: throttles idle, manual braking to a stop. after full stop, we exited at 1 to the south of runway xx to evaluate. on taxiway 2, we discussed the parameters of the reject, including no 'thrust set' call or rto (rejected takeoff) braking, and brake temperatures. we determined that asymmetric thrust during right turn onto runway led to asymmetric thrust during engine advancement to to. we decided to attempted a second static takeoff. second to from runway xyl was normal and uneventful. flight concluded safely at redacted.cause: minor coordination delays and then traffic calls from tower added to feeling of 'hurry up'. while we did discuss mental status, ie 'being in the green', this is a reminder at each break point in taxi/flight to take a deep breath and focus on the next event.closer evaluation of throttle advancement to approximately 40 percent n1 and prioritize static takeoff, especially from maintenance base.avoid using asymmetric thrust entering runway for takeoff.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: A321 First Officer reported they failed to notice damage to the engine nacelle during the preflight check.
text: on day 0, i was the first officer for redacted- redacted. i arrived at the airplane at about xa:20am, having taken the xa:00 am van from the hotel. after arriving at the airplane and putting my bags in the flight deck, i accomplished an origination flow, with the exception of first flight of the day items and went outside to do an exterior inspection. i completed the inspection, following the recommended inspection route, and i did not notice any damage. i returned to the flight deck, and completed first flight of the day items, having ensured that wheel chocks were in place. the captain arrived shortly thereafter, and the flight proceeded normally without incident or any abnormal indications. on day 2, i received a voice mail from person a asking me to call him back. when i did, he let me know that there was damage found on the #2 engine nacelle by the crew who was working the outbound leg after our arrival in redacted. he also shared that he or someone reporting to him had looked back at the camera data in redacted, and found evidence that the damage was present on the ramp at redacted. he shared pictures of the damage with me by text.cause: causal factors include my failure to recognize the damage to the #2 engine nacelle. my recency of flight may have played a role, as this was my third day back on the line after 3 months of schoolhouse work as an ip (flight instructor). during the whole trip i was mindful to arrive early to each flight and give myself plenty of time to complete my duties as i knew it had been more than 3 months since i had flown the line. i went into this trip being especially mindful that i had not been around an airplane for a while, and tried especially hard to take my time and make sure that i wasn't missing anything. during the exterior inspections, i must not have looked closely enough at the aft part of the nacelle before i walked the right wing leading edge. i must have only been looking up as i inspected the leading edge and trailing edge, before walking behind the engine to inspect the right side landing gear and fuselage. i imagine that i walked right by the damage without ever seeing it on the aft portion of the nacelle while i was looking up to inspect the right wing trailing edge. my recommendation would be simply to be even more deliberate and observant during exterior inspections, and to carefully inspect the entirety of the engine nacelle and fuselage skin for damage on all sides.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the hold short line for Runway 12 at MKJP; Norman Manley International Airport; is much further from the approach end of the runway than what is typical and recommends a note be added to the charts.
text: pushed off of the gate and started both engines as normal. after engine start we accomplished all appropriate flows and checklist. we did a brief before leaving the ramp area and called for taxi and was given taxi to holding point runway 12 via taxiway a." we left the ramp area and did the before takeoff checklist and the flight attendants prepared for takeoff. upon the taxi out i remember the captain saying that the hold short line was pretty far back and stopped before crossing the line and i saw the line in front of us. at no point did i think we crossed the line. after holding short we were then given takeoff clearance for runway 12 without any issues or query from the tower. flight was accomplished normally no issues.put a note in company pages about the hold short line being very far from the runway."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: ERJ175 Captain reported misapplication of parking brake resulted in uncommanded aircraft movement.
text: after parking at the gate, i remember trying to set the parking brake. when i looked outside i noticed the airplane moving forward slowly and immediately set the brakes. i realized the parking brake was not set. i talked with the ramper, who said that everything was fine and nobody was hit or hurt.cause: this was caused by my failure to verify that the parking brake handle was fully engaged in the on position and that the indicator light was on. distraction may have been a contributing factor at the time of setting the parking brake immediately after stopping at the gate. the marshaller made an x with his wands very suddenly, resulting in my stepping on the brakes very quickly, causing the aircraft to come to an abrupt halt. i remember this upset me a bit, which may have taken me off gaurd as i usually try to come to a smooth stop for everyone's comfort. suggestions: in the future, i will prioritize setting the parking brake after parking and will make a habit of always looking at the parking brake indicator light everytime i move the brake handle.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: ERJ 145 First Officer reported that they were issued go around instructions due to a departing aircraft on the runway.
text: we were doing a visual approach to runway xx and when we were between 3nm to 2.5nm from the runway redacted gives clearance to aircraft y to depart from runway xx. they are not even lined up in the runway. they are a couple feet from the hold short line. air traffic control told them to expedite departure when given the clearance but aircraft y did not. we knew we need to do a go around because there's simply no way they were going to take off on time. i was hand flying from 1, 000ft agl approximately, and upon reaching 200ft agl air traffic control called the go around. we executed the expected go around with no problems.cause: better air traffic control preparation and commands.suggestions: i suggest that if a takeoff clearance will be given to jet and another jet is landing, and there's 3-2.5nm of distance between the landing traffic and the runway, at least air traffic control needs to have the takeoff plane in line up and wait. giving a clearance that tight, is not necessary for the possible outcome, even though takeoff plane was told to expedite, which in this case they did not do so

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: EMB170 Captain reported multiple system caution indications; along with lack of nose wheel steering resulted in expeditious handling to a safe landing.
text: first officer leg, at cruise, fl230, somewhere abeam redacted we received three simultaneous cautions: hyd 2 low press, ads 1 fail, and ap fail. my first officer is now hand flying, and i'm grabbing the qrh for the hydraulic issue (top message). by the time i'm at the hydraulic section, the hyd 2 message has disappeared, so i move to the ads 1 fail message. it basically says to make sure the ads has reverted, which it did. next, ap (autopilot) fail... we tried unsuccessfully to re-engage the ap so no cat ii approaches. redacted is visual flight rules. now, out of curiosity, i circle back and check the hyd page to see what's going on there. that's when i see amber dashes for the hyd sys 2 pressure (see attached ). after a discussion with my first officer, we decide it would be best to treat this as if sys 2 has no pressure. first, we don't know if there is any pressure (we have a qty indication) the flow lines are showing green. it could be a faulty pressure sensor, but we can't rule out a faulty warning system because we initially got the warning, and then it disappeared. we didn't want to assume everything was fine and find out on the ground that we were wrong, so we went with the hyd sys 2 low press procedure anyway. then we got a hyd 2 elec pump fail message (see attached). then we were led to the loss of hydraulic system 2 procedure and advising air traffic control. i gave the fas the information but i forgot to make the announcement to the passengers as we were on the arrival, and pretty busy with the qrh. somewhere on the approach, after we got through the loss of hydraulic system 2 descent checklist, i took the controls. the gear extended normally, normal landing on xxr with what felt like normal braking, but as we slowed on the roll out i found that i had no steering. i exited the high speed and came to stop on the taxiway. i gave the passengers a brief explanation of what was going on, that we were going to be towed to the gate, and it could take some time for the tug to get out to us. our eicas was now full of more messages and remote cb trip that, i guess, had been inhibited in flight (see attached). we had multiple conversations with cfr (crash fire rescue), ground, and ops and eventually got towed to the gate.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Fuel Issue
synopsis: A321 pilot reported experiencing a fuel transfer issue during cruse flight resulting in the flight crew returning to the departure airport.
text: we were operating redacted to redacted, everything was normal through the first hour. in cruise passing redacted at fl320, we got the fuel act xfr fault ecam message. we ran the ecam, and in doing so we were able to open the transfer valve. however, only the number 2 act was able to be emptied into the center tank. the number 1 tank still about 5500 pounds of fuel that wouldn't transfer. after the second tank was empty, we then got the fuel act unusable ecam since we couldn't get the fuel to transfer. we couldn't make it to redacted with this situation. i called maintenance through dispatch on the satcom and we formulated the plan that it was in the best interest to air return to redacted. once we made the turn, we were going to be about 8500 pounds overweight for landing. we dropped lower in altitude during the return to minimize that number as much as we could till we could get back to the coast. a hold was asked for to burn enough to be able to land underweight. we held over city x for about 37-40 mins before making our way to redacted and landing a few hundred pounds underweight. we went to the gate and a logbook entry was made.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: ERJ 170 flight crew conducting a Visual Approach reported they received a Low Altitude Alert from ATC while on base leg.
text: coming into redacted on a visual approach for runway xx i was the pm and first officer was the pf. on the base leg as we were about to turn final air traffic control gave us a low altitude alert as we were about to level off at faf alt. we both immediately cross checked the altitude and verified we had the airport still insight which we did and as a result we decided to continue the approach which concluded in a normal landing. the only information air traffic control provided was that it might've given him the alert because of our descent rate on our final descent from 4000 to 2100 ft. i believe we were at or just below 2000fpm during that final descent.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A330 First Officer reported a hydraulic failure at cruise altitude. Flight continued to the destination and landed safely.
text: green hyd sys leak. experienced just prior to crossing over the coast bound to redacted. completed applicable ecam. i was ro (relief officer) for this trip and happened to be pf at the time of the ecam caution message. contacted dispatch, maintenance control and fodo (duty officer) to coordinate and assess. continued to destination, manual landing gear extension, instrument landing system xxl redacted. full stop and towed to get from runway. no safety issues. the company process worked as intended.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Crossing Restriction Not Met; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: B737 Captain reported descending below the crossing restriction on approach that resulted in flight towards terrain and ATC issuing a low altitude alert. The flight crew corrected their altitude and landed safely.
text: we were on the redacted arrival. air traffic control instructed, 'slow to 210 then descend to 6000 feet. i switched to vertical speed to slow, set flaps 2, then engaged level change to get back on profile as slowing down had gotten us high. air traffic control cleared us for the rnav z xx. i called to set touchdown zone elevation without reselecting vnav. the aircraft continued to descend below the 3700' limit on the arc of the approach. air traffic control called, 'altitude alert. aircraft x check your altitude immediately'. we realized what had happened and repaired the error. air traffic control cleared us for the visual and turned us over to tower. we landed uneventfully.
