synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving an ATC low altitude alert while on approach.
text: while flying the dca river visual approach, as we became aware of being approximately 100 feet low near key bridge, we also received a low altitude alert from dca tower. we were already beginning to correct by leveling off. we were visual, with the runway in sight. the rest of the approach and landing were uneventful. earlier in the approach we were slightly higher than desired so the rate of descent had been increased to 1, 000 fpm.selecting a steeper descent rate than needed so as to correct quickly to desired glide slope resulted in momentarily being lower than desired.when correcting from being slightly high, use a slightly greater rate of descent versus a large descent rate to avoid possibly becoming lower than desired.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A321 Captain reported an engine bleed air fault ECAM message on climb. Crew diverted for normal approach and landing.
text: shortly after departure on the climb out of redacted we got a ecam message for a eng 1 bleed fault. we complied with the ecam procedure. since the problem was bleed related we stopped the climb at 12, 000ft to assess the situation. we contacted dispatch on the sat phone and were patched in with the duty officer and maintenance. a reset attempt led by maintenance was unsuccessful. it was determined that the problem could not be rectified in the air. we went over the situation with everyone on the call, weighed our options and the first officer and myself felt the safest course of action was to return. we finished remaining checklist/procedures and diverted for a normal approach and landing.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported smoke in the cabin and flight deck.
text: this was the last leg of a 4-day trip. boarding was normal. we were completely full plus a company x pilot in the cockpit jumpseat. we were cleared for takeoff full length on runway xxl at approximately xa:06 utc. we were cleared on the zzzzzx rnav departure out of redacted. takeoff was normal. we were instructed to contact redacted departure at approximately 1000 ft agl. i checked in with redacted departure, the controller instructed us to climb to 5, 000 ft. as i was replying to that instruction i received a call from the cabin. i answered the call and the purser alerted me that they may have a fire in the cabin. the forward galley was filing with smoke and it appeared that it was coming out of one of the ovens in the forward galley. i told the captain what was going on in the cabin. at that time we began smelling a strong acrid odor as well as seeing a haze of smoke in the cockpit. the captain, myself and the jumpseater all donned our oxygen masks and established crew communications. the captain told me that they wanted to return to redacted immediately. i alerted air traffic control that we would like to stop our climb at 5000 and we would probably be heading back to redacted. air traffic control gave us a 280 heading to put us on a downwind for runway xxl and began giving us a descent to 4000 feet. as we leveled at 4000 feet we received an off schedule descent light.i pulled the qrc down from the glare shield and looked at the immediate action items for smoke/fire/fumes. i saw that we had already accomplished the steps of donning our oxygen masks and establishing crew communications. i pulled out the qrh from my side of the pedestal and was about to go to the fire protection section as it was the next step from the qrc but was distracted by the purser calling up from the back. she confirmed that the smoke was coming from the oven. she told me that she didn't want to open the door of the oven. she was afraid that it would make it worse. she told me that she shut the ovens off but there was still a lot of smoke coming out. i instructed her to pull the circuit breakers for both ovens in the forward galley. we continued to receive transmissions from air traffic control. they wanted to know what the issue was, souls and fuel onboard. it was at this time that we received priority handling with air traffic control.at the captains direction, i began setting up the fmc for the instrument landing system xxl at redacted. i loaded the approach, set the instrument landing system frequencies and minimums. i also loaded vref and target speeds for landing. the purser called up front again. i answered and was told that the smoke was starting to dissipate. i told them we were heading back to redacted and we would be on the ground shortly. i told the captain that the smoke was dissipating in the back. we noticed that we did not have the acrid odor or smoke in the cockpit anymore either. we decided it was safe to remove our oxygen masks. we had some issues communicating with each other. i remembered to close the oxygen mask door and test it on my side to return the audio to normal. i failed to remind the captain of this and they continued to have some issues with communication that i wasn't aware of at the time. i pulled up the divert page on the acars portion of the fmc and told the captain that i was going to send a divert notice to dispatch. i glanced over the page briefly and thought that i pressed the send button. i later found out that dispatch didn't know about the divert. so i either didn't press the button hard enough or it didn't go through. i began going into the acars section to get landing data as i knew we were overweight landing back at redacted. i typed in 161.0 for our landing weight and xxl for the runway and pressed send. i didn't see until we were on short final that i received an error for our landing data. i believe that i didn't enter redacted as our landing airport. the landing data page defaulted to redacted for the landing airport and the error was because there isn't a xxl runway at redacted. at this point we were on downwind for xxl. the captain transferred the controls to me and they briefed the approach. i believe at this time the captain also made an announcement to the passengers. i transferred the controls back to the captain. air traffic control began turning us on a base leg and descending us further. the captain began to call for flaps and the gear down. we were given one more turn and then cleared for the instrument landing system xxl. i pulled out the checklist and accomplished the descent checklist and after we were fully configured for landing i accomplished the landing checklist. when we were on short final i received the error for the landing data. i showed it to the captain. i can't remember if the captain acknowledged it or not. the captain later told me that they felt we had plenty of runway for landing considering the headwind and dry runway conditions.the landing was normal and uneventful. we cleared the runway to the right at taxiway 1. there was arff (airport rescue and firefighting ) equipment that was waiting for us as we cleared the runway. they followed us to the gate. i spoke to them on the frequency at one point and they told me that they would be on the jet bridge as we pulled in to make sure the fire in the oven was contained. there was about a 5 minute delay holding short of the gate as we waited for a ramp crew to guide us in. parking and shutdown was normal. the captain called the fight attendants and instructed them to disarm the l1 door and allow the firefighter on the aircraft to look at the oven. we deplaned the passengers and our maintenance crew came out to look at the write-up for the smoke coming out of the oven as well as the overweight landing. maintenance determined that there was a lot of grease all over the top of the foil on many of the meals. they think that the grease dripping off of the foil on our takeoff roll and climb out caused the smoke event.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown; Ground Event / Encounter Person / Animal / Bird; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported difficulties with communications and SOP compliance with ramp personnel prior to push back.  Flight pushed.
text: be advised, the crew got to the aircraft and it was extremely hot. the station indicated that the jet bridge air was hooked up and turned on widebody. this will not help if the battery switch is off and no ground power is established on the aircraft. i got 2nd secondary screened and my luggage was run through the scanner twice and so by the time i got to the gate it was 5 minutes past board. the first officer halted boarding because it was too hot and we needed to cool the cabin off. they remarked the battery switch was off, no ground power and it was hot. they told the flight attendants that i would be down in a minute to assist. we were negative apu, no ground power, no battery on and maintenance deferred it that night, meaning they knew. obviously no communication at all at this station. i had the flight attendants open doors to start circulation and radio coordinated with ops (operations) and the ground handlers to get the air start air hooked up so i could cool off the cabin using the aircraft packs and begin loading. i performed the walk-around, the first officer handled the inside of the aircraft. i was met by an ops supervisor and i explained what i needed as we walked around the aircraft, i asked if he understood, he said yes. while downstairs under the aircraft i briefed the lead ground handler as well as the supervisor that we would require the air start cart for starting engine #1 on this aircraft. and cooling the aircraft. i went so far to walk over the lead and showed him on the air start cart the various switch positions, one for packs usage and one for engine start. i asked him if he understood, he said yes. i continued my walk around and noticed the lead hooked up the air start hose with a major kink in the hose. as they started air, the air cart relief valve kept popping air the air was blocked from entering the aircraft and the packs. (this will play out again) the lead untangled it slightly and the packs received air and were used for cooling. i got back upstairs, the purser thanked me for the help and remarked it was already cooling. i asked her to shut the open doors 1r and 2l and we began boarding at xa:40 for an xb:00 departure, not good. as we were loading up another ground handler asked if he could disconnect power several times, i called ops again requested that a supervisor intervene and talk to all the guys below the wing and i again explained to her (ops agent) that we have to leave the power connected, start #1 engine, disconnect the power and pull off the jetway. i told her to send a supervisor out to brief everyone again, i was falling behind in my duties.i used communication and coordinated with everyone in the operation and i received zero support from ops, leads, supervisors and baggage handlers and i repeated myself several times. we need to look at this incident and make adjustments. early flights are not just the flight crews responsibility, it's everyone's. as we attempted to start the #1 engine, the ground handler switch to engine start mode, we attempted an engine start and not enough air pressure, i told the guy in the head set that the engine will not start with a kink in the hose, he finally untangled it all the way, and we got the pressure we needed for an engine start.we pushed @ xb:12 and arrived to lax 5 minutes late after i bumped up the ci (cost index), and reported everything to dispatch. after departing aus and getting established in level flight i read up on gate notes at lax for gate xx and noted a larger than 90 degree turn to get aligned with gate from taxiway c. meaning both engines running to limit engine blast in the turn. i then contacted dispatch and ask if they would advise lax that we were coming with no apu and we would need ground power and an air start cart. i even stated in the note engine #1 will be running until we get ground power hooked up. then i sent a station note indicating the same thing. i got acknowledgments back from both parties in level flight, the first officer and i reviewed what occurred in austin before departure and talked it through. i had an uneasy feeling about lax but pressed on, surely everyone communicated with everyone, right?we arrived in lax and received taxi instructions to the gate via b c5 c which meant a right turn beyond 90 degrees for gate line up. i made another announcement to the passengers to remain seated until the seat belt sign was extinguished. as i began the turn both engines were running to minimize jet blast for this maneuver. i got the aircraft aligned began a slow taxi in, approximately 40' from the gate stop. i instructed to first officer to shutdown engine #2. again i had a weird feeling. they did, i continued my approach and came to a stop.i set the brakes and looked around at the ground crew, mass confusion was occurring below the wing, the ground handler would not allow the jetway to approach the aircraft because #1 engine was still running. no one knew why it was still running. i opened the window and explained to the ground handler that we had no apu and need ground power before i shut down the engine. the engine noise was too loud. i indicated he needed to get on a headset and called ops again. just then i noticed a fwd cargo light went on. they were opening doors before the engine was shutdown and the aircraft secured. surely this is a mistake i used priority communication behavior... right? the lead ground handler ran over and told the baggage handler to close the door again. i called ops and explained that i coordinated this with several folks before my arrival, the ops folks said they communicated it to ramp, and they acted like it's ops normal. not good!!a portable ground power cart was used on the right side of the aircraft, normally the jetway pulls up, the ground guys hook up ground power and i shut the engine down. i have done well over 100 no apu operations. this was by far the worst! dangerous!! after some confusion, the guys hooked up the portable ground power and we finally shut the engine down 10 minutes later!! this was very dangerous, in fact my messages to dispatch and lax station utilized that word. prior i have never used that word, i had a feeling this was poor communication from the start. i extinguish the seat belt sign made an announcement to the passengers and thanked them for their patience. i deplaned, talk to the gate agent and asked why he didn't drive the jetway up to the aircraft, he explained the ground lead told him not too. because the number 1 engine was running. again, i could have killed that baggage handler. let's be very clear about that... after all checklists were done, i sent the dispatcher a note and indicated lax... was not ready for us... mess and dangerous". his reply... "thats not good at all maybe worth filing something"because the door was opened by ramp before the engine was shutdown, the oooi (out-off-on-in) time are incorrect."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported hearing a loud thud with accompanying jolt and yaw during cruise. Flight secured engine and diverted.
text: aircraft x redacted-redacted. normal boarding and pre-departure checks. pushback and started engine 2 at xa:08. due to flow metering into redacted, waited to start engine 1 at xa:27. no abnormal engine indications on startup or during taxi. both engines had 8 minutes of warmup time and oil pressure/temperature/vibrations within limits before taking the runway. flight off at xa:35. no abnormal indications during climb phase or cruise phase until approx xb:12 at fl340. at xb:12, an audible bang could be heard from the flight deck and cabin, followed by vibrations and a left yawing moment. eicas indicated n1 decreasing to approx 22% with eng1 out caution message. after confirming with the pm/ca verbally that i would be the pilot flying and that i had controls, the pm/ca immediately began consulting engine 1(2) out qrh. to start the apu in accordance with this procedure, pm/ca requested priority handling and requested a descent to fl280. once below fl300, the apu was started. an engine restart was considered. an additional descent to fl240 was requested and the apu-assisted engine restart procedure according to the qrh was attempted once below fl250. the engine restart was unsuccessful. after coordination with dispatch via acars and air traffic control, a decision was made to turn right direct to redacted for diversion and continue descent. the flight attendant was briefed on special procedures according to company sop and pm/ca turned the fasten seatbelt sign on and provided an announcement to the passengers regarding the requirement to divert to redacted. inflight engine shutdown qrh was completed for engine 1. one engine inoperative approach and landing procedure qrh was completed. landing speeds and landing distances were calculated for redacted xxl according to qrh. we confirmed that the aircraft would be under max landing weight. a single engine approach briefing was given by the pm/ca. air traffic control provided delay vectors for an extended right downwind for a visual to redacted xxl to coordinate airport services to follow the aircraft after landing and for us to complete the approach checklist and one engine inoperative go around procedure. we then requested a right turn to join the instrument landing system xxl (in lieu of a visual approach). air traffic control cleared us for instrument landing system xxl approximately 9nm beyond the faf for the approach. at 3nm from the faf, the qrh landing checklist was completed to fully configure the aircraft. the autopilot was disconnected approximately 1nm from the faf and the instrument landing system xxl was hand flown to a normal landing. the after landing checklist was completed. we taxied to the gate, shut down the aircraft, and completed the parking checklist. we consulted airport services and airport operations and began appropriate company reports regarding the incident. a post flight walk around was conducted and found no obvious damage to the aircraft exterior, nor the cowlings, intake fan blades, or exhaust section of engine 1.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported main and back up horizontal stabilizer trim system failure during climb out. Flight returned to departure airport.
text: on day 0 aircraft x had a main and a back up trim failure during the initial climb out. flight crew got to the aircraft at the scheduled time of xa:30 in the morning. a gpu was not available for the initial start up of the apu. started the apu soon arriving at the aircraft. had paxs and cockpit ready to go at xb:10. was given a edt time of xb:45 local. i chose to stay at the gate and only run the apu. at xb:35 i gave the order for a push back. now running 20 minutes late. started both engines and was at the runway xxl at xb:40. at xb:46ish was given clearance to take off. gave the control to the first officer for his takeoff. takeoff was normal and uneventful. climb check was complete and was handed off to departure. climb through 4, 000ft we got an eicas message of ptrim main inop fallowed by ptrim backup inop. air traffic control had just cleared us to fl230. i said the first officer let stop the climb and go down to 4, 000ft. first officer said we have to go back to the field. i agreed and said maintain 4, 000ft and will get radar vectors (rv) and set up for the redacted instrument landing system xxr approach. i called approach and said we have an issue and will need to stay at 4, 000ft and rv for the instrument landing system xxr approach. dispatch acars us asking us if we were ok. i ignored the message. i had to keep it simple and aviate, navigate and communicate.redacted approach was very helpful and wanted to give us rv directly right to the instrument landing system xxr. i requested delay rvs to burn gas, run through a check list (qrh) and set up for the approach. approach gave us 3-4 more rv as i figured the weight of the ac, got vspeed numbers, set up the approach in the flight management system and on the flight panel. i quickly briefed the approach. all during this time dispatch was trying to get a hold of me via acars. i gave back to two quick replies about my intentions. the 2 replies to dispatch came in between a call to the fa and announcement to the passengers. due to time and the quickness of situation i did not use the full special procedures. basically, i said we were returning to redacted due to mechanical issues. the landing will be normal.for the final rv to final i took the controls and had the first officer give me back pressure on the yoke. i brief the first officer he would be my trim by providing back pressure on the yoke as needed by my verbal commands. this worked out well and i have to commend my first officer. he did a great job. the approach was good and straight down the pipe. landing was smooth as butter. touchdown at 1200-1400ft down the runway. i got the ac stopped and turned off the runway by taxi way 1". received a taxi clearance from tower to cross runway xxr and taxi via taxiway "2" and taxiway 3 to the gate. passed by the fire truck that had been rolled for us and gave them a thumbs up and a friendly wave.upon reaching the gate the rampers guided us in to a stop. did the nominal parking flow. the rampers said there was no gate agents at the gate. so i made announcement to the passengers "to please remain seated until we can get a gate agents. " 10 minutes later the gate agents showed up. then were able to deplane all of the paxs normally. i stood by the cockpit door said to each passenger thank you for your patience and sorry for the inconvenience.after once the passengers were off of the airplane and were working with the gate agent on rebooking. i started making phone calls. i called dispatch and then maintenance for the write up of the main and backup pitch trim. also called the chief pilot to cover all my bases."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a galley oven fire on initial climb and return to departure airport.
text: on initial climbout from redacted rwyxxc at approximately 3, 000 ft msl the purser called the flight deck to alert the captain that there was a 'large amount' of black smoke coming from the oven at a flight station. for the duration of the entire event i was not in communication with the back of the aircraft. at this time the captain was hand flying the aircraft to 5, 000 feet and i was pm. air traffic control gave us an initial vector and a climb to 15, 000 feet, i read back the clearance but delayed input into the control panel for concurrence with the captain. we decided to call back and request priority handling and request vectors to land back at redacted. at this time we split duties with the first officer flying the aircraft and handling air traffic control, captain ran the fire protection checklist. received short vectors back to land rwyxxl. the captain loaded the instrument landing system xxl into the fmc for a back up to the visual and then continued to run the non normal checklist. i called the airfield in sight at approximately 9 miles. a faster than normal airspeed was flown while turning onto final due to the unknown status of the galley fire. no instrument landing system frequencies were tuned and the fmc was not re-cruised to our current altitude. flight directors were ignored and the multi-function flight display (mfd) was referenced for runway alignment verification. gear and flaps were dropped to 30 on speed to be configured at approximately 700 feet agl. normal flare and touchdown was made for an overweight landing, on landing rollout is when i noticed that we had not selected an autobrake setting. manual braking was used to slow down and vacate the runway at the last high speed taxiway. crash fire rescue met the aircraft right after vacating the active runway and we taxied on taxiway 1 to hold short of runway xyr. at this time we slowed down and verified all appropriate checklist were completed and passengers were seated. we communicated with operations for a gate and taxied back to gate xx with no further issues.

text: flying from redacted to redacted enroute we got a gpws warning. we were descending on the redacted arrival with the sioe (supervised ioe) as pilot flying. we were cleared to cross redacted [fix] at or above 5, 000' and cleared for the rnav xx approach while in imc conditions. we set the faf crossing altitude of 2100' but through complacency, did not verify vnav was armed. the aircraft continued to descend through 5, 000' to about 2, 500' when we got the gpws warning. we started the climb back to 5, 000' while simultaneously being questioned by air traffic control about our altitude.looking back on this, i could have had better awareness to confirm the flight mode was set correctly to comply with the given instructions instead of getting distracted. after talking about things, it sounds like the vnav was selected twice.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: A321 flight crew reported overheating of galley floor. Diverted and landed uneventfully.
text: during climb, the #1 [fa] called and said that they smelled an electrical odor in the forward galley, near the r1 door. i sent the first officer back to check. he returned and said that he wasn't certain, but the floor near the door felt hot. i was about to call back to ask the fas if that was normal when they called up again to say that the floor material was melting. we were just about to level at fl350 approaching redacted [vor]. i asked the first officer to request priority and ask for a return to redacted. while he had been in the cabin, i looked for nearest airports and determined that the closest large airport was redacted. if the fas had said that there was smoke, i would have dropped into redacted as i know they do have airline service and a long enough runway to stop. gave the plane to the first officer and he got the plane going to redacted at a high speed. about halfway back i called back to see how things were going, the #1 said that the area was growing but still no smoke. i discussed that we were going to stop on the runway to be checked out and that i hoped we wouldn't need to evacuate but to listen if i called for that. she agreed that we didn't want to evacuate but would be ready and would let me know if she saw any reason to do so. air traffic control gave us as direct of a routing as they could with the mountains and we proceeded to xxr. informed air traffic control that we would be stopping on the runway. after we stopped, arff (airport rescue and firefighting) came to check us out, they saw a heat signature in the r1 door area- not blistering paint or any sign of an active fire so they asked us to proceed to the gate so they could check from inside. coming inside, the burn area was still showing about 107 degrees. they looked inside the cargo compartment and the e&e (electronics and equipment bay) area and saw no damage. the circles over the right side of the floor heating pad had disappeared by the time we landed. we deplaned using the l1 door after we determined that it was safe to do so.cause: don't know why the pad decided to overheat. there is no circuit breaker information. i was fairly certain that it was the heating pad overheating but i could not find someway to turn off the power to the unit. with an electric jet i don't want to be pulling breakers without any information as to what they control. however, after the turn to redacted, if a fire had broken out i think i would have started to pull anything that sounded like galley power. a little more info about things that can catch on fire in the plane would be nice.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a low altitude alert while descending to land at BUF. Flight crew was unsure if they misunderstood the clearance altitude or if the controller misspoke.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported descending below and then rejoining the glide path.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Hawker 800 flight crew reported on departure the yoke began violently pitching the aircraft forward and back. Flight crew regained control and continued to landing at destination airport.
text: the entire length of the flight was 10 minutes in duration. shortly after engaging the autopilot after takeoff from redacted, the yoke rapidly began violently pitching the plane forward and back suddenly. we previously had been experiencing unexplained issues with the autopilot including but not limited to: failure to capture localizer course, flight directors disappearing, red elevator trim annunciations necessitating the disconnecting of autopilot and trimming manually. i disconnected the autopilot, and the uncommanded pitch ceased. minutes later, redacted [tracon] control instructed me to fly direct redacted descend and maintain 2000 for the rnav xx into redacted. the autopilot at this time was engaged in nav/vnav mode and 2000 was preselected in the altitude selector. what had occurred was the autopilot did not capture the altitude, instead descending below it. rather than disconnecting immediately and maintaining my assigned altitude manually like i should have, i was late to react appropriately to the error and attempted to rectify the issue using the abnormally behaving automation, all the while the aircraft continued its rapid descent. we were several hundred feet below our assigned altitude before i disconnected and began climbing back to 2000. i then hand-flew the rest of the approach, landing on runway xx. there were no terrain or traffic alerts. i understand had the circumstances been different this could have been a fatal mistake, and i regret the actions i took. i should have taken control immediately upon discovering the deviation instead of trying to diagnose the problem. i am thankful that no other aircraft were affected.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: PA28-181 flight crew reported an NMAC in the traffic pattern resulted in evasive action taken.
text: we cancelled instrument flight rules with redacted approach, about 5 nm from rwyxx. flew offset to north of runway xx, followed the local entry procedure, intending to enter the traffic pattern (left traffic) for rwyxx. we turned crosswind and flew above the der at 2200ft msl, 500ft above the traffic pattern altitude, intending to make the teardrop entry at 45-degree angle (given the existence of multiple airplanes in the pattern/vicinity of the airport, we avoided a direct entry). after the frequency change approval from redacted approach, we have been announcing our location and intention via ctaf when off-setting to north, turning crosswind, starting the teardrop, joining downwind, base, and final at ctaf frequency. we are sure that we tuned into the correct frequency as we heard the preceding aircraft (barron) communicating over ctaf as well. when we were descending while in the tear drop, and joining to the downwind at 45-degree angle, we noticed an aircraft turning into the downwind, in our adsb, about 100 feet below us, which made no radio call. at that time, it was about 500ft horizontal distance, i think. i asked my student, who is flying, to maintain the altitude and even slightly climb, to ensure we won't descend to the same altitude, and asked him if he could visually see the aircraft. he saw it below and behind us (abut 7 o'clock direction, in line with our adsb screen). we flew the downwind faster at around 100knots, to ensure we have enough distance horizontally before descending for the base turn. we confirmed that we have made enough distance and turned/descended to base, final turns, and landed safely. we have been monitoring the distance with the aircraft behind us that seems to have slowed down to secure the distance as well. we did not check the tail number for that aircraft but noticed that it seems an old, vintage aircraft (single-engine), and also noticed that their radio calls after we took the above evasive actions. their adsb seemed sporadic and not consistently shown in our screen, unlike other aircraft that have been shown continually. we assume they might have had an incorrect ctaf frequency at the beginning.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: PA-32 pilot reported misinterpreting a clearance that resulted in a runway incursion and critical ground conflict.
text: while holding short of runway xxr at taxiway 1 at redacted airport, i received a transmission that included flight following information (remain clear of class b airspace, a departure frequency, and a discrete transponder code). at the time, i believed i was on the appropriate frequency for departure. due to the high traffic volume, extended delay prior to taxi, and my position at the hold short line ready for departure, i misinterpreted this transmission and believed it was a takeoff clearance.i read back: 'cleared for takeoff runway xxr, remain clear of the redacted class bravo, departure frequency, and squawk code.' the controller responded with 'readback correct.' i interpreted this as confirmation and believed it was a takeoff clearance. believing i was cleared, i visually checked final approach and did not observe any traffic on final, and observed a cirrus holding short at taxiway 2 (full length), which i believed was the aircraft i had heard waiting for an instrument flight rules clearance to redacted. i then entered runway xxr from taxiway 1. an aircraft was still on the runway but in the process of exiting, and after it cleared the runway, i started my takeoff roll.sometime during the takeoff roll, i heard 'monitor tower, ' which led me to recognize that i may not have been on the correct frequency or had not received a valid takeoff clearance. around liftoff, i attempted to contact tower on the assigned frequency (redacted.x) but did not receive a response and then switched to the other tower frequency (redacted.xx) to establish communication. during this time, i heard another aircraft execute a go-around. i adjusted my climb profile by shallowing the climb to reduce the risk of conflict but still maintain a safe distance above the ground.the problem arose from a misinterpretation of flight following information as a takeoff clearance. i believe some of the contributing factors included high workload due to traffic volume, frequency congestion, extended ground delay leading to expectation bias, and the similarity in cadence between the transmission and a takeoff clearance. receiving the flight following information while holding short of the runway, in a position normally associated with an imminent departure clearance, likely increased expectation bias and contributed to the misinterpretation. additionally, in busy environments it is common for flight following to be delayed or unavailable, and because no earlier indication was given that flight following would be issued later, i did not anticipate receiving it at that point, which likely contributed to the confusion. my perception that i was on the appropriate frequency and ready for departure influenced my judgment and decision-making. the issue was discovered when i heard 'monitor tower' during the takeoff roll, which prompted immediate recognition of a discrepancy.corrective actions included attempting to establish communication with tower, switching frequencies when necessary, and modifying my climb profile to maintain safe separation from other aircraft. no further conflict developed.to prevent recurrence, i will ensure i'm on the correct frequency prior to departure and will positively verify that an explicit takeoff clearance has been received from tower before entering the runway. i will also deliberately pause at the hold short line, particularly in high workload environments, to confirm clearance and reduce the effects of expectation bias.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a rough running engine during climb that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
text: was getting ready to depart redacted to pick up some passengers and fly them back down. everything looked normal on the run up. i departed redacted on an instrument flight rules flight plan to redacted. i was given climb 6000 and proceed direct redacted [vor]. i engaged the garmen autopilot and set it to nav and vs to 500 ft p/min. at around 3000ft i noticed my airspeed was dropping. the autopilot started yelling 'stall stall stall, airspeed airspeed airspeed.' i immediately disengaged the autopilot and pushed the nose down to get my airspeed back. i then began troubleshooting, pulled the throttle out and back in - the engine came back rough. this is when i requested priority handling and let air traffic control know what was happening. i immediately turned back towards redacted. i heard air traffic control give me a vector so i told him i was going direct redacted. at this point the engine was still working* however it was rough. i continued into redacted and was getting ready to join the downwind for xx because that was the active runway when again my rpm dropped. i immediately decided not to go with xx and entered a side slip to land xy. after landing xy i taxied back and squawked the aircraft.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported a rough running engine during cruise that resulted in a diversion to a nearby airport.
text: on a routine training flight with a private pilot working on a flight review we departed from redacted and climbed to 5500 feet with no issues. once at cruise we went through our checklist items, everything checked out normal. we did a simulated engine out scenario and chose a field to descend down to with no issues. the climb out from this scenario went as planned with no indication of any engine issues. we climbed to 3500 feet and leveled off direct to redacted to work on performance landings and take offs. once passed redacted we noticed the engine running rough and making a knocking noise. i immediately took the controls and we quickly went through our checklist items and made a turn for redacted as it was the closest airport and we had it in sight. nothing we tried fixed the issue but we did have partial engine power and were able to maintain altitude. i made a priority handling call to redacted and started reporting that we were inbound and gave several position calls. the landing went well with no other issues and we were able to taxi back to the fbo. once on the ramp we noticed oil dripping on the ground and what appeared to be a bent pushrod on the right side. the plane still had 5 quarts of oil in it at this time.

synopsis: General aviation pilot reported unknowingly flying into an area where UAS operations were taking place. Reporter stated the area was designated by NOTAM; but they did not see it.
text: i flew through a temporary uas operations area during the descent phase of my short flight from redacted to my destination (3s7). the temporary uas operations area was 25 nm in radius, extended from the ground to 5000 ft. elevation and included 3 public-use airports that were open to public use at the time. there was no tfr in place at the time. upon reporting for landing at 3s7, i received a transmission on 122.9 from an individual who did not identify himself and stated that i had flown through a uas operations area and that on departure from 3s7, i should 'not depart to the south'. i responded by inquiring about notams and reported that i would be overnight at 3s7. there was no reply. because my destination was within the uas operations area and open to public-use i had no option but to descend through the uas area on descent. in retrospect, i acknowledge that i should have been more aware of the temporary uas operations area and i should have determined a frequency to use to request advisories, but there was no tfr and i missed seeing the notam. lessons to self: 1) review all notams, even for routine flights, 2) keep the notam feature on foreflight turned on.i appreciate the advice that i was given about not departing 3s7 to the south. however, i question if there is not a better and safer way to handle interaction between ga aircraft and uas operations. if there were indeed extensive uas operations in the area that posed a hazard to ga aircraft, why was there not a tfr?

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: A TRACON controller reported a Citation pilot reported NMAC with a VFR aircraft which did not appear on the controller's radar.
text: i was busy following a runway flow change and sector split when i released aircraft y from redacted. after establishing radar contact, aircraft y reported a scary close call with another aircraft approximately 400 feet from his position. i didn't see a primary anywhere in close proximity to aircraft y. i issued traffic advisories for the only aircraft observed in the area but both were well above aircraft y and on my frequency. aircraft y indicated the conflicting aircraft was talking with redacted [tower]. i advised that we would coordinate with redacted [tower] to see what was out there.shortly thereafter, aircraft x contacted me just outside zzzs class d airspace. i issued a discrete code. the pilot reported a position southwest of redacted and stated he did not have a transponder. i instructed the aircraft to remain clear of the redacted class b airspace.based on the pilots position, timing, and degraded radio quality, i suspected aircraft x may have been the aircraft referenced by aircraft y. i did not ever call him radar contact due to the lack of a transponder and only an intermittent primary target. i told aircraft x to exit the redacted class b mode c veil due to operating without a transponder. the pilot objected, stating he had a right to be there because he doesn't have a generator. i asked for his altitude and relayed that information to the next sector for traffic awareness. he flew nw bound through the veil until nw of redacted field when i briefed the next controller.after being relieved from position, i reviewed the aim regarding operations within the mode c veil with the supervisor. the aim notes that certain older aircraft not originally equipped with certain equipment may be permitted to operate without one but it also indicates that aircraft intending to operate within the mode c veil without a transponder are expected to coordinate with air traffic control in advance to ensure situational awareness and safety. further review of 14 cfr 91.215 says that operations within the mode c veil generally require an operable transponder, with limited exceptions outlined in 91.215(b)(3) for certain aircraft not originally equipped with the required systems. additionally, 91.215(d) requires prior air traffic control authorization for deviations from transponder requirements when applicable.regardless if the exception applies to him, the lack of coordination reduced our ability to provide traffic advisories and maintain situational awareness. i believe that operations within the mode c veil without a transponder and without prior coordination increases the risk of potential unsafe situations. aircraft intending to operate in the mode c veil without a transponder should coordinate with air traffic control in advance to prevent unsafe situations even if they are allowed to be there due to equipment limitations. redacted [tower] could have coordinated with us about the aircraft with equipment issues or no transponder. somehow, we need to reinforce pilot understanding about how potentially unsafe this would be operating in the veil without coordination.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A321 First Officer reported an unstable approach with a bounced landing.
text: i was the pilot flying for the redacted-redacted initial leg of our trip. prior to descent, the pilot monitoring and i briefed the arrival, approach, stabilized approach criteria/considerations, landing, and taxi items. we briefed the threats of high density altitude, increasing temperatures, and a heavy aircraft. the plan was to fly the instrument landing system xxl, even if cleared for the visual, in order to protect against class b airspeed infractions and to fly a stable/predictable approach.flying the arrival and instrument landing system approach were uneventful, meeting stabilized approach criteria we had earlier briefed. winds were variable according to the atis. at approximately 700 ft i disengaged the autopilot once i believe the managed thrust had properly adjusted for the winds. at approximately 650 ft i observed a tailwind on the display. i adjusted to a more nose down attitude in order to keep the aircraft from landing long with the tailwind. at 500 ft the aircraft and pm announced '500 feet' and i responded 'stable' referencing my airspeed on the pfd (primary flight display). when i referenced the pfd at 500 ft for speed, i noticed the wind had shifted from a tailwind to a crosswind. in order to correct my previous tailwind inputs, i shallowed my pitch inputs inside of 500 ft to maintain my aim point.at the 50 ft automated callout i remembered i had previously briefed i would keep the thrust in longer than normal due to the high, hot, heavy conditions. however, i do not remember exactly when i began my thrust reduction. at 30 feet i started my flare but noticed the controls were not as responsive as i was accustomed to on other landings because the airspeed had slowly decayed prior to my flare input. the following events happened in very quick succession. the aircraft bounced, i heard an automated 'pitch' annunciation, the pm said 'continue' ( or something similar), and i flew the nose wheel to the ground and simultaneously engaged the thrust reversers. it was definitely a startle event because of the firm bounce and by the time the thought of 'go-around' entered my mind i was already flying the nose wheel to the ground.we exited the runway and pulled into a de-ice pad while we waited for parking. after providing the flights attendants and passengers an update on our gate, the pm told me what he saw and experienced. we taxied to the gate and conducted a more thorough debrief using the crew debrief card. the captain conducted a walk around of the aircraft after we pulled into the gate and i began preparing for the following flight. after the box was prepared for the following flight, i conducted a walk around to visually inspect the aircraft before the following flight.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a rapid roll oscillation and buffet during approach. Flight continued to a normal landing.
text: just after intercepting the instrument landing system xxl approach course from redacted with flaps 5, 1-1.5 inches of sb, and at 202 kts, a rapid roll oscillation (3 hz) and buffet were encountered for approximately 5 seconds. the phenomena was similar to wake turbulence combined with stall buffet, minus the high aoa. after the gear was extended with flaps 15 at 162 kts, the phenomena was encountered again. as an effect of the two startles, the captain failed to arm appr. subsequently, g/s mode was never active. when the first officer vocalized being high on the papi, the captain pitched down to intercept the vnav path and papi, being fully stable by approximately 700' afe. the landing was normal and a call to the chief pilot was made.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to brake aggressively during taxi to stop at a hold short line.
text: while taxiing east on taxiway bravo, in between b9 and b8, i observed aircraft y landing on runway 27 and possibly about to exit at taxiway b8. i thought that were cleared to taxi to runway 27 via bravo and i initially added a little thrust to make sure we would get past b8 before aircraft y got there. meanwhile, i had tasked my first officer with the before takeoff checklist to the line and he was accomplishing the steps. he then reminded me that we were to hold short of b8. i didn't need to second guess his input because the situation was becoming quite clear. i stopped short of b8, but i had to brake aggressively. i contacted the flight attendants and they reported being shook up. at least two fas were in the aisle, but none were injured. the fas checked the passengers and none were injured. we continued taxi, i made a pa apologizing for the aggressive stop, and we departed san without further incident. once in cruise, my first officer and i debriefed the incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: B757 Captain reported tower advised that smoke was coming from an engine during landing. No fire was deteteced and aircraft was towed to the gate.
text: during preflight, i observed a wet area beneath the right engine. i brought this to the mechanics attention during a face-to-face discussion with the first officer present. the mechanic stated the fluid was due to over-servicing the aircraft. i noted that it appeared similar to hydraulic fluid, however, the mechanic again confirmed it was oil from over-servicing.i conducted a thorough inspection of the engine cowling and surrounding areas during preflight and did not observe any visible leaks or residual fluid.the takeoff, cruise, descent, and approach phases were all uneventful. upon landing, when i attempted to deploy the thrust reversers, an amber indication appeared for the right reverser. during the rollout, the tower advised us that smoke was visible coming from the right engine. there were no fire indications in the cockpit at that time.tower inquired whether we required emergency services, and while we were in the process of exiting the runway, they informed us that arff (airport rescue and firefighting) had been dispatched. tower continued to report that smoke was present but decreasing. we exited the runway and came to a stop on the taxiway to allow arff to inspect the aircraft.shortly thereafter, we received a right hydraulic quantity eicas message. we switched to the arff frequency and communicated directly with them. arff reported no visible fire, only diminishing smoke. as a precaution, we elected to run the evacuation checklist from the qrh.arff advised that there was minimal smoke remaining and that it appeared to be caused by hydraulic fluid contacting the hot section of the engine. we reconfirmed with arff that there was no fire present.i notified dispatch and maintenance control that we had stopped on the taxiway and intended to evacuate the aircraft to facilitate inspection of the right engine. maintenance personnel met the aircraft, and it was subsequently towed back to the gate without further incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A B747 First Officer reported a false fire warning while enroute. Reporter indicated this is a recurring issue.
text: about 6 hours into the flight during cruise i was in the crew rest area when the pf/pm rang the crew rest area. when i entered the cockpit i saw we had an eicas message for fire main deck aft." since we were carrying flowers we briefed in preflight that there had been false cargo fire signals and we thought this might be the issue. even though we briefed it previously we treated it like a fire initially. the pm was using the qrh. the captain, 747 rated dead header and i were going through the supplementary procedure for false cargo fire warning messages. the deadheader and i eventually went down to the main deck to visually verify if there was smoke, fire or neither. we determined that in the main deck we could not locate any smoke or fire. with this information the crew decided to continue to our destination but that we would keep checking the main deck and monitor the ecs (environmental control system) page for temperature readings. eventually the fire indication went away and we landed safely in redacted. cause: plane full of flowers we were carrying.suggestion: something needs to be done so these false fire warnings do not keep happening. one day a crew may not take it seriously enough to start and lose critical time getting the plane on the ground in the event of a real fire."

text: on the ground first officer saw light shining through crack of dv (direct vision) window and a/c (aircraft) frame. opened window and tried to close it again, had hard time closing it but was finally able to. on takeoff there was a loud hissing noise coming from his dv window until we got to around 3, 000 feet and then it made two loud pops and the hissing went away. as we climbed out pressurization and everything looked normal, leveled off at fl250 as we were messaging dispatch and maintenance control about the window. they came back and said that we should be good but if we wanted to go back to redacted to be safe we could, during that time the first officer would occasionally hear a cracking noise coming from the window so we felt it was better to be safe than sorry and divert back to redacted. as we were heading back maintenance control asked if we had performed the qrh procedure windshield cracked or impaired so we ran that and had no problems on the descent into redacted.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Flight instructor reported a runway excursion during landing. Aircraft was re-positioned onto the nearest taxiway.
text: i was conducting a training flight from redacted to redacted to practice pilotage and landings with the student pilot/owner. navigation to redacted was uneventful and we entered the left downwind for runway xx. the approach was normal but about 5 knots fast, and we bounced about a foot after the first touchdown. i told the pilot to restabilize, continue to hold it off, and let it touch down again. when it did, there as a significant shimmy from the tailwheel. there was about an 8-10 knot left crosswind, so i told him to apply more right rudder as we started to move left of the centerline (the stick was already all the way back and left). when the plane continued to turn left, i added full right rudder, but there was no response nor change in direction. the left turn tightened, the left wing raised, and we veered left off the runway, did a 270 degree groundloop and ended up about 5 feet off the left side of runway xx about midfield, facing the runway. there were no injuries and no noticeable damage to the aircraft other than a scuff on the right wingtip where it contacted the grass. we pulled the aircraft from the grass, walked the airplane back on the runway and exited on the nearest taxiway. we called the ia (inspection authority mechanic) who had done the annual for the airplane who was based at redacted and he came out and replaced the tailwheel. the pins that provide tailwheel steering had completely sheared. we tested the new tailwheel, taxied to and departed runway xx and returned to redacted and had a normal landing there.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: RV9 pilot reported a complete electrical failure during cruise and subsequent engine failure after landing.
text: flight departed redacted en route to redacted. air traffic control clearance was obtained to transit the redacted class b airspace direct to redacted. the aircraft overflew redacted as cleared and proceeded direct toward redacted.approximately 10 nm from redacted, while in communication with redacted departure, a decrease in alternator output was observed, followed by progressive electrical system degradation and battery discharge. the pilot began shedding non-essential electrical loads, including the autopilot.an initial call was made to redacted approach to report an electrical malfunction and request a frequency change to redacted tower in anticipation of a potential loss of communications. during this transmission, a complete electrical failure occurred. the mfd (multi-function flight display), pfd (primary flight display), radios, transponder, and gps became inoperative. the pilot was unable to continue radio communication or set an emergency transponder code.engine power remained normal. at this point, the aircraft was approximately 6 nm from redacted. with all primary flight instruments inoperative, foreflight gps was used to approximate position and altitude, however, no airspeed or other flight data were available.the pilot was accompanied by one passenger with no aviation experience. a decision was made to proceed directly to redacted and execute a straight-in approach to the nearest suitable runway equipped with papi for visual glide path guidance. runway xx was selected based on prior departure earlier that day and availability of papi.due to the lack of airspeed, altitude, and other flight instruments, entering the traffic pattern was deemed higher risk because of the potential for unsafe altitude or airspeed conditions. additionally, given the electrically dependent ignition system, engine reliability was uncertain. a straight-in approach minimized maneuvering and time to landing.a no-flap landing was executed on runway xx. the aircraft exited the runway at taxiway 1, where the engine subsequently lost power and could not be restarted.there were no injuries to occupants and no damage to the aircraft or airfield.human factors: need to obtain a secondary handheld com.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported people on the runway while on final approach. Pilot rejected landing and returned for landing.
text: during the downwind leg for landing on runway 26, i announced my position and intent to land at wy05. i noticed several people standing on the taxi area immediately south of the runway at about 1500 feet from the approach end. the runway itself appeared to be clear. upon turning final i noticed three people on the runway at approximately 1500 feet from the approach end. one north of the centerline, one on the centerline and one south of the centerline. i aborted the landing. i re-entered the pattern calling my position and asking if anyone was monitoring the frequency. i did not receive a response on the radio. the runway remained clear and i landed just beyond a group of people standing immediately south of the runway.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Conflict Airborne Conflict; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported a conflict with an aircraft on approach while waiting to depart. Pilot elected to delay the takeoff.
text: at obe, numerous flight training aircraft were performing tight circuit touch and go's resulting in aircraft on the ground being unable to depart or even cross runways. this continued for some time.my aircraft was #2 for departure waiting as training aircraft performed several complete circuits of touch and go's.i keyed the mic contacting aircraft y (#1 for take off) and suggested that he may need to do a expedited take off as the pattern was crowded and i suggested 'obe traffic extend their downwind or practice some go arounds'.someone in the pattern also repeated my request. pattern aircraft did extend there downwind, spacing was then provided for aircraft y to safely depart with a expedited departure.my aircraft was now #1 for departure runway 5 and i waited for the next landing aircraft to clear. i saw the next aircraft turning base to final and i announced and took runway 5 for departure. as i entered the runway for takeoff someone on the radio yelled 'get the [expletive] off the runway' and at that instant i also got a ads-b traffic alert 0.4 mile.those two things caused me doubt my situational awareness and location of other aircraft. i decided the safest thing was to not move until i was certain it was safe to depart.this delay on the runway was not planned malice, rather shaken from the belligerent radio call and traffic alert, i needed time to sort out the situation before moving for takeoff. the almost simultaneous traffic alert and unexpected belligerent radio call was a massive distraction causing me to pause and re-access while still on the ground (runway 5). apparently the landing traffic was determined to land.most of the flight training aircraft in the area operate in the patterns professional, courteously and safely, yet there are some exceptions.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: Aeronca Champ student pilot reported tail wheel broke free during landing with subsequent ground loop on the runway. Aircraft was pushed to the hangar.
text: i was flying from redacted to redacted with my instructor in my 1946 aeronca champ 7ac and i was landing on runway xx. after the flare the plane touched down and i was correcting for the wind and it pushed us down and the tail wheel broke free which gave me no rudder authority causing the plane to ground loop off the runway. there was for physical damage to me or my instructor and there was a small scuff on the right wing tip. there was no damage to any airport property. we pushed the plane to a maintenance hanger and discovered that the two directional pins located inside the maule tailwheel had sheared off and that was likely the lose of rudder control.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Grumman AA5B pilot reported failure of main gear tire during landing roll out. Aircraft was towed off runway.
text: while performing my preflight inspections, i noted that the left main tire was a few psi low. i assumed it was due to the large variations in ambient temperature that the region has been experience lately. i inflated the tire to 35 psi and monitored for leaks while finishing my preflight, with no leaks identified.my route was to redacted, with a full stop landing planned for redacted. upon touching down on runway xx at redacted, i noted that the plane was pulling to the left, so i added right rudder. the pull to the left increased, but i was able to make a right turn to start heading down taxiway 1. before completely clearing the runway on taxiway 1, the plane came to a halt and no amount of throttle could get it to move. at that point, tower closed runway xx and diverted traffic to runway xy. the local fbo, sent a tug over to tow us off the runway. runway xx was closed for a period due to my plane fouling the runway.the local repair shop replaced the tire and tube prior to my departure from redacted.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Cessna Citation Captain reported cabin pressurization issue during climb. Crew returned to departure airport.
text: after picking up the plane from maintenance, i did a preflight check but missed that the bleed air source switch was in the off position. the on position looks very similar as both are vertical. as we climbed out, the cabin altitude got above 10, 000'. we donned masks, descended, ran the checklist, and returned to the airport. the checklist has you check the bleed air source switch position. i saw it vertical and thought it was on. we landed without issue.despite being extra cautious on a post maintenance flight, i still missed the switch position.is it possible to add 2 red markings, one on the switch at 12 o'clock and another on the panel for the on position? that would remove the ambiguity.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Challenger CL-30 Captain reported failure of stab trim system and navigation instrumentation during cruise. Crew diverted and landed safely.
text: ap (autopilot) stab trim fail and pri stab trim fail occurred at fl430 over redacted while enroute to redacted from redacted. the crew executed all appropriate checklists and continued on to alternate for destination, redacted, until the cabin and cockpit started rapidly becoming very cold and navigation instrumentation started to provide false readings in relation to level flight, course, and track. flight conditions were continuous light chop and mountain wave action. the aircraft was being hand flown at this point with secondary pitch trim selected. after discussion, the crew decided that a divert was necessary for the safety of flight to redacted due to weather conditions and longer runways available. air traffic control was advised and priority handling was requested due to the unknown electrical indications that were present at that time with the seriousness of the event that could be encountered if the secondary trim failed. during descent the crew encountered several more false readings of course and track. runway xxr visual approach was selected for the landing and no further issues were encountered. the aircraft was landed and taxied safely to the fbo. the crew gave a brief oral report to the fire fighters and explained to the passengers why the divert was necessary. the passengers were then assisted by company personnel for hotel accommodations and departed.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence

text: began the shift with a weather brief regarding throughput concerns later in the night. the plan of attack was to keep things running without any tmis (traffic management initiatives) until we started getting impacts. around xa:00 the impacts started and the os (operations supervisor) called the command center for a 1st tier ground stop. n90 agreed with the stop but was overruled by the dcc (division command center). when i got back from my break i called the dcc again and asked for a ground stop due to lack of routes. the request was ignored and traffic was continued to run into the airport unimpeded. land 22, depart 31 swap (severe weather avoidance plan) event needs to be controlled better. at xd:00 the surface became almost gridlocked and an aircraft had to back taxi on the departure runway to get to their gate. it situations like this that can get us into trouble and based on recent events should be avoided. tonight's event could had been prevented and was not acceptable in the current climate. listen to your people.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported cabin pressurization issues climbing through FL320. Flight diverted and landed safely.
text: during our climb up to fl320, we began to feel a moderate airframe vibration passing through fl230. we immediately looked at engine indications and captain ask me to reduce power to see if it was engine related. engine indications looked normal and vibration did not change. captain called fa to ask if she could hear and feel the vibration from the cabin. she could. we continued a slow climb while we diagnosed the issue. we then felt our ears pop and we immediately checked cabin pressure. cabin pressure was slowly rising at 400fpm. captain asked air traffic control for a level off and we leveled at fl250. in level flight we noticed the cabin climb rate increase to 700fpm and cabin alt increase to approximately 5000. captain requested a descent and air traffic control gave us pd (pilot's discretion) down to 10000. at this point there were no caution or warning messages. we began a descent at about 2500fpm. in the descent, the cabin rate was still climbing 800-1000fpm. we then increased our descent rate to 4000fpm with flight spoilers deployed. captain called for oxygen masks on and we donned masks out of caution. captain requested priority handling. passing through fl180 the cabin alt caution came on. cabin alt was 8000' and climbing. since we were already in a preventative descent, i continued to fly as captain coordinated with air traffic control. the cabin alt warning came passing through 14000 and initiated the qrc for emergency descent and changed controls. we almost immediately leveled off at 10000' and warning message went out and cabin alt showed 6500'. captain asked me to tell air traffic control we'd like to divert to the nearby airport. since we were stable at a safe altitude, captain decided to switch controls back to me. he then requested 8000' and we began descending again. the fa called and mentioned it was very hot. he asked if the oxygen masks had deployed and if everyone was ok. masks did not deploy and everyone was ok. captain then continued with the qrc even though warning/caution lights went away. during completion of the qrc, captain decided to not deploy passenger oxygen because warning messages were out and the cabin alt was 5000-6000'. we also noticed the cabin temp was at 32c. we both thought deploying the masks unnecessarily would cause undue panic in the very hot cabin. we then descended to 6000' and asked for delay vectors to run qrh and setup for the approach. the captain completed the qrh procedures, messaged dispatch, notified pax (passengers), and coordinated with fas. he then setup and briefed the approach. we completed normal checklists. when we got the landing data, it showed we would be landing about 200lbs heavy. we decided an immediate landing was necessary with cabin temp now at 33c. captain took controls and i advised air traffic control we were ready for the approach. approach and landing were normal. during taxi, i called ops for a gate. they said they had a gate ready to go. i then made a pax announcement stating we were aware of the heat and we already had a gate and we'd have a short taxi. we arrived at the gate, ca made an announcement and pax deplaned normally. i completed a post-flight inspection and ca contacted company. cause: the initial cause of this event was an uncommanded depressurization of the aircraft.suggestions: nothing could have been done with the maintenance issue causing depressurization. we might have been able to hold or add drag to increase fuel consumption but ultimately made the decision that cabin temp was more of a safety issue than landing 200lbs overweight.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that during landing; the pilot flying reduced the thrust levers too slowly causing the aircraft to float past the go around point. The Captain called for a go around; but the thrust levers were locked. The Captain took control and landed the plane.
text: the approach was going well, the pilot flying was stabilized for the entire approach. during the landing phase of flight, the pilot flying reduced the thrust levers too slowly. they were not idle at 50', of which i called out. this caused us to began floating. as we floated past the specified go around point on the runway. i called for the pilot flying to perform a go around. the pilot flying hit the toga button and attempted to advance the thrust levers forward. the thrust levers were locked and would not advance. i then tried to take controls and attempt the go around, but the thrust levers were indeed locked. with no other option, i put the aircraft on the ground at the end of the touchdown zone or slightly after it and applied max thrust reverse and maximum braking. we stopped the aircraft and taxied off of the runway with no further issues. i called maintenance control and wrote up the aircraft for the issue. cause: the cause of the event was incorrect landing technique. the pilot flying did not have a lot of experience in the type of aircraft flown. the thrust levers being locked, preventing us from performing a go around was largely a contributing factor. suggestions: i will question the other pilot more about their experience levels with the aircraft and ensure their landing techniques are included in their briefs.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Speed All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported stall warning/stick shaker activation due to inaccurate speeds on Primary Flight Display during take off.
text: early morning flight departing redacted at xa:00am. deferred apu. ground crew understaffed and in training. so we had to sit there for 25 min waiting for ground crew to show up with no pack (pneumatic air cycle kit). passengers complained about stale air and rising temperature. ground crew showed up and proceeded with engine start with external air. after engine 1 start, we lost ac power for split second due to a small error when transferring ac from ground ac to gen 1. captain quickly fixed it. as a result all the v speeds were cleared out. it was a very short taxi and we were behind schedule. neither ca or myself noticed the speeds cuz we both verified it previously. captain is pf. on take off roll, i called v1, rotate. captain started rotating, stall horn went off that's when i realized the speeds are off, the speeds were bunched up together and were were below rotation speed. stall horn went off, stick shaker, captain lowered nose and increased thrust. we eventually gained enough airspeed and continued without further incident. did not impact runway or lose control, or get into a real stall. cause: early morning departure, behind schedule and complaining passengers. weather conditions was nice weather and very light wind. it looked like nothing could go wrong on that take off. complacency and external pressure definitely contributed to our errors. ac power was only out for 1 second, nothing else was affected except the speeds so neither ca or myself noticed. on take off roll, i called 'v1 rotate' without double checking the actual speed until i noticed v2 was there too and we were below the planned speeds. i should've double checked if these numbers made sense before calling them out. and it took me too long to realize what was going on. i should've realized the number were off sooner and made call outs off my take off data print out. suggestions: need to not let external pressure get to us, like complaining passengers and unusual engine start proc. and delays. need to not let compalcency get to us either, especially on a calm vmc day with very light wind where 'nothing could pososibly go wrong'.need to be aware of things that can potentially be impacted by temporary power loss.take my time, verify things, and not rush through things.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: EMB-170 flight crew reported loss of #2 hydraulic system during approach. Crew executed go-around and landed safely.
text: while on approach into redacted we received the hyd 2 lo press indication and then a hyd 2 lo qty after putting the gear down . we advised air traffic control we will be discontinuing the approach, cleaned up the aircraft and told air traffic control we had experienced a hydraulic system issue and needed to run checklist. at this time, i 'the first officer' flew the aircraft and handled radio communications while the captain went through the checklist. once we established that all checklist had been run and completed, we chose to request priority handling due to the fact that we knew we were losing hydraulic fluid. we felt it was best to have emergency services on the ground to inspect the hydraulic two system area after landing. emergency services inspected the aircraft and then we were advised it was ok to proceed to the gate. upon parking, a puddle of hydraulic fluid was seen forming at the base of the right main landing gear. emergency services pinned the main and speedy dry was placed. exact hydraulic leak location wasn't identified at that time.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Pilatus PC-12 pilot reported a stabilizer trim malfunction during cruise. Pilot reset trim mechanism and continued the flight.
text: in stable cruise flight, imc, negative ice, light to moderate turbulence, ap (autopilot) on.without warning the aircraft started to climb, disengage ap and no change, found stab trim indicator almost maxed out full up. used the emergency trim interrupt switch to stop all trimming. while fighting the high yoke forces and working the qrh to solve the issue the aircraft climbed about 2000 feet and course was changed by about 30 degrees. air traffic control asked and i advised we had a runaway trim situation we were working on. i was able to troubleshoot the primary stab trim as the culprit. pulled the associated circuit breaker, placed the trim interrupt switch back to normal, used the alt stab trim switch to bring the stab trim back down to the proper setting. which then relieved all the abnormal yoke pressure, allowing a descent to the assigned cruise altitude and heading. i engaged the ap and reported to air traffic control that the situation was resolved.

synopsis: Cessna 172 flight instructor reported an NMAC in the traffic pattern with an opposite direction aircraft.
text: i was taking off, runway xx at redacted on day 0. i was the instructor in the right seat. as my student was flying the upwind leg for runway xx, i spotted another cessna pointing straight at us at most 500 feet above us, coming the opposite direction as if they were on final for runway xy. i quickly took controls from my student and took evasive maneuvers by turning an early crosswind to the east. there was not a single radio call from this pilot flying towards us. as i turned east, he turned in the same direction as us briefly, ending up right on our tail. this airplane was traveling much faster than us, so i then had to take another evasive maneuver and turn southbound and vacate the pattern. again - not a single radio call until i asked what they were doing on the radio.
