text: i was training a developmental on mullr/lucke/binns/finals combined when we lost the frequency 126.1. the majority of aircraft were on the frequency, including 3 instrument flight rules jets who were on final into iad. i took over and immediately put all surrounding sectors into holding and went out on guard to have the aircraft on 126.1 switch to a different frequency.this is a reoccurring issue at potomac tracon. we have had many issues with frequencies, creating extremely unsafe situations. i do not know what causes these issues so it is difficult for me to offer a recommendation on how to fix this. i have never experienced the frequencies going out unexpectedly like we do here at potomac tracon.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Hazardous Material Violation; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A319 First Officer reported uncommanded aircraft movement during pushback from the gate when the flight crew felt a shudder and the aircraft started moving without the brakes set. The Captain set the brakes.
text: the push began normally after receiving clearance from the ramp controller. once we appeared to be in the correct position for disconnection with both engines started, we sat for what seemed like an unusual time without communication from the ground crew. the captain eventually inquired if they were ready for him to set the brake, and they said 'please set brake.' before the captain set the brake, we felt the plane shudder as if it was being dropped from the tow tractor and it started rolling forward. at this point the ground crew said 'set brake, set brake, set brake!'. the captain brought the aircraft to a stop and set the parking brake. at no point did the captain verbalize to the crew 'parking brake set, pressure normal' which would have indicated that it was safe to disconnect. we also did not receive the 'breakaway' command that would have indicated a problem with the tug. following the event, the ground crewmember did advise us that they were having trouble with the tow tractor, though it's unclear whether they disconnected the tug without clearance, or the tug had a mechanical failure such that it was still attached to the aircraft and the aircraft was able to push it under idle thrust.following the disconnect, we taxied to the assigned spot. i called operations on the radio to ask for the final weights, as the taxi would be short and the response to the message was that the ramp had not completed their document. the operations person advised us to the return to the gate so that the dangerous goods on board could be re-secured. we did as requested. during the second pushback, we received clearance from ramp and the captain gave push clearance to the ground personnel. we sat for several minutes without moving, at which point the captain queried the push crew. they stated that they were having issues with the tow tractor, and that a supervisor was coming to assist with a reset. we cancelled the push clearance, and the captain advised them of this. the problem was eventually fixed, and we pushed. i did notice that the crew used nonstandard phraseology when communicating with the captain.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Person / Animal / Bird; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue; Ground Incursion Ramp
synopsis: Ramp agent reported a conflict with an aircraft approaching on the lead in line while parking at the gate; when the ramp agent signaled for the aircraft to stop movement and the pilot continued to follow the self park guidance system into the gate with personnel near the aircraft. No injury occurred.
text: the incident involving aircraft x arriving from redacted to redacted was extremely concerning from a safety standpoint and presented the potential for a severe accident involving both personnel and aircraft movement.as the ramp lead, i observed that the jetbridge had been positioned improperly by the jetbridge operator. the jetbridge was raised to an excessively high level, which caused the cage holding the ground air hose at the gate to become lifted off the ground and stuck. this created an unsafe condition because when the cage becomes jammed, movement of the jetbridge can force sudden or uncontrolled motion, increasing the risk of damage to equipment, the aircraft, and nearby personnel.due to this hazard, i immediately gave the pilot the x signal to stop, and one of my agents positioned on the number 1 engine side also reinforced the stop command. the pilot did initially stop. i then turned my attention to assisting the jetbridge operator in correcting the hazardous condition so the area could be made safe.while i was actively addressing the issue, the pilot began taxiing the aircraft into the gate on his own without receiving clearance to continue from me as the ramp lead. this was done after a clear stop command had already been given. i was still on the taxi line and was not aware the aircraft had started moving again. at the same time, the jetbridge was still involved in correcting the original hazard. this created an extremely dangerous situation in which i was placed directly at risk by an advancing aircraft.once i realized the aircraft was moving, i immediately began giving repeated stop commands to the pilot multiple times. my agent also gave stop commands. despite these repeated signals, the pilot continued to taxi forward until the aircraft came dangerously close to me, forcing me to move out of the way to avoid possible serious injury. the pilot then pointed at me in an aggressive manner, appearing to indicate the self-park system as justification for continuing into the gate.this is deeply concerning because a direct stop command from the ramp lead was ignored multiple times during an active safety hazard. the pilot's decision to continue taxiing without clearance, while personnel were still exposed in the movement area and while gate equipment was not yet in a safe condition, created an unacceptable risk of severe injury or fatality. this incident reflects a serious breakdown in communication, situational awareness, and compliance with ramp safety procedures, and it should be treated as a major safety event.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Fractional jet pilots reported an altitude deviation resulting from a strong downdraft during cruise on a published arrival. The flight crew climbed back to the assigned altitude; and continued the flight.
text: while cruising at 11000 feet enroute to redacted (i believe, it happened fast), the pilot in command and i were briefing a part of the arrival. i felt the aircraft start to descend, and noticed we were approximately 100 foot off our altitude and descending rapidly. i notified the pilot in command (as he was pilot flying) that we were descending. he applied power, disengaged the autopilot, and recovered the aircraft. it should be noted that the autopilot never annunciated or disengaged before the pilot in command manually disengaged it.it happened rapidly, and i estimate we lost 400 to 500 feet before recovery.i notified air traffic control that we had encountered a serious and unexpected downdraft and had lost 400 feet but were recovering.in the recovery we continued to deviate altitude based on what i believe were additional updrafts and downdrafts before finally stabilizing the aircraft at 11000 feet and reengaging the autopilot.it should be noted that there was no convective activity around us at the time, we were imc over mountainous terrain, so i assume it had something to do with wind over the mountains.we discussed if it could have been caused by an autopilot failure, but i did not believe that to be the case. the autopilot functioned normally after the event.no further information.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Fuel Issue
synopsis: A321 pilots reported a CTR FUEL TK and RT WING TK overflow ECAM messages at the gate prior to start; then were notified by ramp personnel of fuel spilling onto the ramp. The flight was deplaned and maintenance determined the cause was an aircraft malfunction.
text: after accomplishing the before start checklist, and during the accomplishment of the connecting external error checklist we got an ecam. fuel r wing tk overflow, and ctr tk r xfr pump was indicating faulted. we initially began to run the ecam but ground personnel interrupted us and informed us that fuel was leaking out of the right side of the jet. we shutdown all the fuel pumps at that time and immediately deplaned the aircraft.cause: maintenance told us it was an aircraft malfunction. the crew followed the checklist.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier crew reported GPS jamming during cruise in domestic airspace. The aircraft later regained the GPS signal and continued to the destination.
text: while enroute to phx at fl360, air traffic control was advising aircraft in the area of gps jamming. we lost both gps 1+2 50nm east of elp. i did ecam actions and qrh gps interference checklist. the flight management system downgraded to dme/dme/iru (inertial reference unit). we regained gps signal 220nm west of elp, the ecams went away. the flight management system went back to gps navigation. we continued to phx. i notified air traffic control and dispatch of gps jam.cause: this was an external issue and had nothing to do with the aircraft. this was happening to multiple aircraft in the area from what was being said on the radio.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: EMB-170 Captain reported ground crew failed to follow standard communications procedure resulted in uncommanded aircraft movement.
text: arrived at gate to find out the gate is inop. coordinated with ops for a new gate. ground crew pushed us back and gave us the clear to start. ground crew gave us the clear to start. told the first officer to start eng #1 and briefly looked at the airport diagram to see where the new gate was. after i looked back outside roughly 5 seconds later, the aircraft started rolling and i can see the tug driving away. i set the brakes. the aircraft rolled a distance of about 1-2 feet. i called the ground crew chief to come up and talk to me after we were parked at the new gate. we briefed what happened and he said that he said 'set brakes clear to start one.'i advise him that we did not hear 'set brakes' and recommended he waits for the captain to say 'brakes are set you're clear to disconnect' to avoid this happening again. he agreed and that was the end of it. no further issues.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown
synopsis: A321neo Flight Attendant reported that when the pilots cycle the seatbelt switch; there is no chime to alert that cabin takeoff is occurring.
text: the 321neo seatbelt switch doesn't chime when the pilots cycle it to alert the cabin takeoff is occurring/sterile ended. i have had over 5 flights this past year that this has occurred. the pilots said they cycled the switch each time. this could lead to injury with fas not seated during takeoff.suggestions: maintenance control check the seatbelt sign programming on 321neo.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Other / Unknown
synopsis: CRJ-900 Flight Attendant reported fellow FA failed to follow procedures with disregard to safety standards.
text: on flight, to redacted i met my partner for the first time. because she is more senior i asked her what position she would like to work and she said aft. i didn't want to work fwd but i had no choice. everything went as normally until during the taxi right before take-off i saw she was falling asleep in her jump seat. i watched for a little bit to see if she was okay but she opened her eyes looked at me for a while and continue to sleep again- on and off a few times. i continually looked to see maybe she was just on her phone but she wasn't. i'm 100% sure she was asleep. i had previously told her i didn't need her to do my announcement, so by the time we got into the air she stayed in the back. i had did snacks and the drink orders on the ground so once we could get up, i'd just have to do drinks. the flight was short, so i knew i didn't have much time. she did come to the galley once to grab a trash bag and gloves to do a trash walk then came back to put it in the bin. the flight completed as usual.the following flight from redacted is where the real issues started. the flight was now even shorter, so i did the same as the previous flight: snacks and drink orders on the ground. this time around i hadn't seen my partner fall asleep. once we got into the air i began drinks and had only completely row 1, when the flight deck called. they told me that we didn't have any steering, would have to reset on the ground or be tugged away but didn't declare an emergency. in that moment i immediately began mentally preparing for an emergency while also completely the 2nd row of drinks. as i was pouring drinks, i pulled my flight attendant device and opened the flight attendant manual to ensure my memory served me correctly in this potential emergency. before i could take the second row of drinks to the passengers the flight deck called again and stated that air traffic control is providing priority handling. the flight deck had called back to back within 2 minutes- if that. in that time i looked to see if my partner was on the phone but she wasn't anywhere to be found. i finished up my drinks and immediately began to double check the galley and cabin to secure anything that wasn't secured. the flight deck called again third time to ask for specials and give me a time update. we hadn't had any listed specials so i just relayed that message where they then told me it was 15 minutes left. once the flight deck told us the time, i finally then heard my partner respond okay into the receiver. i always keep my phone timer on so i can also be aware of time just incase. my time was aligned with their time. less than a minute later my partner came to the galley and asked me to repeat what was going on. i relayed the information to her and told her it's priority handling, so be prepared if it turns into something more. she shook her head as if she understood. she told me she missed the first two calls because she was in the bathroom but knowing that i've seen her asleep in the jumpseat and the bathroom sign not illuminated, i don't think she was telling the truth. a few minutes later the double chime sounded and i began to secure the passengers and fulfilling all my duties. she made her way back to her seat from the galley after collecting trash. before the gear could come out and the sit-down chime went off, i had locked the bathroom and was seated. she was not in her brace position but very relaxed in her seat. as we landed i did a partial announcement by stating to remain seated with the seatbelts on and personal items stowed. i didn't want to give the standard announcement because i knew the captain would make an announcement almost immediately being as though we wouldn't turn off the runway. they then told the passengers what was going on. making the taxi a bit longer than usual. once we got to the gate is when i could finally breath. i didn't want to work as fwd but i'm really glad and blessed that i did because i don't trust my partner even with her seniority to handle this situation in the manner it needs to be, let alone to be awake. i am okay just shaken up but with the events of today, i do not feel comfortable flying with her. we only have one leg tomorrow but i do not feel safe knowing how she disregards safety standards regardless of what did or did not occur.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance
synopsis: B737 MAX 9 Technician reported while troubleshooting an intermittent speed limit tape message; they noticed the AOA sensors were asymmetrical. They used a coat hangar to move the AOA vanes to level them.
text: we were working aircraft x, first officer's 'spd limit tape intermittent.' while troubleshooting message and following fault investigation manual (fim) 27-32 task and looking at live data in the maintenance pages we noticed the left and right aoa sensors were asymmetrical. we moved the left and right aoa vanes with a plastic hanger to level them. we then continued with rest of the fim task.suggestion: we should have used a ladder or stand to move the aoa vanes.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A319 facilities maintenance reported ramp agent failed to follow procedure and miss communicated intentions resulted in uncontrolled aircraft movement.
text: the event occurred on gate xx. a ramp agent (person a) and i agreed that he would push the hangar push. person a took the pushback tractor up to the plane as though he was getting it ready to be pushed out. when the time came for the push he immediately grabbed the wing walking wands and went out to assume the wing walking position. i immediately got into the pushback tractor and went through the procedures. the aircraft mechanics said they were going to let the tower know we were ready to pushback. about 10 seconds went by and the plane started to move backwards without the cradle of the pushback tractor engaged. i immediately told them to set the brakes. the pushback tractor was never engaged to the plane. i assumed that because we agreed that person a was pushing out that he did all the steps required to pushback (cradle the wheels of the plane).suggestions: whoever brings the pushback tractor to the plane should also cradle the nose gear wheels.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: GA pilot reported being advised that their ADS-B was not transmitting resulting in flying through ADS-B mandatory airspace with a malfunctioning ADS-B.
text: after the installation of a new airspeed indicator and altimeter and an annual inspection, i flew aircraft x to maintenance shop x at airport redacted and received pitot/static and transponder checks, including the transponder test specified in part 43 appendix f. the appropriate log book entry was made by the repair station when the test was completed successfully, noting a fixed pitot leak. the aircraft was then flown back to its home base.i then embarked on a long cross country flight. this flight involved instrument flight rules flight plans, there was a transition through the redacted class b airspace and a transition through multiple class c airspaces. i received vectors in all of these airspaces.the next day, i similarly made a long cross country flight, intersecting the redacted mode c veil.then a couple days later, i made a return flight to home base, intersecting the redacted mode c veil and overflying another class c airspace.in the vicinity of redacted, a center controller informed me that he was not receiving my ads-b transmissions. upon landing, i booted my global navigation satellite system (gns) - 480 into ground maintenance mode and discovered that the transponder type had been mis-set, disabling the ads-b extended squit. i corrected this setting. the transponder is a gtx-33es, controlled by a gns-480 flight management system. using publicly available sources, i confirmed that ads-b had been disabled since the transponder test, and worked on the subsequent legs after the setting was corrected.this posed a risk to aviation safety due to the operation of my aircraft in mandatory ads-b airspace without functional ads-b. the pilot user interface does not have any indication that ads-b is not functional if the unit is misconfigured.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Incursion Runway
synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported the aircraft behind them executed a touch and go maneuver while they were still on the runway.
text: while on final for rwy xx at redacted, another aircraft announced they would be doing a short approach to xx. i asked if they would be clear of me and they assured they were behind us and no factor. while rolling out after landing, my ipad alerted me to traffic on short final of rwy xx. i had my student look out the back window to see where they were, she then informed me that they have landed (while we were still trying to make taxiway 1. i cleared the runway and looked behind us and saw the other airplanes shadow passing over us, meaning that airplane had executed a touch n go while we were still on the active runway.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor with student reported experiencing smoke in the cockpit resulting in a return to the departure airport.
text: my student and i planned to conduct a pattern flight at redacted. the taxi was uneventful and runup was successful with indications within limits of the poh. we took off of runway xxl, and as soon as we were airborne, my student and i smelt burning plastic/insulation. i told my student to continue to fly while i troubleshot. my first thought was an electrical fire, so i checked the avionics and lights for heat/smoke, and i checked the co2 indicator which was turning brown. we landed after the first lap in the pattern, to where my student noticed a very small amount of smoke in the cockpit. i let tower know that we wanted a full stop to taxi back to the ramp, and that we did not need any assistance since i could not see any smoke. about 5 seconds later, thick white smoke entered the cockpit through the dash, and at that point i knew there was an engine fire, so i told the tower we would shut down the plane. at this point, we had not declared an emergency, but tower provided priority handling at their discretion. i shut the engine down, and my student and i exited the plane. after about 20 seconds, i went to the front of the plane and saw an orange fire burning from inside the engine cowling. i grabbed the fire extinguisher from the aircraft and put the fire out. after successfully putting out the fire, maintenance personnel towed the aircraft back to the hangar to inspect the aircraft. during inspection, it was discovered that a rag was the cause of the fire.to prevent this situation from happening again, although a thorough pre-flight was conducted by the student and the instructor, both parties could have looked inside the cowling for any fod.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: C182 pilot reported while entering the pattern and following another aircraft they lost sight of the other aircraft resulting in overflying the other aircraft.
text: i approached redacted for a full stop landing. while 10 and 7 miles south, i announced my position and intent on the ctaf. as i arrived in the terminal area, there was another high wing cessna in the pattern on the left downwind leg for xx. i coordinated with this pilot to enter the downwind behind them and continue for landing in the number two position. i acquired the plane's position visually and announced that as i entered the downwind behind them. i then began to configure my plane for landing and go through my checklist. at this time, the other plane must have begun its descent because when i looked back up from my checklist, i had lost visual on the plane. it's possible that the hazy air conditions may have also contributed to me losing visual. when the other plane reported that i had passed above them, i immediately re-acquired them visually, making a right turn out of the pattern and announcing my intentions. i then returned to the downwind and landed without issue. i had no further contact with the other pilot. i think the most critical issues were the haze and the difference in airspeed between the two planes with mine being faster and closing the gap between us.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: Corporate pilot reported being advised that a C172 nearly hit their parked aircraft on the ramp; the flight crew reported to the ramp to inspect their aircraft.
text: while parked on ramp a cessna 172 controlled by a student pilot on a solo flight nearly missed hitting our aircraft after a runway excursion. the pilot was able to stop the plane approximately 10-15 feet from the right wing of our aircraft. thankfully there was no damage to our aircraft. we were notified and we came to the airport to assess and assure there was no damage to our aircraft.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Ground Incursion Taxiway
synopsis: Corporate Captain reported the intersection at Taxiway Q and Lima 3 at TEB is confusing in the dark.
text: nighttime arrival into teterboro (teb) landing runway 19 turned off at l5 was instructed by tower to give way to aircraft y and pass behind and make a right turn on (l) lima taxiway and taxi and hold short of runway 19 at (q) quebec. i was following the centerline taxi lights and made a right turn on what i thought was (q) quebec but it was taxiway (l3) lima 3. i saw the runway lead on lights and then realized i had made a wrong turn and stopped immediately. i called the tower and advised i had messed up and made a wrong turn. i did not cross the hold short line. the controller asked if i crossed the hold short line and before i could answer he instructed the aircraft on a two and a half mile final to go around. he then cleared the aircraft behind him was cleared to land. the controller then instructed me to make a left turn on runway 19 and a right on (q) quebec to parking. the intersection is very confusing in the dark and that is why i stopped to receive instructions.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that the field elevation listed for TJBQ Airport is different between ACARS takeoff data and various other Jeppesen charts.
text: tjbq/bqn airfield altitude as listed on the 10-9 airport info page (revised day 4) lists airport elevation as 238 feet. acars takeoff data as of day 0 was still using an afe of 237 feet. airport elevation on various other jepp charts with revision dates prior to day 4 list airport elevation as 237 feet.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the PAPI for Runway 1R at IAD is distracting due to being on full bright at night and the brightness cannot be lowered as ATC does not have control over it.
text: the papi for runway 1r at iad is on full bright at night. we asked the tower if they could lower the brightness and they said they did not have control over the brightness. we were told that the airport authority has been notified, but nothing has been done to correct it. the extremely bright light is very distracting at night.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ATC provides different instructions each time for the RYYMN3 Arrival to BNA that conflict with instructions listed in the NOTAM.
text: i have flown the ryymn3 arrival 4 times in the last week, and despite the notam bna star nashville intl, nashville, tn. ryymn three (rnav) arrival... turnt transition not avbl or auth, " center and approach has requested us to fly the turnt transition each time and with different expectations each time: fly the transition without speed or altitude constraints, fly the transition with altitude constraint only, and fly the transition with constraints. we requested clarification each time and was given different instructions."

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation - Altitude Undershoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: EMB-505 flight crew reported a CFTT e on departure climb.
text: upon receiving departure clearance, initial departure altitude was copied and read back by the first officer as 'one zero thousand.' inadvertently 'one thousand' was written on the departure paperwork and also set in the altitude selector. it was briefed as initial departure altitude with higher expected. upon departure aural warnings sounded due to low level flight with an resolution advisory and 'five hundred' to where a climb away from terrain was commenced. departure control was contacted and the altitude was confirmed to be ten thousand which climb was commenced and the flight continued without incident.suggestions: what was heard and read back was not what was correct. the altimeter setting was checked and verified to field elevation and that should have been compared to initial departure altitude. going forward, for the initial brief, any questions about low level departure altitudes should be brought up immediately and re-contact with appropriate air traffic control facility to compare and verify.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance
synopsis: A321 pilot reported HI ENGINE VIBRATION message during departure climb. Flight returned to departure airport.
text: climbing out of 10000 feet ended up with a hi engine 2 vibration ecam redacted-redacted. discussed issue with dispatch/maintenance. parameters on engine 2 vibrations were also felt in fwd/mid cabin which prompted an overweight landing back in redacted. landed without incident and taxied to gate.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: A321 pilot reported temporary loss of aircraft control during cruise due to clear air turbulence.
text: during cruise flight at fl320 we encountered a brief period of very strong clear air turbulence. the aircraft lost approximately 500 feet of altitude and lost approximately 30 knots of air speed. air traffic control was advised and we were given a heading to fly. the auto pilot remained engaged and as we were recovering we were offered a lower altitude. to my knowledge no traffic conflict occurred.a report from air traffic control regarding the turbulence in the area would have been helpful

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter FOD
synopsis: CRJ 700 flight crew reported engine vibration during initial climb. Flight crew returned to departure airport and found blown tire during post flight.
text: the flight began as normal and uneventful. both engine starts along with taxi for takeoff were all normal with no abnormal indications. during the takeoff roll we didn't notice or feel any abnormalities beside the runway being very rough and bumpy (which is normal for redacted). after rotation and during climb out i noticed that i could feel a slight vibration from the airplane engine and looked at the vib indicator and notice it was sitting around 3.9. we initially followed immediate action items (non involved), then i called for the qrc, then captain assigned me to continue pf duties while he conducted the qrh. while we ran the checklist i asked air traffic control to level off at 12, 000 feet and stay there while we were troubleshooting. once i brought the thrust levers back to a normal 250kt cruise speed the engine vibs returned to a normal green range, we continued with the checklist and it directed us to continue with the flight while monitoring the engine vibes. we both agreed that declaring an emergency didn't seem appropriate since the engine was operating normally at lower thrust settings. we communicated with dispatch and came to the agreement to return to redacted. the rest of the flight we asked air traffic control for 'speed our discretion'. we flew back to redacted without any other abnormalities. during the landing we didn't feel anything abnormal and even during the taxi to the gate. when we arrived at the gate xx we heard a ramp truck report to ramp control that the aircraft he was looking at had a blown tire. we asked ramp to confirm if it was our aircraft he was talking about, and he confirmed it. during the walk around i saw that the inboard left main tire had blown, i also noticed dents and tire marks on the underside of the wing and flap. the engine showed indications that tire debris had entered the engine. we then notified ground control of potential fod on runway xxl and xxr.would have been helpful if someone had noticed our tire blow out during departure. we had no indications that a tire had blown.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: EMB 145 First Officer reported a fuel quantity malfunction on the EICAS and MFD. Flight continued to landing.
text: lost fuel indication on tank 2 on eicas and mfd it was accompanied by erroneous message fuel 1 lo. then it came back as tank two with a 0 fuel quantity. we requested priority handling and landed uneventfully.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Fuel Issue
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported an engine failure due to fuel starvation resulted in an off-airport landing.
text: flight purpose was to regain proficiency after not flying for several months. checked fuel quantity using sight gauges and found 2 gallons in the right tank and 5 gallons in the left tank. i expected to use about 4 gallons during the flight. other aircraft were parked at the fuel pump, so i decided to fill up after the flight.after some airwork and practice landings at another airfield, i headed home. as i was initiating the descent from 3000 msl (about 2000 agl), i got a fuel pressure warning from the dynon system. the fuel pressure indication was fluctuating widely. i decided to stay at my present altitude until within easy gliding distance of my home airport. roughly a minute later, the dynon system gave me an engine speed warning and the engine stopped.i glanced at the glide ring on the dynon system and my home airport was right on the edge. knowing that the glide ring was based on conservative glide data, i was tempted to continue to my home airport. then i thought about the reason that i had used conservative glide data (because i might encounter sinking air) and decided that a farm field nearby was a better option. after an uneventful landing in the field, i contacted a neighbor and had him bring fuel to the field. we added five gallons to each tank and i made an uneventful flight home.after getting home, i reviewed the poh. it states that the pilot should alternate between the left and right tank. i had been in the habit of setting both fuel valves to open assuming that, if one tank became empty, fuel would flow from the other one. the poh stated that is not guaranteed with both valves open. in the future, i will follow the poh recommended practice for setting the fuel valves.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported a conflict during landing roll with a construction vehicle entering the runway.
text: while doing a touch and go with a student, a car (white ford suv) associated with construction happening near the airport beacon/asos station entered the runway prior to our rotation (while we were still rolling down the runway). the car began to drive from its position just past the hold short line towards the runway we were on as we rolled past the taxiway. i advised the vehicle over the ctaf frequency that all vehicles must remain behind the hold short line while there is an aircraft on any part of the runway. the vehicle did not respond and it is unclear whether they had a radio at all because they were not making any calls regarding their movement on the airport surface. i finished the flight with my student without further event and called the safety hotline after the lesson was finished.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported a NMAC during vectors for approach resulting in a RA climb. Flight continued to a landing.
text: during arrival into boca raton airport, while being vectored for the rnav (gps) runway 5 approach by miami tracon, the aircraft was descending through approximately 2, 000 feet in compliance with an assigned altitude restriction to maintain 2, 000 feet until established on the approach. the first officer (first officer) was pilot flying (pf), and the captain was pilot monitoring (pm) handling communications. at approximately xa:53-xa:55, miami tracon issued a traffic advisory indicating traffic below the aircraft. the captain acknowledged the call and initiated a visual search for the reported traffic. shortly thereafter, the aircraft's tcas generated a traffic advisory (traffic advisory), which escalated almost immediately to a resolution advisory (resolution advisory) with the command 'climb, climb.' in response to the resolution advisory, and consistent with standard operating procedures and regulatory guidance, the flight crew immediately complied with the tcas command. control inputs were made to establish the commanded climb, maximum available thrust was applied, and vertical guidance provided by tcas was followed. the aircraft climbed to approximately 3, 100 feet (+/- 100 feet) before the tcas annunciated 'clear of conflict.' the maneuver was executed in a controlled manner, with no injuries or damage. the conflicting traffic was not visually acquired during the maneuver. subsequent post-flight review of ads-b data indicated that aircraft y was operating in the vicinity at approximately 2, 500 feet. based on available information, that aircraft appeared to be operating under visual flight rules and not in communication with miami tracon. this information is observational only and not intended to assign causation. due to the time-critical nature of the event and associated workload, the tcas resolution advisory was not communicated to air traffic control during the maneuver. air traffic control was notified via telephone after landing.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: Cessna Citation X Captain reported a lack of pressurization with the aircraft during climb. Flight crew returned to the departure airport.
text: after departure from redacted our aircraft was not pressurizing. we leveled off at 7000 feet msl and began running configuration checks. we started our apu which returned the cabin altitude to its scheduled altitude. we then took delay vectors to burn fuel for approximately 30 minutes and returned to redacted uneventfully.

anomaly: Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Wake Vortex Encounter
synopsis: BE-350 First Officer reported inflight control issues and a track deviation resulted from a wake turbulence encounter departing TUS in trail of three F-16s.
text: crew received clearance to take off runway30 approximately 5 minutes after 3 f-16s departed.pm called vr, then called positive rate and aircraft was configured appropriately. passing through 300 feet agl the crew experienced the left wing drop and the plane began to turn from the assigned departure heading of 300°. pm called out '3-0-0 departure heading' to the pf and he acknowledged while already in the process of correcting. by the time pf could regain control, the heading showed 270°. speed at that point was indicating 120 kais. pf required nearly full aileron and half rudder, while lowering the nose slightly. pf noticed the winds at the time of upset indicated 30kt from the left. once the aircraft was back on course and stable, air traffic control prompted us on our assigned 300° heading and the crew replied with their current 300° heading. no other concern or questioning arose from air traffic control.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Cessna 152 Flight Instructor reported a low altitude alert from ATC during climb. Flight crew requested a climb and was issued a radar vector.
text: i was flying with a student who has an faa atp minimum equipment list but was not current on a single engine land airplane. my student wanted to gain flight recency. i was the pilot in command and instructor on board. right after takeoff my student, was having difficulty with the comms. (we had been having issues with the comms/headsets throughout the flight). after we began our initial climbing turn, while still in vmc i got distracted and tried to troubleshoot the comms/headset issue. i was also dealing with turbulent weather during the climb out (strong up/down drafts). in hindsight, i realize that i was task saturated and that resulted in a momentarily loss of sa (situational awareness). upon initial contact with redacted [tracon], we were given a low altitude alert. it was just prior to this that i realized that we had failed to turn outbound on the redacted [vor] redacted radial per the dp (departure procedure). since we were vmc, i requested a climb and was issued a radar vector.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS)
synopsis: Part 107 UAS pilot reported flying in controlled airspace without authorization.
text: i was operating a dji mavic 3 pro under part 107 rules at location x, for a recreational photo flight. i opened my flight planning app (aloft air control) and prepared a laanc request for the redacted class c airspace. i mistakenly believed the request had been fully submitted, when in fact i had failed to press the final confirmation button. the flight lasted approximately 8 minutes at a maximum altitude of 252ft agl, i'd planned to stay at or below 200ft agl, but the additional 52ft was to account for the increasing height of the hill i flew near. the area was clear of other aircraft and bystanders. upon landing, i checked my phone and realized the laanc was still in 'draft' mode. to prevent this in the future, i have updated my pre-flight checklist to include a mandatory verification of the laanc approval text/email before takeoff.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS)
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported letting someone else fly their drone. When the UAS pilot got the drone back; they discovered the other person had flown above 400 feet and in clouds.
text: this incident happened on day 0, xa:15. it was a cloudy day with a very low 300ft ceiling. i arrived at my friend's house at around xa:10, and i decided to take my drone out while i was waiting. there is an open field in front of his house, and it is a clear-to-fly airspace for drones under 400ft, but a little close to the nearby airport's controlled airspace. after i got my potensic atom 2 drone out, a teenager approached me and asked to fly my drone, and stated he owned a dji mini series before. as i just got two newer model dji drones, i feel i no longer value this drone that much. i have altered the maximum distance to around 500m(1640ft) horizontally, and did not change the maximum altitude at 120m(400ft) before handing it to him. i saw he started the motor without any problem, and started climbing, clearing nearby objects. i turned around and went inside my friend's house to use his restroom.after 5 or 6 minutes, when i went out, i saw the drone was descending below the cloud. after he returned the drone to me, i found it was slightly wet on the hull. i checked the drone, and i found the altitude limit was lifted to the max at 800m(2625ft), and the flight log indicated a 798m(2618ft) maximum flight altitude and probably busted b airspace at my location, which was where i realized it is a clear violation for both losing vlos and busting altitude.i do understand the risks of flying uas above 400ft, especially into b airspace, and now i also know the risk of putting drones into the hands of someone you do not know. i truly regret letting an unfamiliar person operate my drone, and the lack of continuous supervision. in the future, i will not allow others to operate the aircraft without direct supervision and will never let incidents like this happen again.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: A ZLC Center trainee reported a NMAC between an air carrier and an unmanned balloon at FL330.
text: we had derelict balloons launched about 60 miles northwest of llc [vor] climbing to fl330. balloons had no transponder. we were given a position report that they were 40 miles north of llc [vor], and supposed to be stationary. approximately 2 hours later, a plane reported a balloon east of bam [vor]. aircraft x then saw the balloon at their 12 o'clock same altitude. controller turned the aircraft to the south. the pilot later reported that had they stayed on their route, the balloon would have passed within 100ft of them. there had been no update to the controllers for a couple hours, due to the fact that the balloons were assumed to still be on the boundary of oakland and salt lake 43 artcc sector.balloons should not be flown that high throughout our airspace without transponders. at the minimum there should be accurate position reports given much more frequently then 1-2 hours or until a plane spots them miles away from the location they were thought to be at.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: A ZFW Center Controller reported due to known forecast weather; traffic volume in the sectors in their area was over published limits for an extended period and insufficient staffing led to Controllers working over ten hours contrary to FAA regulations. Reporter stated due to insufficient staffing; control positions were combined creating dangerous situations.
text: staffing started a dramatic decline in the area. weather had been forecast for the okc area up to the northwest all shift long. the weather had built enough to make one gap for most trans-continental traffic east to west to funnel through a gap over irw. aircraft were diverting southwesterly around to irw and then points west and northwest. the ukw area had sectors all split off, with dsides on sector xx, xy, and xz. a handoff was put on sector xx which left 0 people in the break list for such a high stress, high volume situation. holdover overtime was used where possible, but eventually staffing declined more, with 7 positions open with 7 controllers available. this includes 2 of the mid workers that came in. we could no longer support a handoff on sector xx which absolutely needed one. the controller on sector xz asked and said he needed to have a dside, but we had no staffing to provide one. the controller on sector xy also said he needed help, but we did not have help to offer him. we had 2 rside's that were trainees, and 1 dside trainee that could not work sector xz dside as we had to combine sector xz with xa because of the lack of bodies. the traffic volume was some of the highest i have seen, especially that late in the evening. i was later informed that the command center had gone home and left us all to fend for ourselves with no outside help besides controllers to controllers. this is an insanely unacceptable situation and one of the more dangerous i've witnessed in my career. there was a lack of experience in the area. a lack of anything being done by command center. a lack of adequate staffing. extremely high and complex workload while controllers are forced to suck it up and deal with it for hours on end without breaks. controllers were put in an extremely risk heavy and dangerous position, asking and voicing their need for help and d sides, and yet we are unable to provide them with any help what so ever. the controller on sector xa, being slow but necessary to have been split off, was essentially acting as a 'handoff' or 3rd set of eyes for the sectors above them. this is totally unacceptable. the faa is constantly knowingly putting it's controllers in harms way and throwing them to the fire. late last night we entered a situation that was forecast well in advance. command center did nothing to alleviate or spread traffic out effectively and left to essentially put the entire workload on controllers that are perpetually over worked. controllers needed dsides and handoffs and yet due to staffing it wasn't possible. i am not aware of a staffing trigger that evening. we were hung out to dry last night by an administration that fully knows about these issues that occur all the time, and nothing is being done. this was a total failure of outside leadership.we cannot work hours on end sectors that have 40+ aircraft for hours on end. this was a forecast situation in which command center had en entire shift to come up with a plan better than 'let them all go through one gap and let the controllers figure it out'. any aircraft transiting the airspace down over irw heading up to the north west should've come through that gap.any aircraft diverting around the weather going to points out west or southwest, should have been routed down over adm and out into sector xz. this would even out the workload between multiple airspaces, instead of having every single east-west transcon going through one spot and intersecting 2 different centers, and 4+ sectors of airspace. then, right as we're in the thick of it, command center decides to go home. we had multiple controllers in the center here go over 10 hours last night, and almost everyone was held over and working without a break in sight. command center can stay and help try to figure something out.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Center Controller reported they lost communication with a small aircraft that descended below its assigned altitude and flew below the minimum safe altitude for terrain clearance.
text: i took the radar handoff on aircraft x from redacted [artcc] at 090. i was working other traffic waiting for that aircraft to check in when i noticed him descending. we often struggle to talk to low aircraft in this area. we've also had issues showing some aircraft up to 400 feet low in this sector recently, but when i got caught up i tried to call redacted [artcc] to check the aircraft's clearance and see if they had gone back to redacted [artcc]. it took a minute but redacted [artcc] confirmed their last clearance was 090 and they hadn't talked to him again. i tried calling the aircraft with no answer. they were still descending so i issued low altitude alerts in the blind and redacted remote communication air to ground (rcag)s. with no answer or correction i then asked am aircraft to relay the low altitude alert. i turned off my low sector xx transmitter to allow for that while working my low/hi sector xy traffic. a few minutes went by then flight data called to say aircraft x called them airborne, advising they were unable to contact me and cancelling instrument flight rules. i removed the strip and continued my session.redacted arrivals are a weak point in the sector. the redacted rcag could potentially be moved to redacted to allow for better communications with these aircraft with i believe minimal impact on the sector. if not an option then a backup emergency communications (buec) could be put at redacted instead.if no radio can be installed/relocated then we should look at a formalized procedure to work with redacted [artcc] on these arrivals where they could coordinate and provide the clearance.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Ground Equipment Issue
synopsis: A tower local controller reported they were not aware their trainee cleared an aircraft for takeoff while another aircraft was on short final landing.
text: while i was providing training, my trainee cleared aircraft x for takeoff on runway xxl with aircraft y on short final for runway xxl. i did not catch it as my attention was focused on the aircraft on extended downwind as i was worried one might turn base early and cut off someone on final. aircraft x crossed the hold bars and then stopped short of the runway edge line and asked again if they were cleared for takeoff because they just saw an aircraft land in front of them. that is when i realized that my trainee most likely forgot about the aircraft or didn't see the aircraft short final thinking he had a hole to get a departure out when he did not. the traffic was very busy especially because local 1 and 2 where combined. they were combined because we recently got new radios and there have been a lot of issues with them. the local 2 frequency was redacted.xx and out of service. with it being out of service, we did not have the option to have local 2 split off from local 1. under normal circumstances, we definitely would have had split locals during this time and had the locals been split i doubt my trainee would have made this mistake.frequency outage leading to locals being combined, when there definitely should have been split, is the biggest contributing factor to this event. my recommendations are make fixing frequencies, especially local frequencies, a much higher priority so we don't continue to keep working combined locals at a busy airport when they should be split. another recommendation is give us a 3rd tower frequency that we can use as a backup frequency if one of the tower frequencies is ots (out of service). that way one frequency outage doesn't lead us to unsafely combining locals.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Airspace Violation All Types; Conflict Airborne Conflict; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air traffic controller reported working combined positions with high complexity resulting in an aircraft entering an area below the MVA and outside of their airspace. The controller issued a climb and turn to correct the situation.
text: i was working a combined feeder and satellite sector for redacted. va (visual approach) runway xxl/ instrument landing system runway xxr was in use. with almost no notice we lost the use of runway xxr because of a tall vessel in the runway xxr approach area at approx xa:00z. this forced all ac to use runway xxl. i was vectoring all of the redacted arrivals to blend flows with the other feeder sectors, working arrivals into a satellite and working overflight ac. this is not uncommon, but it does create a heavier workload. once runway xxr reopened there was a bit of a scramble to reassign ac to the appropriate runways. i had a lot of things to do and i had released an instrument flight rules from redacted aircraft x. i am not trying to assign any blame, but things were busy and the situation was just bad in general and a lot was happening. at approx xa:35z aircraft y and aircraft z had a conflict alert (ca) in the final box. same altitude and closing, and i was honestly kind of in shock. they were same altitude and the targets were nearly merged. it was extremely distracting to say the least. aircraft x had departed redacted and was nearing the edge of the class d. he never checked in, so i had to call redacted to have them switch him. i got him, radar id'd him and put him on a heading away from the final box. i couldn't climb him yet, so i assigned a 270 and went on to the next task. aircraft a was seeking flight following to redacted and was nearby so i gave him info about pattern traffic and changed his frequency. he never read this back, then called me after to change his destination. i was having an issue with his data tag and he them went to a vfr tag on his own. he was leaving my airspace so i quickly assigned him a tag to try and get a handoff to redacted. at the same time aircraft b was looking for flight following and for some reason his tag had been terminated. i had basically 4 things going on in different corners of my airspace. i couldn't get aircraft b to tag up because of a stars flaw. aircraft a was pulling my attention away and messing with his transponder, and i was trying to sequence ac in a complicated runway config. aircraft x called my to ask for higher about 10 miles into redacted airspace. he was at 2000 in a 3000 foot mva for approximately 5 miles. i immediately coordinated with redacted and turned him back into my airspace. i then climbed him and transferred him to the appropriate sector.recommendation: this was honestly such a tense moment, and a high workload that you can pick your poison. the supervisors were helping coordinate, but stupid things were drastically making my life harder. sequencing in these instances is typically the priority, but having to call a tower to talk to the instrument flight rules they just departed, 2 separate automation issues, and an honestly terrifying proximity of 2 ac made for the right blend of distractions. the action was not on the left side of the scope, and i let an instrument flight rules get away from me to fix radar tags on 2 visual flight rules ac and sequence jets to redacted. i guess it was the straw that broke the camels back. i think the biggest problem is that we get these tall ships in the harbor and they throw the operation into disarray. there was no notice except, hey this is the last ac to xxr, make it work.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: B737 Captain reported a low altitude alert from ATC during approach. Flight crew continued the approach.
text: during vectoring to final for runway xxr a visual approach was cleared by air traffic control. pf task saturated while configuring and slowing while simultaneously descending and turning to final. pm providing timely inputs and assists, however during the process, pf descended below instrument landing system g/s (on visual approach in vmc) and simultaneously received an altitude query from air traffic control, pm observed 200' low at faf (based on instrument landing system alt). checklist and configuration completed within gates. crosswinds caused additional saturation and resulted in pm making late 1k call.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 Captain reported that the electric trim switches were inoperative during approach. Flight continued to an uneventful landing.
text: while on an intercept heading to join the xxr localizer in redacted, the autopilot was disengaged to hand fly the approach. i discovered that my electric trim switches were inoperative. i asked the first officer to test their trim switches but they were also inoperative. the autopilot had been trimming prior to disengagement, so we discussed the possibility of an auto land but decided that if the trim failed at low altitude with the ap (autopilot) on, it would present a greater risk. we proceeded to run the (ng) stabilizer trim inoperative checklist and found that the aircraft appeared to be able to manually trim. we requested priority handling as a precaution in case of further trim or flight control issues. since we were having a flight control malfunction, i elected to keep flying and had the first officer brief the fas and give a pa. we had an uneventful landing a few minutes later after concluding the checklist. we spoke with the fire commander at the gate who said the aircraft seemed fine to him, then i spoke to dispatch and we called and debriefed with the chief pilot together.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: A320 flight crew reported loss of a hydraulic system during climb phase. Crew returned to departure airport.
text: we departed the gate and had a quick taxi to xxl @ taxiway 1. the takeoff was a normal with a strong crosswind from the south. after takeoff (approx. 1000ft) an ecam appeared. hyd y rsvr lo lvl followed by i believe a ptu (power transfer unit) fault and a low pressure. we told departure that we needed to stop the climb and take care of an issue. at this time we had not declared an emergency. we leveled at 5000ft, maintained 220 kts, on a heading of 270, and the autopilot was on. the ecam was announce and we decided that i would continue flying and the pm would run the ecam. the pm went through the items instructed by the ecam. i was flying and working the radios, but i believe the ptu was turned off and possibly the yellow engine pump. after the ecam was completed and the screens were normal, the pm contacted dispatch via acars and was given a frequency so that we could have verbal communication. according to the pm communication was difficult due to poor reception. after we discussed the situation, we decided that returning to redacted was the best option. we discussed requesting priority handling and decide to do so because of the spoilers 2 and 4 being inop. after our plans were settled i requested priority handling and notified air traffic control of our intentions, souls, and fuel on board. air traffic control began vectoring us for an instrument landing system to xyc. the pm informed the fa of the situation and gave them a briefing. dispatch sent us landing distance numbers approx, 8900 feet which was well within the 10800 feet for xyc. the pm ran through the overweight landing checklist. i configured early and dropped the gear early to burn more fuel to reduce the overweight landing issue, and the flaps would be moving slower than normal. the autopilot came off at about 1000 feet. the flight controls felt spongier than normal but not so much that aircraft was difficult to control. the strong crosswind remained present. i would consider the touchdown to be smooth. the capt took the controls at 80 knots and taxied off the runway at taxiway 2 and held on taxiway 3 short of 4. emergency vehicles were behind us. we went to frequency redacted.xx where ground and emergency services were accessible. emergency service circled the aircraft and found no evidence of damage or fire. the brakes topped out at 505c on the number 1 caliper. the other were 380 to 425. we discussed our ability to taxi in but were hesitant due to the brake temp and we had been made aware that a fluid was now leaking from the belly of the aircraft. a tug arrived and we decided out of an abundance of caution that we would be towed in. this took a while. mx (maintenance) arrived and asked for the gear pins. we had trouble locating the gear pins. they asked if the aircraft taxied fine. we stated yes and since the brakes had cooled significantly, we decided to taxi it back to the gate. the aircraft was choked at the gate and the maintenance requests were sent in.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: A Citation Latitude First Officer reported a hydraulic system failure. The flight crew landed safely after a go around.
text: hydraulic system failure. complete loss of hydraulic fluid and all associated systems. we performed all the steps on the qrh for all system faults. having only emergency braking, we chose the longest practical runway. the first approach we went around for excessive crosswinds. the second approach we landed and immediately pulled the emergency brake. full actuation of the emergency brake resulted in minimal braking and the aircraft rolled approximately 4000 feet.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported a temporary GPS failure during cruise.
text: while operating flight from mmsd we experienced a loss of position on gps right quickly followed by gps left. we were cruising at fl410 and approximately 80nm east of cul vor. we advised air traffic control and requested direct to trc vor using terrestrial navigation, and notified dispatch. approximately five minutes later our gps returned to normal operation, no further issues were noted.during this event we were using the depression rings and procedures this event occurred over some of the highest terrain on our flight. all of those procedures are gps based.i'm unsure what to recommend to avoid an event of this type in the future. we saw and acted upon the scratchpad messages, checked the qrh then referenced and used the supplemental aom procedures. i would recommend adding using the pos button on the electronic flight instrument system (efis) control panel to the procedures, this would give the crew a line of position and dme reference from the ground station being referenced by the inertial reference system (irs). also we were dispatched with minimum fuel to destination landing with approximately 5, 500 ibs with a planned cruise altitude of fl410. i had 1, 000 ibs added i mention this because fuel can give a crew options.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation - Track / Heading All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported GPS jamming during cruise began approaching Pakistan and persisted for an unusually long distance.
text: cruise flight approaching pakistan the spoofing started, which is a bit sooner than normal. the normal systems that get affected were affected, including gps and ads. once we got toward europe, the problems did not go away, as they do most of the time, but persisted, including the gps clock in accuracy of 4 minutes. during the atlantic crossing, we eventually had a gross navigational error of approximately 12 miles. we also had acars messages that would not clear out, with the continued chime, such as those when receiving a new message. we finally did an ads reset which fixed that problem.it's normal to get spoofing over the middle eastern countries now, but this was much stronger than usual and started sooner than usual. we had to give our position reports via acars and we were unable to receive our ocean clearance via acars and had a resort to voice communications for it.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported experiencing GPS jamming during cruise.
text: loss of gps signal multiple times east and north of the white sands range. multiple aircraft in the area, including us, reported it to air traffic control.cause: gps jamming.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported abnormal right aileron control responses during climbout.
text: abnormal aileron control feel. during preflight, the first officer and i reviewed the logbook and noted a previously closed write-up stating: 'noticed excessive yoke movement up to 2 units without aileron response.' the write-up was discussed during the departure brief. control checks after start were normal. during departure from redacted, during departure while hand flying in moderate turbulence, the first officer noticed an abnormal aileron control feel. during right aileron input, resistance was sometimes normal, sometimes significantly lighter than normal, and at times initially normal before abruptly becoming very light. left aileron inputs were initially normal. the first officer advised me of the condition and elected to continue hand flying while we discussed what he was experiencing. i subsequently hand flew the aircraft and immediately experienced the same abnormal and inconsistent aileron control feel the first officer had described.throughout this period, the aircraft responded appropriately to all control wheel inputs. however, the feel or resistance of the ailerons was highly variable, at times heavier than normal, at times lighter, and occasionally transitioning from heavy to very light during a single control input. we elected not to use the autopilot and to continue the climb to fl300 (planned fl370) to evaluate the condition, and coordinate with dispatch and maintenance before making further decisions and determining the safest course of action. there is no published qrh procedure that directly addressed the abnormal aileron control feel. the jammed or restricted flight controls qrh was reviewed as the closest reference, although it did not precisely match the condition observed. in accordance with our plan strategy, i transferred aircraft control and radios to the first officer, who is very experienced and had a good feel for the aircraft. i contacted dispatch and maintenance control via crew phone. maintenance control stated they were not aware of known issues with the aileron system that would produce the symptoms described and advised that the aileron system does not share characteristics with elevator systems that typically experience bearing-related feel issues. no additional guidance was provided. the abnormal aileron feel persisted, remaining variable.after further discussion, and considering the current condition in combination with the recent prior closed aileron write-up, we determined that although the aircraft remained controllable, we could not ensure an adequate margin of safety to continue to destination, nor could we be confident the condition would not worsen. we notified air traffic control and elected to divert to redacted which was previously coordinated with dispatch. redacted was chosen to allow sufficient fuel burn to reach landing weight with minimal maneuvering, favorable weather, long runways, and crew familiarity. we started the apu, and initially remained at fl300/275 kias and did not change airspeed. to continue assessing controllability while burning fuel, we later descended to fl260 and further slowed to 250 kias to stay in smooth air and then later descended slowly to 16, 000. airspeed changes were then made in 5 knot increments, closely monitoring control feel with each change. the abnormal aileron feel remained variable throughout all speeds. we extended the landing gear and began configuring early to assist with fuel burn and continue evaluating controlabillity. as a precaution, we elected to limit bank angle to 15 degrees and elected to land flaps 15 to maintain higher approach speed and roll margin. the aircraft was hand flown for the remainder of the flight, as we were unsure how the autopilot might respond given the abnormal aileron control feel.below 10, 000 feet, continuous light turbulence required frequent control inputs. the aileron feel remained abnormal and variable, however, aircraft control remained effective. the non routine landing considerations qrh was completed. we requested theils runway xxc at redacted and requested arff to observe the aircraft after landing. descent and before landing checklists were completed, with continuous updates provided to the flight attendants and passengers. the landing was normal. we remained on the runway for a post landing airport rescue and firefighting (arff) inspection, no abnormalities were observed. arff accompanied us during a normal taxi to the gate. the shutdown was normal. passengers were reaccommodated onto another aircraft. after completion of the flight, both pilots discussed that we did not feel fit to continue flying. the redacted chief pilot assisted in removing us from further duty. threat and error management (tem) was used throughout the event, including the decisions to notify air traffic control, divert to redacted, restrict bank angle, slow and configure gradually, and land flaps 15 to preserve controllability and safety margin.cause: the following day i noticed a maintenance write up for this aircraft that air was suspected in the hydraulic lines. that would be a condition i believe would be consistent with what was felt on the controls. however, that was not something considered during the flight as our attention was more about safe recovery of the aircraft.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a ground conflict with another aircraft during taxi. Flight crew brought the airplane to a stop.
text: taxiing on a to 13r with instructions to hold short of mb. i heard ground give taxi clearance to an aircraft to taxi to 13r via a behind aircraft x. we were not told to give way to anyone. as we approached kf i observed aircraft y rapidly approaching a. i did not observe them slow down. i said stop stop" and the captain confirmed that he saw them and was stopping. my feet were flat on the floor but ready to apply brakes if necessary given the distance wasn't too close. we had a brief discussion about it and i was fairly certain they were supposed to give to us given there wasn't any same make aircraft anywhere near us. the captain asked ground and the active ground controller both stated aircraft y was supposed to give way to us. the event was a bit alarming given how quickly they entered a and didn't see us at all.cause: aircraft y was given an instruction to pass behind us. they did not. we stopped to avoid hitting them or more accurately to avoid having their wing hit us.suggestions: sop and communication prevented this. sop and crm on their aircraft should have prevented it."

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Inflight Event / Encounter Wake Vortex Encounter
synopsis: ERJ-170 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence at FL340 from a preceding wide body aircraft; resulting in an uncommanded bank. Flight crew immediately climbed to FL350 without a clearance to avoid the wake.
text: on flight redacted at xa16, approximately 25 miles south of airport 1m9 while on frequency 124.27. we were at cruise at flight level 340 and smooth air. there was an aircraft ahead of us approximately 12 miles at the time at 360. that aircraft started to descend into our flight path as we were both apparently heading to memphis. it seemed to be getting closer as it descended down and it was approximately 8 miles or so in lateral distance ahead of us. it was less than 1000 feet above us and continued its descent to the same altitude of 340. not knowing what type of aircraft or its call sign standing out to us. i didn't think much about it, i did make comment that it was not a company a or same type aircraft due to its strobe lights not being the same. as a descended down to about 350 or less, we got a little light chop, and i thought that that would be it as we passed through its wake or as i assumed. everything seem normal until it happened.soon after we experienced a moderate chop and then successive small rolls to the left and right, followed by a heavier role to the right greater than 30° less than 45° as we did not get a bank angle, but the auto pilot disconnected. at this time, i told the first officer to manage it and then to climb to 350 immediately and which he did. i responded to air traffic control telling them we are responding to a wake turbulence encounter and leveling at 350. the first officer over shot during the process and then descended back down to 350. we were then in smooth air at 350.i believe at this time air traffic control tells me that the traffic was a heavy airbus ahead of us about 7 miles or so leading to that situation. i contacted the flight attendants to check on their conditions and of the cabin. they responded no issues no injuries. as we continue to memphis following this aircraft, air traffic control allow us to descend with discretion so we maintained higher altitude throughout this flight all the way to landing to avoid getting in the wake turbulence. although we did experience just a little bit, but not bad on short final.once at gate and debriefed fo, i called operations about clarification if write up is required in afml (aircraft flight maintenance log) ( it is not explicit but vaguely assumed via 'severe turbulence ') i did write it up regardless. i then contacted dispatch and maintenance control and followed through the severe turbulence process with maintenance control. they stated the ap (autopilot) disconnected due to slat or aileron miscomp or something when they remotely pinged the aircraft.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Small transport flight crew reported an altitude deviation while on vectors for approach. Flight crew climbed to ATC assigned altitude and continued the approach.
text: we were flying into oak getting vectors for the instrument landing system 28r and after getting instructions to descend to 3000 shortly after air traffic control told us to immediately climb to 3400 as that was the minimum vectoring altitude and that we had been instructed to descend to 4000 not 3000. we had been instructed previously to descend to 4000 but after were instructed to descend down to 3000 so i'm not sure where the confusion happened between us and air traffic control. the only explanation i can think of is either air traffic control mistakenly told us to descend to 3000 or we mistakenly misheard an instruction to descend to 3000 which was intended for another aircraft. there was no follow up from air traffic control after the incident and we continued into oak

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: A ramp worker reported they pushed an aircraft back too close to the road as a van was driving by.
text: i was pushing a plane back at gate xx and the pilot wanted me to push deep so i kept pushing back to the point where i was about to be on the roadway and a van drove right behind me. so close that if i started the engine early, they would've felt it at full force.
