anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a ground conflict with another aircraft during taxi. Captain brought the aircraft to a stop.
text: whilst in sfo taxiing on a, abeam e, going towards runway 1r we were told to follow air carrier x. we did not see an air carrier x aircraft and decided to stop. whilst looking at my jeppesen traffic i noticed the only air carrier x traffic was behind us. just when we decided to call ground to ask for clarification ground called us and told us to expedite across the intersection (a transitioning into f). when i attempted to speed up i had to immediately stop because aircraft y came with high speed off of 28r - e - b - f. if i had followed the ground's directions we would have crashed. it was a busy day at sfo and ground was clearly busy but it was apparent that he was losing situational awareness regarding our position.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor; Ground Event / Encounter Other / Unknown
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being advised of a wheel fire during taxi. Captain stopped aircraft and was subsequently towed to gate.
text: the first officer was flying a normal approach to runway xxr. as the aircraft settled on to the runway, first officer said that the braking felt a little weird and that the aircraft was not decelerating correctly. first officer disconnected the autobrakes via brake pressure, and i said let's go to the next high speed [exit taxiway] 1 because i did not want to try and stress the brake system more. i took control of the aircraft and finished the rollout to 1, made a left turn and the aircraft brakes appeared to be grabbing, and letting go. i then made another left on to taxiway 2 and began taxing east on 2. i slowed for a second to gain a better understanding of what was going on. first officer asked if i wanted him to tell air traffic control that we were having brake problems, i asked him to hold off until we got east of the next turn off taxiway 3 going eastbound because that was a normal turn off and i wanted to get east of it before the next aircraft landed. after i past [taxiway] 3, we called air traffic control and told them we may need to taxi slowly because of brake problems. as the ground speed dropped below antiskid engagement speed, 27 mph, the aircraft began to roll normally. no more wobble, no more grabbing, so we continued.the tower asked if wanted different taxi routing because of the brake problem. i told them no, i then explained to first officer that i did want to heat the brakes up any longer on the longer route. i then said, first officer, i'm not sure what is going on so we will leave both engines running for idle speed, control and avoid braking.air traffic control immediately cleared us across runway xxl so we didn't have to stop, then taxied to 4, 5 and ramp on the bridge. i asked first officer to input an elb (electronic log book) for the anomaly and he did. as i turned on 5, first officer then got a clearance for parking via 5, 6 to the alley for gate x. i asked first officer to contact maintenance because we need to have a discussion with them and because it was an international flight, i needed them to catch us before we went on to customs. on initial contact with maintenance, they informed us we had a wheel fire, we notified ramp to dispatch arff (airport rescue and firefighting) to our location. first officer asked if i wanted to evacuate and i said no we simply did not have enough information to that. i stopped the aircraft and made an announcement to the passengers and crew and told them we were not on the gate yet, and fire rescue will be inspecting the rear tires. after a few minutes, i engaged with mx (maintenance) control and ramp to find out where the arff was on the field and an eta. numerous employees gathered and took pictures from afar, but no one could tell me if it was getting worse. i made another announcement to the pax reassuring them that we were safe and the arff would be pulling up shortly. each announcement had to be translated for our passengers by the flight attendants. i made announcements every 5-7 minutes.arff arrived and got on the ramp frequency, asked us to shut down the right engine, so they could inspect the right wheels, we complied. the left engine was still running, the apu was running. first officer asked about shutting down the left engine, we did, and now the packs were running off the apu bleed air. we spoke with arff on ramp frequency for a minute and no one said an active fire was present. as we sat there for about 5 minutes, no communication with arff, they elected to spray fire retardant on the brakes, 1st the right side, then the left side brakes. this forced smoke and fumes into the cabin because the retardant struck the hot brakes, formed a smoke and the south wind blew it right into the pack intake system. as soon as it happened i reached up and turned off the packs, and made an announcement to the passengers and crew to remain seated. i later found out the flight attendants were getting ready to evacuate until they heard my announcement. this whole sequence of events took less than 20 seconds.i called mx on radio one and notified them i was no longer communicating with arff and that they just created a problem with smoke in the cabin. poor communications between arff and the crew.then arff told me to taxi into the gate, i told first officer to tell them mx would be towing us, both engines were shut off. after a few minutes, i elected to turn the packs back on, made an announcement and asked the passengers to be patient.numerous vehicles airport ops, mx, baggage handlers, police, etc., were around the aircraft, but no one was telling me about an active fire. then mx showed up and requested that i through down the gear pins. right then i knew we were not on fire, and mx was going to set the gear pins for pull in to the gate. again, no verbal confirmation from anyone.ground personnel finally showed up, some frequency communication problems with them, then they pulled us into the gate about :40 total time from the fire notification by mx (camera - not sure how they knew) and in at the gate. the passenger deplaned, i contacted mx again and requested a face-to-face with someone so i could give them a quick debrief. someone came up, took my statement. i was informed right then… for the 1st time by the mx guy that we did not have a fire, only the hub cap melted. good thing we didn't evacuate on just a report of a fire and not confirmation. i wanted to go down to the ramp but customs had not released the aircraft yet. first officer and i proceeded to customs, cleared customs got on the bus and called the chief pilot from the employee parking lot.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a GPWS Glideslope warning during approach. Crew stabilized approach and continued to a landing.
text: when we were assigned the vunox1a arrival, air traffic control gave us further direct points on the arrival. near gr259, we were cleared direct to the sampa intersection. before reaching sampa, we were cleared direct to lomen (the final fix on the arrival) and assigned 6, 000 feet as the final altitude.during the arrival, when air traffic control issued a clearance, they used the word 'via' for direct sampa. this led to some confusion on the flight deck. i verified with the controller what he meant, and he clarified that he wanted us at sampa at 6, 000 feet. we rectified the situation, though the phrasing was non-standard.before reaching lomen, air traffic control cleared us for the instrument landing system 10l approach. at this point, we were slightly higher than the glideslope, and i noticed that the first officer had not armed approach mode on the mode control panel (mcp). i informed him that we were cleared for the approach and prompted him to arm the approach button.by the time this was completed, he became preoccupied with the high altitude, he selected flch and dialed 3, 000 feet in the mcp altitude window. before i could warn him, he disconnected the autopilot and decided to follow the flight director (fd), which was providing incorrect guidance at that moment.consequently, we received a gpws 'glideslope' alert. i told him, 'you need to go up, you need to capture that glideslope, ' as i noticed he was below the slope and continuing to pitch the nose down.we were stabilized by 800 feet resolution advisory and completed the landing checklist. the weather was vmc, the field was in sight, and the glideslope was captured. despite the instability prior to the 1, 000-foot agl stable approach gate, i decided not to call for a go-around, as i felt it would have caused further confusion in the cockpit. we landed without further issues and discussed the event during the van ride.cause: one of the contributing factors to this event was the fatigue. even though we all felt fine at the beginning of the flight, with rolling delays for a couple days, ever changing departure times and multiple long delay made things a bit harder on us.suggestions: we were delayed due to aircraft maintenance, which caused rolling delays. i woke up on my own for the early departure, but there was no wake-up call.when i called dispatch, they told me they were having customs issues. nobody updated the departure time until we were on the plane. once we boarded, there was no ground crew available to load the aircraft, which caused further delays. eventually, we were delayed by almost four hours, which contributed to our fatigue.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported GPS jamming during cruise flight. GPS system returned to normal and flight continued.
text: shortly after reaching cruise at fl410, approximately 80nm east of the cul vor, we received a message r-gps invalid, and shortly thereafter a l-gps invalid, which was confirmed on flight management computer page 2 as blank lat/longs for both positions. we referenced the qrh, notified air traffic control and requested direct to the trc navaid for which we were getting good navaid reception. after approximately 5 min both gps returned and we resumed rnav navigation.cause: we suspected possible gps jamming operations. likely it would be best to route traffic away from known interference events. also, additional fuel should be planned to allow for the longer path navaid-to-navaid vs rnav -direct.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that while climbing through 2;500 feet; ATC alerted them of traffic at their 11:00 position and 3;000 feet. They got an RA to descend and took evasive action to avoid a possible collision.
text: after departing runway 07 on the litra1d departure climbing through 2500' we were alerted to traffic by goldson radar. traffic was reported to be at our 11:00 position and 3, 000 feet. at the time the traffic was reported we were imc in a cloud. shortly after the report aircraft y showed up as a primary target at +200 feet and course converging. about one second after that, we were clear of the cloud, i got visual contact with the converging aircraft and simultaneously we received an resolution advisory to descend. the proper resolution advisory maneuver was performed by the first officer with appropriate very aggressive flight control pressure to initiate the descent and avoid the collision. we recovered from the maneuver at approximately 1900 feet. negative g forces were felt in the cabin as reported by the cabin crewcause: goldson radar should not have cleared aircraft y to cross the rnav departure course at an altitude that conflicted with the charted altitudes on the departure

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Inflight Event / Encounter Unstabilized Approach; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported GPS jamming during cruise and approach phase; which caused the RNAV approach to be unusable; requiring approach and landing on runway with tailwind.
text: enroute to abq i had the colter4 arrival loaded and the rnav (rnp) 26 approach loaded into the flight management system. abq atis was calling winds 260/08 and rnav 26 in use. we checked in with zabq and were not given any other information other than got you check in". several other aircraft checked in with zabq and then center stared letting people know "whites sand is testing gps and ads-b jamming." as we started setting up for the arrival and rnav i noted we had high accuracy on the prog page, however we had zero satellites and no gps signal. we asked zabq how people are doing the rnav app road into abq with no gps and he said to do the rnav visual. we said we're not doing a night visual around mountains. we asked for an early switch to abq approach to see what other people are doing. switching to abq approach two aircraft were in the same predicament we were in. one aircraft elected to do the instrument landing system runway 8. they noted a 30kt tailwind until 300 feet agl then a 5 kt tailwind at touch down. at this point we only had about 7, 000 of fuel and no listed divert. the second aircraft did the same instrument landing system 8 approach and reported them same. i elected to do the same. we briefed the approach and i briefed the first officer. we flew the approach as advertised at 300 get the tail wind died off. this caused our indicated airspeed to jump about 10kts at 300 for a brief moment the. quickly captured back to on speed. landed and taxi in was uneventful.cause: wsmr (white sands missile range) regularly conducts jamming. if this is known ahead of time we should add fuel and an alternate for a situation where the only approach to the runway in gps. center and approach control need to communicate better to each other and aircraft inbound. center seemed to not think this was a big deal, approach was overworked with four inbound aircraft all unable to shoot the approach do to jamming, weather and all other runways beside 08/26 being closed."

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter Fuel Issue
synopsis: ERJ175 First Officer reported that after takeoff; they received a flap fail indication and other caution messages. Flight crew attempted to run the QRH; but was unable to clear any messages. They decided to divert due to unreliable fuel.
text: we departed redacted en route and immediately received a flap fail. we quickly received other caution messages, including windshear detection fail, speed brake fail, aoa limit fail, etc. after attemping to run the qrh procedures, we were unable to clear any messages. i requested that we return to redacted, but the ca used his authority to continue us to destination. we notified dispatch, they approved, and we continued. en route our landing fuel became unreliable, so we made the decision to divert to redacted. we landed without incident. cause: the cause of the event was due to airplane automation error.suggestions: i believe that to avoid this recurrence in the future, if we were unable to clear the caution messages that we should've returned to redacted as a precaution as opposed to continuing on the flight.

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Crossing Restriction Not Met; Deviation - Altitude Overshoot; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a CFTT event occurred during approach. Crew corrected altitude and continued approach.
text: we were cleared for the rnav xx approach to redacted by redacted center. the tower was closed. after passing fix redacted began descent from 3200 to 2000 as published. i was slowing and configuring per non-precision profile. i was fully configured by 3mi from faf(redacted). i chose to set the missed approach altitude but did not notice we had not altitude select (alts) capped 2000. we continued descending approximately 800fpm. the captain saw the deviation about 1700ft and called altitude, i said correcting. we climbed back to the 2000ft published altitude prior to the faf and then began normal descent to the runway. no further problems. the cause was my setting the missed approach altitude prior to alts capping the published altitude and not recognizing. due to terrain the altitude change between segments on the approach is larger than no terrain areas and my feel for elapsed time was off for the altitude change compared to other non-precisions i have done. i did not verify the alts cap. from the start of the approach thing had progressed nicely and i got lulled into a complacency after we got fully configured.suggestions: this is a sobering lesson knowing we were so close to the ground and i put us into a premature descent unknowingly. and only the captain recognized it. this will stay with me for a long time. i know to make sure we have captured an altitude before spinning the knob. take a moment to be sure it's the correct timing for the input.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported on takeoff roll experiencing the aircraft veering hard to the left resulting in the flight crew rejecting the takeoff and returning to the gate.
text: during takeoff roll on runway xx the aircraft started to veer hard to the left. i applied full right rudder and the airplane continued to veer hard to the left. determining i could not retain positive control of the aircraft i decided to reject the takeoff between 10-20 kts. and we exited the runway at taxiway 1. we requested to go to the hold bay of runway xy, while taxiing i had to steer the plane to the right because the nose wheel was taking us to the left. once there i set the parking break and had the first officer complete the rejected takeoff checklist. after the checklist i called maintenance, they instructed us to return to the gate and deplane. there was a right up from earlier in the day about the nose wheel veering to the left. no further incident occurred.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: B737 First Officer reported during landing roll experiencing a braking issue resulting in a brake fire during the taxi to the gate.
text: i was flying a normal approach to runway xxr. as the aircraft touched down on the runway, i observed slower than expected deceleration. i manually disengaged the autobrakes and immediately noted a lack of braking response. i notified the captain, who took control of the aircraft at approximately 80 knots. during the turnoff, the same braking issue was observed. once on taxiway fa i advised air traffic control that we might need to taxi slowly due to the braking issue. air traffic control offered an alternate taxi route to avoid stopping and crossing an active runway. once established on the taxiway, brake performance returned to normal. after clearing the runway xxl, i completed and submitted an electronic log book entry and contacted maintenance control to report the issue and request that a mechanic meet the aircraft at the gate for further evaluation.approximately 30 seconds after contacting maintenance, the anti-skid inop light illuminated. shortly thereafter, we were advised by either ramp personnel or maintenance that the brakes were reportedly on fire. at that time, we were approximately 100 feet short of the gate. due to the potential fire hazard, we elected to stop the aircraft on the ramp rather than proceed to the gate.i immediately requested fire and rescue. there was a delay in their arrival, estimated at approximately 5-10 minutes. during this time, we maintained communication with ground personnel, the flight attendants, and passengers.both engines were shut down at the request of fire and rescue personnel. fire and rescue approached the aircraft and initially reported no visible fire. shortly thereafter, they began applying fire retardant to the brake area without prior coordination. as a result, fumes entered the cabin. upon recognizing this, we promptly shut down both packs to mitigate further cabin contamination.throughout the event, there appeared to be a lack of coordinated communication between operations, ramp, and maintenance, which contributed to confusion and increased workload in an already time-critical situation.a tug was eventually dispatched, and the aircraft was towed to the gate without further incident.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Weight And Balance; Flight Deck / Cabin / Aircraft Event Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor
synopsis: B787 Captain reported experiencing electrical smell during the climb; resulting in the flight crew returning to the departure airport where they landed safely.
text: climbing through approximately fl190 electrical smell through out aircraft.all crew members on flight deck in jumpseat confirmed.relief pilot first officer entered the cabin to inspect w/ relief pilot capt who was riding in cabin.all crew members in cabin confirmed electrical smell.passengers also aware. not dissipating but also not increasing in intensity.requested return to redacted initially from redacted [artcc] but not understood so requested priority handling. air traffic control initiated vectors for return.congested airspace with many aircraft above and below so requested permission to dump fuel.air traffic control vectored again and then approved fuel dump. max landing weight selected for dump.dump completed in 1 and 1/2 turns in hold.after dump completed landing weight showed 1200lbs above max landing weight. chose not to run again.overweight landing. gross weight 426200lbsexited hold with vectors to land xxc redacted.landed and exited runway, cleared and stopped on adjacent taxi way for exterior inspection by airport rescue and firefighting (arff).aircraft cleared by arff and taxied to gate followed by arff interior inspection.passengers off loaded.worked with maintenance and maintenance control for eventual (individual) engine run at gate.

synopsis: Citation Longitude flight crew reported experiencing a left engine vibration; and engine temperature exceedance; followed by an automatic engine shutdown. Flight crew diverted to a nearby airport.
text: in cruise at fl430 east of city x we observed an aircraft vibration. after about 20 seconds we observed an engine vibration l amber cas message and a short time later a left engine itt (interstage turbine temperature) exceedance followed by the left engine shutting down uncommanded. we diverted to redacted (original destination redacted) completed a normal landing and had the aircraft towed from the runway to the fbo.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported concerns with GPS jamming during cruise. Jamming ceased and flight continued.
text: during cruise flight, our gps capability was jammed. while running the qrh checklist, we informed air traffic control of our gps issue and i asked if white sands was jamming gps signals in our vicinity. air traffic control checked, confirmed they were, and several other commercial aircraft stated on our frequency they were also having gps issues. anticipating landing runway 30 at tus, i noted the only instrument approaches for runway 30 were rnavs. as a precaution, i contacted dispatch and requested they add phx as an alternate (phx landing runway had ground-based instrument landing system approaches). our gps reception was restored about 10 miles east of waypoint jokim, the final waypoint on the assigned zonna star. as the result of restored gps capability, we were able to execute a safe approach. my concern is gps jamming by our government with no advance notice unnecessarily reduces the safety margin. with mountainous terrain and davis monthan airbase nearby, which can and has been mistaken for tus, having to conduct a visual approach at night to an unfamiliar airfield unnecessarily complex. if we experienced a non normal requiring a divert to an area being jammed, the gps jamming may have precluded a safe approach from being made. is disabling commercial aircraft gps capability necessary and wise?cause: the causal factor was our aircraft gps capability being jammed by white sands. my recommendation is don't jam commercial aircraft gps capability. if our government must jam gps signal, duration must be the shortest possible timeframe and commercial aircraft should be routed so as their flight path will not be impacted by the jamming.

anomaly: Ground Event / Encounter Other / Unknown; No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported landing on Runway 17L at DFW and feeling that a slight porpoise or bounce had occurred; which the reporter stated may have been caused by the concrete becoming deformed due to environmental conditions.
text: this is a general safety report. i was pf flying runway 17l at dfw on this leg. my captain on my flight had warned me at cruise that only a few weeks prior, they and a different first officer on another sequence were called regarding either a hard or bounced landing on runway 17l at dfw. further investigation yielded information indicating that the runway pavement itself is likely the issue here. i was ready for it, and landed per company and faa requirements (descent rate, within tdz, etc.) and no event nor write up was issued on my landing. that is, by every standard, my landing was normal." however, about 2 - 3 seconds after touching down on 17l just beyond the 1000-foot blocks, it felt like an uncommanded, undesired slight porpoise / bounce occurred. had i landed slightly longer or carried extra energy into the flare and rollout, this could have yielded a serious safety concern. another company aircraft landing right behind us reported the same thing. i believe an issue with the concrete within the tdz of 17l is developing that needs immediate addressing by the airport and faa. our flight was completed normally without any need for maintenance action, calls, nor any other required report. this report is being submitted for informational purposes only.i'm not an engineer, however, i understand the difficulties that even the roadway engineering departments experience due to our extreme heat and moisture swings (one year drought, followed by torrential rains). it is my educated guess that the runway tdz on 17l is somehow warping or that the concrete has become / is becoming deformed due to environmental conditions. i think that this requires action to prevent further degradation of the concrete and to avoid safety of flight issues for all aircraft."

anomaly: Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Clearance; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported descending below MSA during approach. Crew corrected and continued approach.
text: on base for runway xxr outside of redacted. air traffic control clearance was to descend to 8000. then maintain 8000 until established on the localizer cleared instrument landing system xxr. the plane was still outside of redacted. first officer spun in 7000 (faf altitude). the plane descended to 7000 while established on loc but still outside of redacted. air traffic control informed us msa in the area was 7500. we climbed back up to 7500 and captured the glidepath from there. landed without further event. cause: air traffic control descended us to 8000 outside of redacted. minimum alt at redacted is 9000 feet. we were established on the localizer and descended to the faf altitude of 7000 while still outside of redacted because of the clearance (maintain 8000 until established on the localizer)suggestions: let the airplane capture the assigned altitude before continuing to path to the faf altitude.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported finding a passenger door handle 'popped' during cruise. Flight landed safely at the destination.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Maintenance; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy
synopsis: Air carrier Technician reported after installing the nose landing gear upper torque link on an EMB-145; they adjusted the weight on wheels sensor gap. On the first flight the nose landing would not retract.
text: i was tasked with installing a upper torque link on a nlg leg. the gear was to be installed on aircraft x. the upper torque link on the new gear had been previously canned for use on another aircraft. i was to install the upper torque link while the damaged nlg leg was being removed from aircraft x. i installed the upper torque link in accordance with emb145 aircraft maintenance manual (amm) task redacted. after installation i checked the gap of the nlg wow proximity sensor. i found it to be incorrect. i adjusted the gap in accordance with emb145 amm task xxxxxxxxxxxxy. i set the gap to a few thousandths above the minimum of (.052). to achieve this gap the target for the sensor had to be slightly fwd of center for the nlg wow sensor. as compared to the rest of the fleet this is not an uncommon condition. after the installation of the new gear all operational and leak checks were complied with. no defects were detected or found. i preformed numerous additional gear swings not required per the maintenance manual. i make a habit of doing this after a gear change as an extra level of safety. if there is any problem with the extension and retraction system it needs to be known. aircraft x was released two days later and went to the gate. after takeoff the gear failed to retract. the nlg wow sensor gap was determined to be the cause for the gear not retracting.i have adjusted many wow proximity switches on the emb-145 using both methods with no issues. i am not really sure how this problem with the sensor adjustment occurred. i rechecked the gap after i completed the adjustment and it still measured good.suggestion: although i would think that the results should be the same. there are two different procedures for adjusting gear proximity switches. possibly one procedure is more accurate then the other.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical
synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor with student reported complete electrical failure during pattern work. Flight continued to landing.
text: while doing pattern work at redacted with a student, we were on short final during one of the laps when we started hearing a loud clicking/static noise in the headsets. right after that, the garmin 650 started flickering and then shut off, followed by the audio panel and radios, resulting in a loss of all communications. at the same time, basically all electrical equipment went offline except the two g5s, which stayed on in reversionary mode. i checked the breakers and saw the alternator breaker was popped. since this all happened on short final, i went around to avoid rushing the landing and to troubleshoot what was going on. in the climb, i reset the alternator breaker once and recycled the electrical, but nothing came back and we still had no radios. at that point, it was a full electrical failure, so i decided to come in for a full-stop landing. after shutdown, we reported it to maintenance. there were no prior indications of a problem earlier in the flight, we had flown from redacted, completed multiple maneuvers, and then proceeded to redacted for pattern work. the issue was likely caused by an alternator, voltage regulator, or wiring failure, as indicated by the tripped alternator breaker and total loss of electrical systems. the clicking noise and flickering display suggest an electrical fault prior to complete failure. prevention would include proper inspection of the alternator, regulator, and wiring, along with early recognition of electrical issues

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Less Severe; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported during final approach an air carrier was landing same runway opposite direction. Pilot performed a go-around.
text: took off from redacted on runway xx and departed towards redacted. no other planes were flying at redacted so there was no way to test radios other than a squelch test. squelch test was fine and all checklist items were covered before departure. made all radio calls coming towards redacted and chose to use runway xy due to calm winds. as soon as we turned final, we noticed a jet flaring on runway xz coming straight at us. at that time we executed a go around and banked out to the right. we could not hear them on our com 1 as the volume was very low and the squelch had been audible due to idle power settings. as soon as we noticed the problem, we switched over to com 2 to test our radio and alerted the jet of the issue.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported being cleared by Tower for takeoff while there was an aircraft on short final approach. Pilot stopped aircraft to avoid collision.
text: after landing at vqq from the rnav 09r approach, aircraft x taxis out from runway 09r. controller requested what aircraft x's intentions were while exiting, aircraft x requests a taxi back to runway 09r and pick up of instrument flight rules clearance back to redacted. controller gave aircraft x a 180-degree turn and hold-short-of-runway 09r instruction, then a frequency change to ground control. aircraft x received instrument flight rules clearance from ground control. upon completion of the checklist aircraft x, called in tower controller, ready for departure and holding short of runway 09r. tower cleared aircraft x to take off runway 09r. aircraft x repeated clearance back and realized another aircraft, aircraft y, was on final at 300 ft and continuing to descend for runway 09r while aircraft x was expecting the other aircraft to execute a missed or a go around. pilot in command took flight control and stopped aircraft x just beyond the hold-short line and advised tower of the aircraft landing as aircraft x was cleared to take off. at this point, tower called the canceled takeoff clearance. aircraft x was approximately 100 feet from landing aircraft y.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Small aircraft flight instructor reported an NMAC during climb. Flight continued.
text: my student and i were departing runway 21r at pdk for a north departure. while we were in the upwind, tower had cleared aircraft y for takeoff on 21l and instructed them to turn to a 320 heading. because of the closely spaced parallel runways, i was watching my student to make sure we were maintaining the centerline of 21r on the climb out. we were following a aircraft in the crosswind turning downwind when tower asked if we had them in sight. i said that we had traffic in sight, and we were instructed to turn outside of them to depart the area to the north. as we were turning crosswind, tower asked aircraft y if they had us in sight. the crew said no. at this point, i saw aircraft y turning towards us, at our altitude, and climbing on our gtn display. i grabbed the controls to level off from our climb. tower then told aircraft y they were going to cross on top of us by 200' and to go to approach. the crew never said if they received a traffic advisory or resolution advisory, nor did they say they had us in sight. then tower called us to let us know that aircraft y would cross above us and to continue on course. i believe this event could have been prevented with better communication. based on listening to the transmissions, tower did not warn either of us about each other until the event was happening. i think tower could have instructed aircraft y to look for us sooner, or that he would call their turn to heading 320. i think tower could have told us to maintain at or below a certain altitude until the jet passed, or to turn an early crosswind and turn outside of the aircraft to the north.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: Small aircraft instructor reported an NMAC while on final approach. Flight initiated a go-around and returned to departure airport.
text: aircraft x departed for the purpose of landings at x04, multiple touch and goes were conducted with proper radio calls prior to the incident.on the pattern that the incident occurred, aircraft x turned crosswind to downwind as standard, flaps were applied to slow down to allow an aircraft to joining the 45 midfield left downwind to runway 33, as well as a downwind extension of approximately 2 miles instead of the standard 1 mile to follow the traffic, once established on final, <300 feet aircraft y turned his base leg in an attempt to complete a short approach. no radio calls were heard from aircraft y during their attempted maneuver. as aircraft y turned his final, they descended above aircraft x as in an aggressive overtake maneuver. aircraft x had right of way per 91.113.i do not believe aircraft y had aircraft x in sight at any point of the attempted landing, ads-b was a factor here as well as both aircraft were equipped with mode s transponders. a go-around was initiated as a result of the incident from aircraft x for safety as well as a termination of the flight direct back to departure airport.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported taking evasive action from conflicting aircraft without ADS-B resulted in a NMAC.
text: i am a student in cfi training, and i was out today with my instructor in our school's piper archer iii practicing maneuvers with me acting as pilot in command. after the completion of our maneuvers, i set us up to fly back to our home airport, so i positioned the aircraft on a south bound heading. as we were flying that cardinal direction for a few minutes, i noticed what appeared at first to be a large bird cutting very rapidly diagonally across my 11 o'clock position. i instinctively banked right around 20-30 degrees to avoid it, and it was only then that i realized that it was an aircraft. my instructor at the time was distracted, but once i got their attention we both were pretty stunned, as we could still see the aircraft flying behind us now once i straightened out the bank. it looked to be a similar sized plane to ours.we checked our plane's multi-function display (mfd) as well as foreflight and did not see this plane on our radar, and so there were no near collision alerts given to us. i was tuned in to the local unicom frequency for the area, but we did not hear any calls from the other pilot about positioning. we definitely would have been within 500 feet from each other and at the same altitude, my best guess would be around 300/400ft. once i entered the delta airspace of our home airport and was set up in the left downwind, my instructor visibly noticed that that same plane was on final approach, and once i looked again at my plane's mfd it was at that point we saw them appearing on our radar. so it looks like they have ads-b capabilities, but it may not be functioning correctly all the time. they landed a lot quicker than we did as i had to extend my downwind for traffic, but i wish i had found that pilot and gotten their contact information after the fact.

anomaly: Conflict Ground Conflict; Critical
synopsis: Flight instructor reported departing runway with student resulting in a possible go-around for an aircraft on final.
text: my student and i were holding short of runway xx at redacted airport. there was an aircraft in the pattern that we were aware of (aircraft y). when aircraft y made their base call i looked down final and saw him turning base as well as confirming what i saw with ads-b in. i told my student it was ok to take runway xx for immediate departure to the south back to redacted. we thought aircraft y would have time to land after our takeoff. i made the radio call saying we were departing runway xx for a southbound departure. when on the roll, aircraft y came on frequency and said 'whatever guy just took runway xx, you have aircraft y on short final and you need to report this!!'. we are unsure if he went around but assume he did because of what he said to us. we stayed on the departure leg until 1000 feet and during the climb out made a radio call saying we were making our southbound turn to depart. overall, i should not have told my student to takeoff and should have waited until aircraft y did their touch and go for us to depart.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Inflight Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence
synopsis: C-172 flight instructor reported experiencing strong winds and thermal effects during practice maneuvers resulting in an altitude deviation.
text: on day 0, the student pilot and instructor took off for the purpose of conducting training for the student's private pilot license. the training content for the day was to practice ground reference maneuvers, specifically turns around a point. this was the first training iteration for ground reference maneuvers for the student and as such the instructor briefed that a demonstration of the maneuver would be conducted before the applicant was afforded an opportunity. as the instructor and student neared the practice area the instructor assumed the role of pilot flying and began to demonstrate the maneuver. in an effort to demonstrate the maneuver in the entirety of the envelope as dictated by the acs (airman certification standards) (600-1000ft agl) and showcase the effect of wind during the maneuver at different altitudes, the instructor began the maneuver at the bottom of the altitude envelope. as the instructor was descending to the bottom of the envelope, thermal effects and strong wind conditions began to upset the aircraft and while the instructor was correcting these effects the aircraft temporarily descended below 500' agl as indicated by the instructors efb. the instructor immediately recovered the aircraft above 500' agl and all subsequent operations were conducted within the performance standards as governed by the private pilot airplane acs and far 91.113.

anomaly: Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Taxiway
synopsis: Cessna Caravan 208B pilot reported a runway excursion after landing. Pilot continued to parking.
text: while landing on runway xx redacted, my left main wheel went over the yellow line on taxiway 1, while taxiing off the runway. the left main wheel went on the grass. there was a trail of grass ripped up. no taxiway or runway lights were damaged. there was no damage to the plane, caravan 208b. i had maintenance look at the main wheel and tire, no further action was needed. this event occurred, primarily due to a quartering tailwind and possibly newer equipment being installed on the plane.

anomaly: Airspace Violation All Types; Conflict NMAC; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported an NMAC with a UAS during climb.
text: during enroute climb from bfl heading southeast, approximately 4.3 nm magnetic bearing 121 from bfl, we encountered a red and white fixed-wing drone at 4, 900 feet traveling roughly the opposite direction. it crossed from east to west across our path at approximately the same altitude. its closest distance to our plane was approximately 80 feet. unknown brand or markings. the drone did not appear on ads-b 1090 or 978 frequencies.

anomaly: Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Event / Encounter Weather / Turbulence; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: LSA pilot reported loss of control on landing due to quartering tailwind resulting in a runway excursion.
text: during a landing rollout on runway xx at redacted, the aircraft encountered a localized, quartering tailwind gust that was not reflected in the previous awos report. despite following established traffic, the aircraft experienced significant directional instability shortly after touchdown.the combination of the high groundspeed from the tailwind and the lsa's free-castering nosewheel led to a diverging yaw that could not be corrected with full rudder deflection or differential braking. recognizing that a high-energy ground loop on the asphalt was imminent, i utilized my pilot in command authority to make a deliberate, proactive transition off the pavement and onto the wide, level grass adjacent to the runway. this choice utilized the grass's lower lateral friction and higher rolling resistance to stabilize the aircraft. the aircraft was brought to a safe, controlled stop on the grass with no damage or injuries.human factors & contributing factors:environmental: rapidly deteriorating surface conditions were confirmed by metars showing a 70-degree wind shift in just 20 minutes (from 130° at 08kt to 200° at 11kt), transitioning the runway from a headwind to a quartering tailwind while i was in the pattern.herd mentality: i initially deferred to the 'de facto' runway in use by other aircraft (two landed just before me) rather than independently verifying the current windsock indication during the final approach.aircraft design: the light wing loading and free-castering nosewheel make it sensitive to 'tripping' or pivoting on high-friction pavement during a tailwind-induced swerve.corrective actions & lessons learned:personal minimums: i have established a new personal minimum of a zero-tailwind component for this aircraft due to the narrow safety margins it provides during rollout in such conditions.checklist revision: i have modified my short-final flow to include a mandatory visual verification of the windsock to ensure surface conditions match my expectations, regardless of radio traffic, 'runway in use', or awos.safety training: my previous tailwheel transition training was critical in recognizing the point of 'no return' on the pavement and choosing the more forgiving grass surface to dissipate energy safely.systemic recommendation:it is recommended that lsa manufacturers and flight/transition training providers include specific warnings in the pilot's operating handbook (poh) and flight training supplements regarding the hazards of tailwind landings in these aircraft. documentation should explicitly address how light wing loading and castering nosewheels can lead to rapid loss of directional control on pavement, which may not be intuitive to pilots transitioning from heavier ga aircraft.

anomaly: Aircraft Equipment Problem Critical; Deviation - Altitude Excursion From Assigned Altitude
synopsis: BD-700 Captain reported a dual pressurization pack failure resulted in expeditious descent and return to departure airport.
text: on a maintenance flight, we took off and climbed to fl490 as discussed with control. after two minutes in cruise, the right pack failed. a few seconds later, the left pack failed, and cabin altitude rose rapidly. immediately, i told my copilot to put his oxygen mask on as i was donning mine and to request priority handling for the descent. he requested priority handling. air traffic control asked if fl370 would be adequate as i started a descent. the dual pack failure checklist was started once we were configured in the descent. in the lower 40, 000s, the red cabin altitude warning light came on. shortly after the warning light, both the packs were reset. the cabin altitude started to stabilize and reverse the trend. we descended to fl370 and stabilized the aircraft. the cabin altitude came back into a normal range shortly after leveling off, and we had a normal return to redacted.

anomaly: Conflict NMAC
synopsis: PA-28 instructor reported on touch and go; a C-172 on a go around failed to side step resulted in traffic directly above them.
text: was doing a routine traffic pattern flight at redacted runway xx, we performed a touch and go and a trailing c172 behind the pa28 executed a go around while the pa28 also did a touch and go. looking on foreflight, as the pa28 was about to turn crosswind, their ipad flashed 'traffic' and looked down and saw an aircraft directly above them. the c172 did not perform the aim (aeronautical information manual) procedure to side step on a go-around and continued to climb directly above the pa28. the pa28 momentarily leveled off the climb once obtaining visual of the aircraft executing the go-around and continued to land as normal.

anomaly: Ground Event / Encounter Loss Of Aircraft Control; Ground Excursion Runway
synopsis: PA28-151 instructor reported student tried to exit runway with excessive speed resulted in a runway excursion with loss of control.
text: on day 0 around xa:50 (local), while on landing on runway xx, my student and i were taxiing off of runway xx at [taxiway] 1 and the taxi speed was too fast and there was not enough differential breaking to the left, as i attempted to take controls, we ended up in the grass. i called tower to let them know, they asked if i could move, i said yes, then i proceeded to taxi off the grass back on to 1. i called ground, got cleared to taxi back to the south ramp. as a corrective action, i will guard the controls, take evasive action quickly and effectively coach students on how to taxi off the runway at the speed of a brisk walk.

anomaly: Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural FAR; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Unauthorized Flight Operations (UAS); No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation
synopsis: Recreational / Hobbyist UAS pilot reported becoming aware that another UAS pilot may have flown around infrastructure.
text: hello, i apologize and hate to act like the 'drone police' but, a few of us have had a few less than positive experiences with a fellow operator. we've done our best to advise to the best of our abilities and to get through to him. i've decided at this point to leave the educating to the professionals. i just don't want fellow operators ruining what is an evolutionary hobby that is constantly receiving new rules and updates to follow. i feel these operators give all drone operators a negative name when they so blatantly disregard collaboration or help from a more knowledgeable operator.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Conflict NMAC
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they did not vector an aircraft from base leg to final approach in a timely manner and the aircraft flew across the final approach course into confliction with an aircraft landing the parallel runway.
text: i sat down on position. we were xxl only for a tall vessel in the approach area of xxr. within the hour, xxr was available again and traffic began to build. i was in the process of figuring out who already on my frequency could switch over to xxr to alleviate some of the pressure i knew was coming. aircraft x was being vectored for the visual approach runway xxl, straight in from the redacted. aircraft y was being vectored for the instrument landing system runway xxr, right downwind from redacted. aircraft x was about 15 miles from the airport, he was issued traffic on aircraft y, who was turning for the right base. aircraft x reported the traffic in sight and was instructed to maintain visual separation. aircraft y was told that traffic landing runway xxl had him in sight and was maintaining visual separation. while this was unfolding, we were in the process of opening a seond position so it was a stand alone scope. the second position was opened as aircraft y was given the base turn. i was coordinating with the second position the sequence offline and who would be their first aircraft and the general sequence for xxl/r. an aircraft, 25 miles south of the airport on a right base, that we had determined was going be worked by the second position checked in on my frequency. i immediately gave them second position frequency. at that time i realized that i was late turning aircraft y and he would overshoot the xxr final. i gave aircraft y a 070 heading to try and salvage the situation. i informed aircraft x that the aircraft y traffic would be through their approach course and gave them the option to continue or climb. they opted to continue, reiterating that they had the traffic in sight. i then saw that aircraft y must have gotten a tcas-resolution advisory because they started to climb. i never heard them report that they were responding to an resolution advisory. i canceled the approach clearance and issued a 040 heading and climbed aircraft y to 4000. i re-sequenced aircraft y back around and they landed without further incident. i feel that i should have held the aircraft x at 4000 until i completed the vector to have aircraft y join the final. as soon as aircraft x reported the traffic in sight i gave them the visual approach clearance.

anomaly: ATC Issue All Types; Deviation / Discrepancy - Procedural Published Material / Policy; Inflight Event / Encounter CFTT / CFIT
synopsis: A TRACON controller reported they descended an aircraft too early and it flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
text: aircraft x was inbound redacted. wanted the instrument landing system runway xx. i was trying to coordinate with redacted [center] to get control to send him direct to redacted, since it was a turn more into their airspace. redacted [center] was not answering. i told the pilot to expect direct redacted. then i gave them a descent too early. i was distracted trying to get control of them, and i thought they came over at 100. they must have been at 70. i noticed it was too early as they were crossing the boundary between mvas, at too low of an altitude.i should have worked the aircraft into my airspace, and vectored him for the instrument landing system once he was in my airspace, while i was trying to coordinate control to turn him to the iaf.
